#4421. This Chinese EV Maker Wants To Put A Foot Bath In The Back Seat Of Your Car. Really

Browse this and many other websites without banner ads, personalized tracking and video ads.

If you've ever been in the back of a Rolls-Royce, you'll know just how lovely its rear lambswool carpets are. Their shag is so deep, soft, and luxurious that it's a crime to keep your shoes on back there. While enjoying them, you might think they're the pinnacle of rear seat foot comfort. However, Chinese EV maker Deepal wants to one-up even Rolls-Royce, with an extendable backseat foot bath.

According to Australia's Which Car?, Changan sub-brand Deepal recently filed a patent for a foot bath that would extend out from under the front seats, so that passengers can literally wash their feet while on the move. Once extended, rear passengers can place their feet in the water, which is presumably heated, and even massage them on rollers at the bottom of the basin. Hopefully, there's a towel rack or cubby back there, otherwise you're taking wet feet out and soaking the carpets, which sounds like a nightmare for interior mold.

What about sloshing? I can't even drive around with a Wawa coffee cup filled near the top or it'll slosh out of the spout onto my center console. So how is a basin of water not going to toss all of its water onto the floor at the first bump or turn? According to Car Expert, Deepal's patent claims that the basin can actually block the water from sloshing out. It also has guide holes which let sloshing water recirculate into the bottom, keeping the liquid level low.

There's also a disinfection assembly, to keep the water from being gross, and a quick disconnect to dispose of the water from the vehicle body.

Will this technology ever actually make production? Who knows, as automakers often patent wild ideas just to future-proof their ability to make it one day. But foot baths are quite popular in China, so who knows, maybe there's enough demand for this sort of thing. If it never makes production (which seems likely),though, I think some deep carpets and no shoes, Die Hard-style, will do just fine.

#4420. BYD’s newest EV is about as big as a Toyota Camry, but brings a lot more tech for $23K

BYD launched the new Seal 07 in China, where it starts at around $23,000. It’s about the size of a Toyota Camry, but brings a surprising amount of tech and premium features for the money.

After introducing the updated first-generation Seal 07 in March, BYD launched the second-gen model on Thursday.

The second-generation Seal 07, which BYD calls the “new choice for a class-leading luxury experience,” is available in battery electric (EV) and plug-in hybrid (PHEV) powertrains.

BYD offers five variants, including two PHEVs and three EVs, starting at 139,900 yuan (about $21,000) for the plug-in hybrid and 149,900 yuan (around $22,500) for the fully electric version.

The new Seal 07 EV uses a 76.7 kWh second-generation BYD Blade LFP battery, providing a CLTC range of up to 481 miles (775 km).

It comes standard with a single rear-mounted electric motor producing up to 328 hp (245 kW) and 269 lb-ft (365 Nm) of torque, which BYD says enables it to accelerate from 0 to 62 mph (0 to 100 km/h) in 5.5 seconds.

All plug-in hybrid variants use BYD’s latest DM-i system, which features a 1.5L turbocharged engine with 154 hp (115 kW) and a 214 hp (160 kW) front electric motor.

The new Seal 07 PHEV has a smaller 37 kWh battery that provides up to 205 miles (330 km) of pure electric CLTC range. That’s a considerable jump from the 143 miles (230 km) of electric range the previous generation offered.

Thanks to BYD’s latest Blade Battery 2.0 and Flash Charging technology, the vehicle’s battery can recharge from 10% to 70% in just 5 minutes. To go from 10% to 97%, it takes just nine minutes.

Both versions are 5,080 mm long, 1,960 mm wide, and 1,495 mm tall, with a 2,960 mm wheelbase, which is slightly bigger than the Toyota Camry.

Inside, the new Seal 07 adopts BYD’s latest cabin design, including a 15.6″ floating center infotainment screen, a 10.25″ instrument cluster, and two rear passenger entertainment screens.

BYD added several premium extras, including a built-in 6.8L smart refrigerator, zero gravity seats, and driver headrest audio. It also offers the most rear passenger space and the largest frunk (160L) in its class, according to BYD.

The Seal 07 debuts BYD’s Smart Ecosystem 2.0, including “Diva,” a smartwatch that can interact with the vehicle and let drivers manage functions remotely.

Higher-priced models offer BYD’s God’s Eye B intelligent driving system, with a roof-mounted LiDAR available as an option. The setup provides safety and convenience features such as Navigation on Autopilot in the city and on highways, plus full-scenario intelligent parking.

BYD is offering a limited-time “Super trade-in price” promo, starting at 145,900 yuan ($22,000) for the new Seal 07 EV and 135,900 yuan ($20,500) for the PHEV version.

#4417. Tesla wants its sworn Cybercab answers to NHTSA kept entirely secret

Tesla has answered NHTSA’s Special Order demanding it prove, under oath, that the Cybercab meets federal safety standards. The response landed on the October 30 deadline, and Tesla asked the agency to keep all of it confidential.

The only part of the filing the public can read is a 30-page guide for firefighters. Everything about how a car with no steering wheel, pedals, or mirrors was certified as compliant is blacked out.

We reported in September that NHTSA had ordered Tesla to show its work on the Cybercab’s certification. The order came one week after the company started charging for Cybercab rides in Austin on September 3 and put 21 questions to the company, with civil penalties of up to $139 million for an incomplete answer and criminal exposure for a false one.

Tesla first tried to buy time. On September 18, it asked for eight more weeks, until November 20, citing “the voluminous nature of the request” and the work of searching its records and writing “thorough narrative formats in response to each question.” NHTSA gave it 30 days instead. The new deadline was October 30, and Tesla met it.

Three Tesla documents now sit in the AQ26002 docket, and two of them are empty.

The first is Tesla’s response letter, dated October 30 and addressed from 1 Tesla Road in Austin. It is one page long. The only text is: “The entirety of this file is confidential business information.”

The second is a placeholder for Tesla’s answer to Request 8, which asked the company to explain, standard by standard, how it determined the Cybercab complies: which subpart it certified to, and whether it ran physical tests, simulations, or engineering analyses. Per NHTSA’s note, the responsive documents carry a confidentiality request “for the entirety of each document.”

The third is the only substantive document: Tesla’s Cybercab First Responder Interaction Plan, version 1.2, dated September 3. It’s a real document with useful information in it. It’s also something Tesla has had on its website since July, aimed at police and fire crews, not regulators.

So the public gets a tow-truck manual, and the certification argument stays sealed.

The Special Order wasn’t a fishing expedition. It named the rules the Cybercab doesn’t obviously meet, and it seeks to understand how Tesla believes it can get around it.

FMVSS 135 says “the service brakes shall be activated by means of a foot control.” NHTSA has stated in public that a manufacturer of a vehicle with no foot brake can’t certify to it, then asked Tesla how it did. FMVSS 108 requires a turn-signal control that cancels itself when the steering wheel turns. FMVSS 111 requires mirrors. And the agency wanted to know whether Tesla certified the car with temporary driver controls bolted in and then removed them, which would run into the Safety Act’s “make inoperative” prohibition.

It also asked how the Cybercab is legal without a Part 555 exemption, the route Amazon’s Zoox took for its own steering-wheel-less robotaxi in July. Zoox applied, made its case, and got an exemption capped at 2,500 vehicles a year. Tesla self-certified and started charging for rides.

Every one of those answers is now under a confidentiality claim.

The first-responder plan was written for a different audience, but it brushes against several of NHTSA’s questions.

It says the Cybercab is “not typically equipped with a steering wheel or acceleration and brake pedals.” The word “typically” is doing work there. The same document notes that a Cybercab with a steering wheel and pedals “is typically an engineering or test vehicle, and operates at SAE Level 2 autonomy,” and includes instructions for driving one. That’s relevant to Requests 5 through 7, which asked whether the subject vehicles can be driven with temporarily attached controls.

It describes an operational design domain covering “all public roadways, such as freeways, highways, city streets, and rural roads,” at all hours, in light and moderate rain, fog, and snow. That is a far wider envelope than the Austin geofence the cars run in today, and it references an “Arizona Areas of Operation Appendix.” Request 1 asked for the ODD and Request 2 for scaling plans.

And it confirms that first responders can be granted access to on-board touchscreen controls to move the car, after showing a badge to the B-pillar camera (that’s interesting). Request 20 asked whether the touchscreen can move the vehicle and under what restrictions.

Nothing in it touches brakes, mirrors, telltales, or the certification itself.

Confidentiality requests go to NHTSA’s Chief Counsel under Part 512. The agency decides whether Tesla’s claim holds, and it can order a public version released if it doesn’t. NHTSA hasn’t said anything about the request, and it hasn’t found the Cybercab noncompliant with any standard.

This is familiar. In June 2025, Tesla asked NHTSA to hide its answers about the original Robotaxi launch in Austin, a service running on supervised FSD while FSD was under investigation. Those answers never surfaced.

NHTSA’s opening resume for the audit put the affected population at about 1,000 vehicles. The Cybercab is still carrying passengers in Austin while the agency reads a filing nobody else can.

I don't see how the answers can have confidential business secrets. It is about meeting public safety standards, not asking for schematics, technical details or designs. It is about clear public safety requirement and how the vehicle qualify as meeting it.

The so called keyword from Tesla's self certification is "applicable". Tesla may argue that many of those requirements aren't applicable in their test vehicle. But I would like to see the justifications on that.

Tesla’s position in September was that the Cybercab complies with every applicable federal standard, including the one that requires a brake pedal. If that’s true, the argument for it is the most interesting document in the autonomous vehicle industry right now, and Tesla just asked the government to make sure nobody reads it.

We get why a company redacts test data and supplier details. But the legal theory for how a car with no foot brake meets a foot-brake rule doesn’t sound like a trade secret to me. Zoox’s exemption petition is public. Waymo’s safety framework is public. Tesla’s case for why it didn’t need to ask is sealed, cover letter included.

NHTSA now has to decide whether “the entirety of this file” is really confidential business information. If it says no, we’ll finally see how Tesla certified this car. If it says yes, about 1,000 Cybercabs keep driving on a certification the public isn’t allowed to check.

#4416. Tesla's Kickflipping Roadster Looks Like A Great Way To Lose Your Lunch

Browse this and many other websites without banner ads, personalized tracking and video ads.

Car companies have spent the last 140 years figuring out how to perfect ground travel. Tesla decided that winning that war was unimaginative at best. And as we've all seen by now, the carmaker instead took its next-gen Roadster to the sky last month to demonstrate what it might look like to own a flying car one day.

But what would it actually be like to drive (fly?) the thing? This week, Tesla released a video showing a first-person camera view of the Roadster executing its rad kick-flip maneuver and other stunts. It does not look pleasant to experience firsthand.

If you watched the Roadster unveiling last month, this all probably looks familiar. It's the same stunts we saw that day, including the upside-down dive off of the half-pipe and the jump-spin over the Tesla Semi. But seeing it from the car's perspective adds a whole new layer to it, and shows this dizzying experience a person would have from the cockpit.

Watching the cold gas thrusters at work up close during the kickflip gives you a sense of how much goes into ensuring that the car stays upright. The car adjusts the volume of nitrogen that it releases in order to prevent car from over-rotating and transferring from a barrel roll to an out-of-control corkscrew. Just one simple nudge and it lands back on all four wheels.

Then there's the nosedive off of the half-pipe. A bit more correcting to keep the roll and yaw in check—but the Roadster does it without a hiccup.

All of these amazing stunts happened without a driver; Tesla put a dummy in the front seat. Many actual human beings might feel dizzy or even sick from these kinds of tricks.

Tesla hasn't published what kind of g-forces the kickflip generates, but watching the onboard footage also makes me wonder what kind of fighter pilot-style harness and big bolsters are needed to keep the driver in-place versus the road-going version of the car. Heck, you might need to be a fighter pilot to endure these maneuvers.

It's really hard not to appreciate how much engineering went into making the demo happen. Sure, it takes hours to fill up the 600-liter ultra-high-pressure composite-overwrapped pressure vessels with 10,000 PSI of nitrogen for just a few seconds of joy. But man, is it cool to watch from just about any perspective.

And while Tesla can't guarantee that the flying version of its car will reach a single driveway (or be road legal, for that matter), it's still a very cool, very over-engineered party trick unlike anything we'll likely see from a car manufacturer again. If you're going to buy one and put it through its paces, though, I'd recommend having a light lunch.

#4415. 2027 Chevrolet Silverado 1500 Test: Capability, Comfort, and Style

With two new small-block V-8s, a new interior, and a wide-ranging trim lineup, the Silverado covers pickup needs from towing to dune jumps.

In ancient times, trucks were tools for farmers and construction workers. The idea that they should offer amenities like air conditioning or power steering would have been questionable, and the suggestion of heated seats or ambient lighting would have been laughed off the assembly line. We live in a gentler era, though, and the 2027 Chevy Silverado 1500 reflects the mainstream popularity of pickups for both work and play. Chevy’s half-ton lineup gets a major overhaul for the coming model year with reshaped sheetmetal; redesigned interiors featuring carbon fiber, wood, and bright pops of color; and two brand-new small-block V-8s that will delight internal-combustion loyalists.

Chevy has made enough changes to the Silverado for 2027 to call it a new generation, although what generation that is depends on if you’re starting your count from the first introduction of Silverado as its own model (1998) or all the way back to the first use of the name (1975, as a trim on the C/K models). We’re going from the ’90s, which would make this new truck the fifth generation. To earn its generational title, the Silverado wears a new exterior, crisp as a starched shirt, set off by LED lights, burly wheel lip moldings, and a redesigned bumper. Underneath, the chassis will be familiar from the previous year, albeit with some suspension tweaks for more stable towing and a better ride.

See all results for used cars for sale near 54935

The biggest news for truck fans won’t be the body styling or the interior decorating, but what’s under the big, angular hood. Lower trims still start out with an upgraded turbocharged 2.7-liter four-cylinder, now making 350 horsepower and 455 pound-feet of torque. Diesel fans get the returning Duramax turbo 3.0-liter inline-six, still rated at 305 horses and 495 pound-feet, but now with an optional 34-gallon fuel tank for a claimed (and bladder-challenging) 900-mile range.

And then there are the eight-cylinder stars of the show. These new V-8s are not bored-out versions of the outgoing 5.3- and 6.2-liter mills, but instead comprise completely new blocks, heads, intakes, and exhausts. The new engines measure out at 5.7 and 6.6 liters—or 346 and 401 cubic inches, for those speaking older tongues. Those designations were appealing enough to Chevrolet that they stamped them on the back of the aluminum blocks.

Most of our drive was divided between kitted-out High Country and rambunctious ZR2 models, both with the 6.6-liter, and we can report that the big small-block is powerful (481 ponies, 501 pound-feet), sonorous, and unexpectedly smooth, with elegant on-road manners and impressive trail performance. It’s also very quiet at idle, an effect of using newly added port fuel injection at low rpm and adding in direct injection as throttle input increases.

See all results for used cars for sale near 54935

Back at the C/D homestead, we spent time with the 402-hp, 428-lb-ft 5.7-liter V-8 in the lesser off-road-oriented Trail Boss trim. The Trail Boss is the light-beer equivalent of the hoppy ZR2, offering some trail tech without going all-in on off-road. A roughly two-inch suspension lift, 34-inch Goodyear Wrangler Territory MT tires on 18-inch wheels, and optional underbody cameras give the Trail Boss gravel-road cred. On the pavement, the Trail Boss rides with a little more rear-end jiggle than the High Country (with its adaptive dampers) or the ZR2 (with its Multimatic DSSV setup). At the test track, the Boss got to 60 mph in a reasonable 6.4 seconds and covered the quarter-mile in 14.6 seconds at its 94-mph top speed. But its dirt-focused rubber likely hampered its performance elsewhere. Braking from 70 mph took 198 feet and a twirl around the skidpad returned just 0.70 g of grip while fighting some unsurprising understeer.

In the real world, the Trail Boss felt quicker and more planted than its test results suggest, and the 5.7 offers nearly silent running (a mere 66 decibels and 21 sones at 70 mph). It’d better, given its $2690 option price. When combined with other options on our test truck, covering everything from multi-camera arrays to a slick coat of green paint, our mid-price model ended up with an as-tested window sticker of $76,795. That much scratch could get you into a rear-wheel-drive High Country model with the 5.7 or within spitting distance of a Duramax-equipped ZR2. Upgrading either of those trims to the 6.6-liter (not available on the Trail Boss) would require an extra $2505 for the ZR2 and $2800 for the High Country, with the latter also mandating an upgrade to 4WD. These new V-8s are slick but dear.

Even the base 2.7-liter work truck has a starting price of $40,045, but at least the lower trims benefit from some of the same features as the top-shelf models. The Silverado’s interior rework means that every 2027 truck showcases data on a 12.2-inch gauge cluster and a 16.3-inch center screen. ZR2 and High Country trims get an additional 11.5-inch passenger screen. The displays mark the return of Android Auto and Apple Car Play, but the system still includes Google built-in nav and search functions. We found the native navigation prone to directional confusion, so we’re glad GM walked back its plans to ditch phone mirroring.

The new GM UI is crisp and quick, but we had some issues with the touchscreen’s accuracy. Organizationally, the Silverado interior is scattered, with some controls on the left side of the dash, some in menus in the touchscreen, and some on hard buttons above the console. Chevy allows for menu customizations that create shortcuts to regularly used controls, but until a customer sets that up, they should be prepared for a hunt.

Dialing in the least-irritating combination of driver assist functions might take some time, but setting up for a proper truck job like towing will not. And it’ll handle a proper truck job: The new light-duty Chevy now boasts up to 13,700 pounds of max towing capacity (when properly equipped). The Silverado offers helpful setup and safety tech like a trailer brake-gain assistant for setting trailer brake proportions, as well as several split-view camera angles with overlay graphics that promise to make parking easier and prevent a jackknife. Super Cruise–equipped trucks can tow with the system running, although automatic lane changes are not available while towing.

The Silverado lineup includes everything from a regular cab with an extended cargo bed to the feature-heavy crew-cab top trims. The cabin is noticeably nicer than previous models, and the crew cab will comfortably fit a large, er, crew. Pickup trucks have changed a lot in the past century—largely for the better—but with increased comfort and capability come increased prices. No matter how good the Silverado’s two new V-8s are, there’s no way to drive around that truth.

Like many girls, she planned to be a vet-astronaut-artist, and came closest to that last one by attending UCLA art school. She painted images of cars, but did not own one. Elana reluctantly got a driver’s license at age 21 and discovered that she not only loved cars and wanted to drive them, but that other people loved cars and wanted to read about them, which meant somebody had to write about them. #4414. Battlefield Labs is coming back for a short session to test out next week's Battlefield 6 update, and you can expect more tests in the future, too

Battlefield Labs is evolving, as it reopens its doors for its next - unusual - session.

Battlefield Studios is seemingly trying something different with Battlefield 6’s next patch, which everyone assumed would be a standard, mid-season update not intended to change the game significantly.

However, it appears that it may bring more to the game than we realised, enough that the developer sees it as an excuse to bring back the pre-launch Battlefield Labs testing initiative.

The December 9 patch kicks off the final phase of the game’s first season, which is set to take the game through the holidays and into the new year. We’ve known about its content for a while, and it’s definitely the lightest, compared to the two previous phases.

Battlefield Studios announced a host of new changes that will be included in the same patch, which are apparently significant enough to require player testing. The developer is reviving Battlefield Labs to help it do so, but only for three two-hour sessions, split across the game’s three main server regions (EU, NA, APAC).

All tests are scheduled for today, December 2, and they remain under NDA. Battlefield Labs is also sticking with PC as its chosen platform yet again, though you will be able to join through Steam this time, alongside the EA app.

The focus of the test will be on three key areas that the December 9 patch will be touching. First, there’s footstep audio, an issue that was really brought into focus with the launch of Redsec Battle Royale. You can expect to hear enemy footsteps from farther away, and intuitively know the type of surface they’re moving on.

The patch also brings another pass to hit registration and netcode, which BF Studios says should improve responsiveness in close-quarter situations. Finally, there are broader changes to other combat areas that the announcement didn’t elaborate on.

All testing will take place on Eastwood, and Operation Firestorm, rotating between Conquest, and Escalation.

Going forward, Battlefield Studios said to expect Labs to be open to more players, and for the process itself to be smoother. The developer wants to have faster turnaround times, after all, so that the initiative can test smaller changes and be more responsive to player feedback.

Some of the more involved, future sessions will include experiments with map layout changes and various other non-standard compositions of player and vehicle numbers. Of course, you can also expect new maps and modes to be tested in Labs, similar to how the CTE was used in Battlefield 4’s long life.

#4413. Hyundai is recalling nearly 30,000 Kona Electric vehicles due to an airbag software defect

Hyundai issued a recall affecting nearly 30,000 Kona Electric vehicles due to a software error that could cause the airbag to fail to deploy in a crash.

In a letter sent to the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration on November 4, Hyundai said it was recalling certain 2019 to 2023 Kona Electric and 2019 to 2022 Veloster N vehicles.

The recall impacts 37,901 vehicles in total, including 29,058 Kona Electric and 8,843 Veloster N models.

According to documents submitted to the NHTSA, the issue stems from a software error with the airbag control unit (ACU) that can cause the airbag malfunction indicator light (MIL) to come on and the airbag system to deactivate under certain driving conditions.

The data may become corrupted during a system reboot or power interruption while the system is writing to the ACU’s memory. When this happens, the airbag MIL will illuminate to warn drivers.

As of October 22, 2026, Hyundai is aware of 331 alleged incidents related to the issue. However, none have resulted in a crash, fire, or injury.

Owners can take their vehicle to the closest dealer, where it will update the ACU software, free of charge.

Hyundai expects to mail out owner notification letters on January 1, 2027. In the meantime, owners can contact Hyundai’s customer service at 1-855-371-9460 with any questions or concerns. Hyundai’s recall number is 311.

You can also contact the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration Vehicle Safety Hotline at 1-888-327-4236 or visit the NHTSA.gov website for more information. The NHTSA campaign number is 26V728.

#4412. Tesla Is Now Powering One Of Its Biggest Charging Rivals

Browse this and many other websites without banner ads, personalized tracking and video ads.

Superchargers aren't just a Tesla thing anymore. Today EVgo announced that it opened its first location powered by Tesla hardware. The 12-stall charging station in Chicago kicks off an expansion that will include hundreds more Supercharger stalls nationwide, EVgo said.

With the shift to the North American Charging Standard (NACS), Tesla has shifted in some aspects toward a brand-agnostic tech provider. The NACS port was once a Tesla exclusive; now it’s the port of choice when it comes to modern EVs. Similarly, Tesla’s V4 Supercharging cabinets are available for purchase and installation by any commercial client. Tesla's V4 Supercharging cabinets are powerful, offering speeds up to 500 kW.

“Deploying our first EVgo Supercharger marks an important milestone in growing our customer base while supporting the EV industry’s transition to NACS,” said EVgo CEO Badar Khan.

The first EVgo location in Chicago has both CCS and NACS ports, thanks to the Magic Dock connector. The first batch of Tesla-powered EVgo stations will be built at grocery stores and shopping outlet centers owned by real estate company Regency Centers. This developer has had a longstanding partnership with EVgo; it already had plans to implement 400 more charging stalls. It says that Illinois is a great place to start its Supercharger push, since EV registrations have grown 60% over the past two years.

One nice bonus for Tesla drivers: EVgo’s Superchargers come up in Tesla’s in-car navigation system. As long as the “third-party charging” box is checked in the Tesla navigation app, users will be able to navigate to and charge just as easily as they would for a normal Tesla Supercharging station.

EVgo’s expansion spans more than just one developer or a handful of NACS ports. The company says it already is on track to hit 500 NACS-enabled charging stations nationwide (not counting the Supercharging network). Within the next two years, it wants all of its existing stations built after 2023 to have at least one NACS plug.

Tesla isn’t the only DC fast-charging company with hardware capable of charging natively via a NACS port. Once the NACS plug shape was officially certified by SAE, charging cabinet manufacturers quickly integrated it into their designs. However, Tesla’s Supercharging cabinets are known for their reliability. Tesla itself claims that uptime is 99%, and the network is known for being one of the best in the business.

In a recent survey of EV drivers, EVgo came in second place in terms of reliability after Tesla. Implementing more Tesla Supercharging cabinets could continue to elevate EVgo's reputation.

#4410. Honkai: Star Rail 3.8 will run for an extra two weeks while Version 4.0 is in the oven

The next Honkai: Star Rail update is upon us, and there's a mix of good - and unusual news.

HoYoverse just hosted a sizeable Honkai: Star Rail Special Program, revealing more than just the game’s next major update. Version 3.8 was the big highlight, of course, with the new release arriving soon, on December 16-17 depending on your server region.

Alongside showing everything coming with this next update, the developer also announced that 3.8 will go on for eight weeks, rather than the usual six. V3.8 is dubbed "Memories are the Prelude to Dreams", and it brings an end to the Amphoreus journey.

The story in "Memories are the Prelude to Dreams" takes place after the final battle of Amphoreus, where Constance "The Dahlia" appears to deliver a twist: the Trailblazer's memories are scattered, with many parts missing.

This final quest revolves around finding them in order to piece together the mystery, and involves a return to Penacony. This memory-hunting adventure is told from the perspective of Firefly, which will also explain how she entered the dreamscape initially and met the squad.

The new playable character is The Dahlia, whose power is linked to the the Remembrance path, which allows her to fabricate memories. Despite taking her powers from the Remembrance, The Dhalia actually follows the Path of Nihility in-game: she’s a 5-Star character who shines in teams dealing Break DMG.

The Dhalia can unleash a Gloomy Zone that causes Toughness Reduction inflicted by allies to trigger Super Break DMG, even before you break your enemies’ Weaknesses. The Dahlia can also invite one teammate to become her Dance Partner, which allows them (and her) to deal additional Super Break DMG each time they attack an enemy. If you trigger her Ultimate after picking a Dance Partner, she applies Type Weaknesses of both partners to enemies.

While The Dahlia is the only new character appearing in this final Amphoreus update, there'll be reruns aplenty, with an unusual third banner phase to make up for the extra long wait for 4.0. Appropriately for her role in the story, Firefly will make her return alongside The Dahlia in Phase 1, while Fugue and Lingsha will both have banner reruns in Phase 2, which is expected on January 7th. A bonus two-week-long Phase 3 will then begin on January 28th, seeing brief reappearances for popular returning characters Aglaea and Sunday, before things (presumably) go back to normal with the new annual update.

Something else to look forward to in 3.8 is The Chrysos Awoo Championship, which invites players to become chimera trainers and compete in team-based battles. The Remnants of Twilight event kicks off with the new patch, too, featuring its own set of challenges. However, HoYoverse have confirmed that there won't be an extra event during Phase 3 — but hopefully that'll give you some time to wrap up the last of the Amphoreus story content, which is longer than the previous four chapters put together.

#4408. Meta-backed 250 MW solar farm breaks ground in Arkansas

Arkansas is getting another 250 megawatts (MW) of solar power, and Meta has signed up to buy it.

EDP Renewables North America (EDPR NA) broke ground on Cypress Knee Solar in Chicot County, in the southeastern corner of the state, on November 4. The solar farm is expected to be completed by 2028, bringing several hundred construction jobs and an estimated $25 million in county revenue over its lifetime.

Meta’s long-term power purchase agreement helps it work toward its pledge to match 100% of its annual electricity use with renewable energy generation. Don’t confuse that pledge with Meta powering its data centers with renewables around the clock, though – Facebook and Instagram’s parent company is also backing new gas plants to meet its growing power demand.

The companies announced the deal in May. Cypress Knee is their third clean-energy agreement, bringing the total capacity covered by Meta’s deals with EDPR NA to 545 MW.

“As energy demand continues to rise, projects like Cypress Knee Solar help strengthen grid reliability while creating jobs, generating meaningful local revenue, and delivering long-term benefits to the communities that host them,” said EDPR NA CEO Sandhya Ganapathy.

EDPR NA says it has already contributed more than $77,000 during project development, including money to restore the Lakeside High School greenhouse, resources for the Lakeside Robotics team, and funding for the Lake Village food pantry.

#4407. BMW Is Giving New EV Buyers $500 In Free Charging

Browse this and many other websites without banner ads, personalized tracking and video ads.

BMW's latest Neue Klasse EVs push the boundaries of range and charging speed. In short, they're some damn good electric cars. Now there's another reason to buy one: free charging.

BMW on Thursday said it's offering $500 in public charging credits for 2027 electric models. It applies to the i5, i7, and iX3, and is open to drivers who buy or lease. The benefits last for one year from the car's purchase date.

Here's how the $500 breaks down. BMW says $300 of it can be redeemed at more than 15 charging networks, including Ionna, Shell Recharge, ChargePoint, and EVgo. The other $200 only applies to Ionna locations. (BMW is one of the automakers backing Ionna.)

To access the funds, drivers need to set up an account through the BMW app. Once they do that and handle payment through BMW ChargingNetwork, credits are automatically applied to eligible charging purchases.

BMW is also offering buyers of 2027 EVs one free year of Ionna membership, which gets drivers 25% discounts on sessions at the fast-growing charging player.

If $500 in free charging sounds nice and you're considering these vehicles, I have one note of caution after getting behind the wheel of all three.

The i5 is a solid all-around EV. It drives well, looks familiar, and offers over 300 miles of range in some trims. But the i7 and iX3 are miles ahead in terms of onboard technology and specs. The latter models use BMW's Neue Klasse architecture and feature an overhauled digital interface with a wonderful "Panoramic Vision" display below the windshield. The iX3 offers over 400 miles of range and 400 kilowatt charging. Expect similar capabilities to trickle throughout BMW's lineup and into the next iteration of the i5 too.

The EV5 is the fully electric SUV we want, but can’t have in the US. After launching it in China in 2023, Kia introduced the global version last year, which is now on sale in Europe, Canada, the UK, and other markets.

It has already been a big part of Kia’s comeback in China and is expected to become one of its best-selling EVs.

Kia appears to be preparing an updated version. A new EV5 model was recently spotted by ShortsCar in a South Korean parking garage without camouflage, and it’s expected to be the updated version.

You can see in the video that the design has changed quite a bit. Up front, the hood and headlights remain about the same, but new design elements like a black accent light are added.

It also features a unique bumper design, similar to that of the rugged EV5 WKNDR Concept Kia revealed last November at the Guangzhou Motor Show.

The biggest changes are inside, where the interior appears to be completely overhauled. Instead of the current large display screen spanning from the driver to the center, the new EV5 features a display that extends from the center to the passenger side.

#4405. Hyundai Has a Clever Way to Add Power to a Two-Way Tailgate

A little transmission would let one drive motor raise and lower the whole tailgate or swing one section sideways.

Multifunction and split tailgates are definitely a thing now, and there’s probably no going back. Many truckmakers offer some sort of door-within-a-door or built-in-step arrangement that adds utility to what was previously just a hinged wall that kept stuff in the bed. A new Hyundai/Kia concept could take that to the next level by applying power to a two-way tailgate.

A recently published U.S. patent application covering a previously disclosed design builds on previous filings that describe a split tailgate that opens two ways: the conventional way, swinging the whole unit down with hinge action at the bottom, or sideways opening, with a vertical hinge allowing a portion of the tailgate to swing out, providing belly-up-to-the-bed access. That much we've seen before.

See all results for used Hyundai for sale near 10001

The distinguishing feature is that this split tailgate can open and close in either direction, and do so with power from a single drive motor. All two-way tailgates currently offered by Ford, Honda, and Ram require manual operation for side-opening, and only Ford’s offers powered raising and lowering. Not only does the Hyundai/Kia idea remove that unnecessary application of work, but it does so with clever simplicity.

Think of the mechanism as a little transmission that sends one drive motor’s power to either of two outputs. One operates the bottom hinge to raise or lower the entire tailgate. The other operates a spindle that pushes or pulls a lever to swing one section sideways. A second motor operates the clutch mechanism that selects between them. So there are two motors, but only one does the work of moving the tailgate.

Sure, you could figure out a way to package two drive motors into such a tailgate or its surroundings, but that’s unnecessary complexity and likely more weight. The latest patent describes control logic that should avoid any expensive crashes. Before beginning either opening sequence, the controller checks that both tailgate latches are engaged and the vehicle is stopped. It then selects the appropriate drive path, releases the corresponding latch, and powers the gate open.

One notable design difference seen in the application’s drawings is that the vertical hinge lives at the seam between the tailgate’s two sections, not on the truck bed as in Honda’s and Ram’s production implementations, and the side-opening portion latches to the truck’s box. Ford also uses a mid-tailgate vertical hinge, but its panel within a panel is surrounded by more tailgate on either side.

See all results for used Hyundai for sale near 10001

If something like this were to make production, it would most likely turn up on the mid-size body-on-frame pickup Hyundai has promised. We’ve also seen a patent for a hardtop for the related SUV that would allow for one-person roof assembly. There’s nothing that says both innovations couldn’t end up on both of the new off-roaders, but of course there's no guarantee of either.

#4404. Tomorrow’s Battlefield 6 patch is the first step towards improving footstep audio, and it might actually fix the settings reset bug

The next major Battlefield 6 patch is nearly upon us, and Battlefield Studios is promising a bounty of changes - including a couple of fixes to some big bugs.

Battlefield 6 is about to receive a new update. Version 1.1.3.0 is set to arrive tomorrow, December 9 to kick off the third and final phase of the game’s first season. Winter Offensive brings some holiday-themed new content to the game, but it’s not the most interesting part of the patch.

That honour goes to a couple of the high-level changes Battlefield Studios has included with the new patch, which range from a major pass on audio to a fix for a particularly annoying bug that’s been seemingly introduced with a recent patch.

Thew new content takes the form of a limited-time version of the game’s Empire State map, which covers it in snow and tweaks its layout slightly. To go along with that there are new limited-time modes for both multiplayer and Redsec’s Gauntlet. The event mode will be available in Conquest, and Domination.

The Ice Climbing Axe is the only new weapon in this drop. The battle pass gets a new Winter Offensive bonus path, just like we’ve seen with previous seasonal stages. This is how you unlock the axe, too.

Easily the most interesting change in this update is the range of improvements to audio across the board. First, footstep audio received a big pass that should make it easier to hear enemy footsteps, easier to locate them, and across different surfaces.

Some of the bugs that caused certain sounds to simply vanish have been fixed. This was especially prevalent in battle royale matches. BF Studios explained in the patch notes that it has adjusted memory priorities for in-game sounds in order to prioritise the most crucial ones. This is not the end of the road on audio, however, as the developer continues to work on making the soundscape more stable and reliable.

Some of those audio changes are the result of recent testing done in Battlefield Labs, which is also responsible for another exciting addition in this latest patch: improvements to hit registration.

While BF6 has had solid and stable netcode, certain situations would sometimes create uncertainty about how you died, and why certain actions seemingly failed to perform at that particular moment.

The focus in this update is to improve the reliability of how actions in close-quarter combat are translated, which includes firing before fully going into ADS, quick aim changes and more.

Speaking of close-range, the patch also brings another pass to soldier visibility to make it easier for enemies to stand out from the background. This is particularly relevant in areas with low contrast, or busy environments with lots of particle and visual effects.

1.1.3.0 also brings yet another set of weapon handling and gunplay tweaks, this time focusing on accuracy issues with first shots. You can also expect more tweaks to attachment behaviour with regards to recoil.

Something else worth highlighting is that vehicle gameplay is getting several smaller tweaks that have to do with how they interact with the world, how their HUDs behave and more. Finally, your settings should no longer be reset after applying an update. BF Studios says there are still some instances where that might happen, but the issue should be fixed for the majority of players.

You can read the full change log on the Battlefield blog.

#4403. Gas Prices Got You Down? This 261-MPG Volkswagen Solves That—For $140,000

Browse this and many other websites without banner ads, personalized tracking and video ads.

In 2013, VW launched one of the most fascinating experiments in fuel efficiency ever made. The Volkswagen XL1 took 12 years to develop and ended up costing a whopping $150,000 at the time. However, as an engineering exercise, it was brilliant. And since VW only made 250, it's even rarer than a Bugatti Veyron from the same era.

If you're looking for an extreme answer to high gas prices, today's your lucky day. There's currently an XL1 in the Netherlands up for auction on Catawiki. The 2016 model up for grabs has just over 1,000 miles on the odometer and is apparently in excellent condition inside and out.

The XL1 project was spearheaded by Ferdinand Piech, VW's top boss at the time. Not known to ever give up on his lofty, ambitious goals, Piech fought for 12 years, and through several iterations, to finally achieve his "one liter" car, something that could burn just one liter of fuel per every 100 km. VW pulled out all the stops to make it extraordinarily efficient; the result was something closer to a supercar than a Toyota Prius.

That teardrop-shaped body is made from carbon fiber, as is its chassis, saving weight. It debuted a full year before BMW's i3, an EV/PHEV which only had a carbon chassis but a plastic body. The car has butterfly doors and two seats that are offset to optimize the car's aerodynamic shape.

Power comes from an 800cc, two-cylinder, turbo-diesel engine behind the driver—this makes it mid-engine, like a supercar—plus a plug-in hybrid system centered around a 5.5 kilowatt-hour battery. The plug-in hybrid powertrain wasn't originally planned, and didn't come about until near the end of its development, so it needed a massive 50-pound removable charging box in the trunk so you could plug it in.

With a funky hybrid powertrain, a curb weight of just 1,852 pounds, and a drag coefficient of just 0.189, the XL1 was capable of an EU-tested 0.9 liters per 100 km, which equates to 261 mpg. It can also travel 31 miles on battery power alone, registering an insane efficiency of 6.2 miles per kWh, about double today's more conventional EVs. VW said at the time of the XL1's launch that it only needed about 8 horsepower to sustain a steady 62 mph.

The main downside is performance: It only makes 68 horsepower, so it takes almost 13 seconds to get to 60 mph.

This specific car up for auction is expected to fetch around $140,000, according to the auction house. So even with its incredible fuel economy and currently outrageous fuel prices, the XL1's financial breakeven point is still a long ways away. Plus, it runs on diesel, which has seen even steeper price spikes than regular gas. A used EV cuts you off from the gas station entirely, and is a better all-around choice of course.

But for someone who wants an amazing piece of automotive history, the XL1 could be worth the price. Plus, it'll sip on fuel like no other for many of your daily errands—and look cool doing it.

#4402. Ford’s electric pickup is suddenly selling like hotcakes at 50% off used

Once America’s most popular electric pickup, the Ford F-150 Lightning is finding a second life on the used market.

The F-150 Lightning is hard to pass up at 50% to 60% off sticker price, even used. With new models no longer available, Ford’s electric pickup is suddenly selling like hotcakes on the used market.

After the last model rolled off the assembly line last December, CEO Jim Farley said the decision to end production came as the “very high-end EVs, the $50K, 70K, $80,000 vehicles, they just weren’t selling.”

At 50% to 60% off, it now looks like a bargain in the used market. “When Ford was selling it brand new, the math was complicated,” Jimmy Douglas, CEO of Plug, a wholesale EV dealer, recently told Bloomberg.

On the used market, however, “the Lightning is 50% to 60% of the sticker price and that is really a sweet spot,” he added.

Used Ford F-150 Lightnings are selling in about 20 days, less than half the 44-day average for used vehicles in the US. According to Edmunds.com, prices are now up 4% to about $50,000 since the start of the year.

Douglass said that close to one-third of used models are sold by rival dealerships that would normally flip them back to Ford. However, many are opting to sell them directly because of demand.

Chase Norris from Colorado called the electric pickup a bargain. He purchased a used Lightning for around $40,000 and considers it a major upgrade from his previous gas F-150.

EV Group CEO and cofounder Alex Lawrence, which sells pre-owned electric vehicles, said he can’t get his hands on any reasonably priced used F-150 Lightnings currently.

He said many Lightning buyers use it as a second truck to save money during their weekly commute.

It looks essentially the same as the gas-powered F-150, offers instant torque, and produces zero tailpipe emissions, but the electric pickup failed to meet Ford’s expectations because of its higher price.

The base F-150 Lightning Pro debuted in 2021 with a starting MSRP of $39,974, but that was quickly raised to around $60,000 a year or so later.

According to Edmunds.com, the average transaction price for the F-150 Lightning in its first year of sales was $79,000 because Ford focused on higher-priced trims. The gas version’s ATP was about $19,000 less.

Even with the higher sticker price, Ford was losing a considerable amount on each Lightning it produced. In Q1 2024, Ford lost more than $100,000 on every EV it built.

Next year, Ford will take another crack at the electric pickup market with the Fathom, the first vehicle based on its “groundbreaking” new Universal Electric Vehicle (UEV) platform.

Ford said the Fathom will start at $28,350 for the standard-range version. Even with the $1,595 delivery fee included, the electric pickup will start at under $30,000.

As the first vehicle built on its UEV platform, Ford promises the Fathom will be a step-change from its first-generation EVs.

According to Ford, the electric pickup will offer more interior space than a Toyota RAV4 and will be the first vehicle with Apple Maps directly integrated into the navigation system.

We also know the electric pickup will have a NACS port after a few prototypes were spotted charging at a Tesla Supercharger this summer.

Ford reportedly aims to sell around 100,000 Fathoms in its first year. CEO Jim Farley said on the company’s third-quarter earnings call last week that the launch remains on track for Q4 2027.

Farley called the Fathom a “breakthrough product” and said that the MSRP under $30,000 is perfect for today’s market.

At least some F-150 owners are already trading in for lower-priced options. A member of the Ford F-150 Lightning Owners Group, JF, said that although it was a great ride, “Carvana gave us just a little less than we paid new,” adding, “R2, here we come!”

When Torque News reached out, JF said he “really liked the Lightning,” but wanted something smaller. “With the current increase in resale value, the time to trade seemed right,” JF added.

The Rivian R2 (see our review) Performance with the Launch Package is now available to order starting at $57,990 with an EPA-estimated range of up to 330 miles and 656 hp. The R2 Premium will go on sale later this year, starting at $53,990

In Spring 2027, Rivian will launch the R2 Standard, starting at $44,990 with an estimated range of up to 275 miles and 350 hp.

So were they losing $100k / truck, or the average loss when all development was included ended up being $100k? Big difference. I don't believe the cost to build each one was $170k+. That makes no sense. They just priced them too high to amortize the development costs over enough vehicles to make them profitable. Every vehicle has to sell a minimum # before they start to make a profit.

Surging F-150 Lightning sales on the used market show buyers want electric pickups. But at the right price.

At $60,000 to $70,000, the Lightning wasn’t so attractive, but at $40,000 used, it suddenly is. Perhaps Ford is on to something with its next-gen EV pickup, the Fathom, set to go on sale starting at under $30,000.

Will it deliver on its promise? Ford has yet to reveal battery specs, towing capacity, range, or any other specs. We should learn more soon.

#4401. E-quipment highlight: Jungheinrich launches new forklift for Asian markets

Like many equipment brands, German forklift maker Jungheinrich has been struggling to crack the Asian industrial markets – but the company is set to change all that with the launch of a new line of 1.6- to 3-ton class electric forklifts designed specifically to navigate the region’s tight warehouses and factories.

Jungheinrich launched the next generation of its EFG MB and MC electric counterbalance forklifts, giving businesses more flexibility to match truck performance with the battery options, charging systems, and operator features that meet their specific needs.

“Different operations have different requirements,” said Lisa Jing Xue, Managing Director at Jungheinrich’s Qingpu Plant, China. “With the EFG M series, customers can configure the (forklift) truck around their application, workload and operators – whether they need greater maneuverability for confined warehouse spaces, or a stable, powerful truck for demanding transport and stacking work.”

Forklift buyers can choose between two performance packages, prioritizing energy efficiency for everyday material handling or more driving and lifting muscle for more demanding, high-throughput operations. The higher-performance package comes standard on models rated for 2.5-3.0 tons, with a choice of either lead-acid or lithium-ion batteries with 346 or 690 Ah of capacity available to suit different workloads and shift patterns. Both ship with regenerative braking tech that can recover up to 30% of the energy used in stopping and lowering loads, too, helping to keep these machines running longer between charging sessions.

“We carried out extensive customer research to understand what the market needs,” added Jing Xue. “Customers can invest in the performance required today and add further capabilities as their application demands.”

Optional features include fingertip controls, a larger 4″ digital display, upgraded LED lighting, and operator-assistance (ADAS) systems, while flexible seating and cabin configurations are designed to keep drivers comfortable through long shifts. A slim B-pillar and glass roof help visibility in busy warehouses, while the four-wheel EFG MC gets automatic cornering speed reduction as standard. Integrated telematics are also standard, giving fleet managers access to utilization data, maintenance planning and pre-operational checks from day one.

Jungheinrich says the order books for both the three- and four-wheel electric forklifts are open now, ready to be supported by the company’s 6,000+ person strong service network across the Asia-Pacific region.

#4400. Acura Kicks Off Sales of More Than 3000 Official Reproduction Parts for the 1st-Gen NSX

Acura’s NSX heritage parts program moves from announcement to U.S. sales, giving owners fresh support for their aging supercars.

Buying or owning an older supercar is one thing. Keeping it on the road is another issue, and that's only complicated further when it comes to finding replacement parts. Acura is now making that aspect of ownership about as easy as it could possibly be for first-gen NSX owners: this week, the brand is officially kicking off sales of more than 3000 reproduction parts through its Honda Heritage Parts program.

The new welcome development for NSX owners comes through Acura dealerships nationwide and through Honda's DreamShop. The reality here is that, although great cars like the NSX have exceptional enthusiast support, factory-backed parts re-creation is hard to match. It's one thing to hope you'll find a part across used listings and another to know it's available at a local dealer.

If all this sounds familiar, it's for good reason. As Road & Track reported in March, the company has been intending to bring reproduction parts to American dealers for a minute now. This latest development moves the story along to actual sales. That said, there are two very clear sides to this business: “Genuine Honda Reproduction Parts” use the same materials and production methods as the original components; “Honda Compatible Parts” are redeveloped replacements for original pieces that the company no longer sells.

See all results for used Honda for sale near 77521

That differentiation allows the brand to build what it feels makes sense and lean on suppliers elsewhere. Originally, Acura said it would cover the powertrain, interior, exterior, electrical, and chassis components. That's a wide swath to be sure—but for now, owners will still need to check availability to be sure that the individual piece they need is available.

That said, all of this signals just how key the NSX is to Acura and Honda. Supporting a supercar decades after production helps owners keep and maintain the car in question. In addition, it gives prospective buyers a touch more confidence about picking one up. In other words, it could boost the second-hand market and the overarching value of the nameplate itself. That won't make an NSX (or any other supercar) cheap or easy to maintain, but it eases some of the frustration.

#4398. Battlefield 6's latest update dubbed the game's simultaneously best and worst patch as it runs into all kinds of issues

What's likely going to be the last major Battlefield 6 update of the year has launched with a number of unexpected issues.

There’s been a lot of anticipation for Battlefield 6’s version 1.1.3.0 patch. The patch kicks off the third and final phase of the game’s first season, adding some new holiday-themed content. More the new content itself, the update’s biggest additions are almost entirely gameplay-related.

Unfortunately, for as much as the changes in 1.1.3.0 have been well received, the launch has been marred by a series of technical issues, some of which are a little unusual.

Immediately after patch 1.1.3.0 went live, players on PC started reporting massive stutters that would occur every few seconds. The issue is especially pronounced in Redsec Battle Royale, but much deadlier in traditional multiplayer.

Battlefield Studios quickly acknowledged it, pointing out a workaround that appears to be working for players on Steam. According to those players, going offline on Steam’s friends menu has fixed stuttering for them.

The issue remains for other players on PC, however, and the developer said it’s working on a proper fix.

Perhaps the most disrupting problem the patch has caused is one that prevents players from being able to interact with the game’s menu. Tiles become unresponsive, or outright unselectable when you try to hover near them.

Ironically, the top set of tiles designed to make it easy for players to quickly jump into the new content has been the most affected. Restarting the game sometimes fixes the issue, and some players report that it only happens upon first launch after installing the update.

But Battlefield Studios later clarified that, unsurprisingly, there’s an actual reason behind the bug. Once again, a fix is being investigated, and the developer will offer an update once some progress has been made.

A little further down the list of importance is an issue that stops players from being able to skip tiers within the new Winter Offensive bonus path in the game’s battle pass. BF Studios took out the feature entirely while it works on a fix, so while you can continue making progress in the bonus path, you won’t be able to skip tiers.

This is all a shame to see. Outside of all the problems, the meat of the new update has been almost universally praised. The visibility improvements, and netcode updates have been celebrated. Many players were also happy to see meaningful updates to footstep audio and overall clarity.

It’s also unusual for a Battlefield 6 patch to run into so many issues at launch. The sentiment around 1.1.3.0 so far is that it’s the game’s best and worst update yet. Hopefully those issues will be fixed before the development team breaks for the holidays.

#4397. A computer scientist breaks through a limit that stood since 1996

Finding the shortest route between two locations is something navigation apps like Google Maps do every day. Behind the scenes, sophisticated algorithms analyze networks of roads and intersections to identify efficient paths. But what if a computer needed to calculate the shortest distance between every possible pair of locations in an enormous network?

That challenge extends far beyond maps. Similar calculations are important for transportation systems, communication networks, and even biological structures involving proteins, neurons, or other interconnected components. As these networks grow, determining the shortest routes between all their points becomes increasingly difficult.

Computer scientists call this the All-Pairs Shortest Paths (APSP) problem. It involves finding the shortest distance between every pair of points in a graph. In this context, a 'graph' is simply a collection of points (called vertices) joined by connections (called edges). Those points might represent cities, PCs, subway stations, or organs, while the connections could stand for highways, cables, railway lines, or blood vessels.

Why Calculating Shortest Paths Is So Difficult

Determining the exact shortest distances across a massive network can consume enormous amounts of computing time and memory. In densely connected networks, some conventional approaches require what mathematicians call cubic time. That means doubling the number of points can increase the computational workload by roughly eight times.

Because the required computation (work) can grow much faster than the network itself, researchers have spent decades searching for more efficient methods. One promising solution is to use approximation algorithms, which calculate estimates rather than exact answers. The goal is to produce distances that are sufficiently accurate while dramatically reducing the amount of computation required.

An important advance came in 1996, when researchers Dor, Halperin, and Zwick (DHZ) developed a method capable of producing distance estimates within twice the actual shortest distance for sufficiently distant points, while operating in nearly optimal time.

This level of accuracy is known as a "2‑approximation." For example, if the shortest possible route between two locations is 10 kilometers, an estimate satisfying this guarantee would fall between 10 and 20 kilometers.

Rather than examining every possible route, the DHZ approach uses a relatively small selection of points from the network (referred to as sampled vertices). These strategically selected points serve as shortcuts that help the algorithm estimate distances more efficiently.

The approach works particularly well when the points being compared are far apart.

Consider a journey between Delhi and Chennai. Because the cities are separated by a considerable distance, the algorithm can often find a sampled point close to the shortest route. This allows it to calculate an estimate that remains within the promised limit of twice the actual distance.

However, the same strategy becomes less dependable when the two points are close together.

Imagine calculating the shortest route between two neighborhoods in the Mumbai suburbs. The sampled points might be located too far from the most direct connection, forcing the algorithm to estimate a much longer route.

For example, two points might be connected by a path containing just two edges, yet the sampled route could contain five. Because five exceeds twice the true distance of two, the result violates the "at most twice" accuracy guarantee.

This weakness meant that the original algorithm's mathematical guarantee applied only when the points were sufficiently far apart. For closer connections, the same level of accuracy could not always be assured.

That limitation remained a challenge for nearly three decades.

A New Algorithm Breaks Through a Decades-Old Limit

Now, Dr. Manoj Gupta, an Associate Professor at the Indian Institute of Technology Gandhinagar, has introduced a refinement that extends the accuracy guarantee to points much closer together than earlier methods allowed.

Gupta presented his research at the 66th Annual Symposium on Foundations of Computer Science (FOCS 2025) in a paper titled "Improved 2-Approximate Shortest Paths for close vertex pairs."

The achievement is particularly significant because the improved algorithm preserves the overall runtime of the earlier approach while expanding the range of distances for which reliable estimates can be guaranteed.

The breakthrough comes from rethinking how points are sampled within the network.

Traditional methods depended on a collection of representative points to estimate distances. Gupta's approach instead introduces a multi-scale sampling strategy that organizes information about the network at several different levels.

By analyzing connections at multiple scales rather than relying on a single sampling layer, the algorithm can account for shorter routes that previous approaches might overlook.

This more sophisticated sampling technique reduces the minimum distance required for the 2-approximation guarantee to hold, without increasing the algorithm's overall computational complexity.

Returning to the transportation example, the original DHZ method could efficiently estimate sufficiently long journeys, such as the route between Delhi and Chennai. The improved approach extends that dependable accuracy to much shorter connections (such as Mumbai's suburbs).

The central achievement is not simply a new way to estimate distances. It is the ability to provide the same mathematical accuracy guarantee across a wider range of distances while maintaining computational efficiency.

Why This Computer Science Breakthrough Matters

Massive networks are fundamental to modern technology. Internet infrastructure, transportation systems, social media platforms, and artificial intelligence applications all depend on analyzing complicated webs of interconnected information.

In many situations, obtaining a perfectly exact distance is less important than producing a dependable estimate quickly. When networks contain enormous numbers of connections, the ability to balance accuracy and speed becomes especially valuable.

Gupta's research strengthens the mathematical foundations of algorithms designed to handle these challenges. Although the findings are theoretical and do not establish immediate improvements to specific commercial systems, they offer a better way to approach distance calculations in large networks.

The work also provides insight into how the overall structure of a network can be understood through carefully selected local connections. By improving how these relationships are sampled and analyzed, researchers can move closer to efficiently estimating distances between every pair of points in a massive system.

Progress in theoretical computer science often comes through incremental refinements rather than dramatic changes. Improving an influential result that dates back to 1996 therefore represents a meaningful advance.

By extending a longstanding accuracy guarantee without increasing overall runtime, the new algorithm pushes beyond an important mathematical boundary and strengthens the techniques underlying some of today's most complex connected systems.

Mitsubishi’s new Pajero SUV looks like a legitimate competitor to the Toyota 4Runner and Land Cruiser, now that we have the full specs on this new off-road-oriented SUV. It’s set to go on sale in Japan next month, and while Mitsubishi says it still hasn’t reached a decision about U.S. availability, its dimensions and pricing put it in line with Toyota’s popular mid-size SUVs.

The Pajero measures 193.7 inches long, 75.8 inches wide, and 75.2 inches tall. Those measurements are all within a few inches of the 4Runner, though the Mitsu is narrower overall. It has three rows of seats and seating for seven, and it’s built on a ladder frame and has standard four-wheel drive.

Though Japan-market pricing isn’t an indicator of what this model could cost if it comes to the States, we do know that the Pajero starts at the equivalent of $39,000 and goes up to $50,000 for the loaded Super Exceed trim level pictured here. #4395. The Great Barrier Reef's most notorious coral killer may actually be helping it

Crown-of-thorns starfish (COTS) are among the most feared creatures on coral reefs. Covered in sharp, toxin-filled spines, these predators are notorious for consuming coral and leaving widespread destruction in their wake.

However, new research from the University of Sydney suggests these infamous reef destroyers may also have a surprisingly beneficial side. When their populations remain under control, crown-of-thorns starfish can help maintain healthy coral communities and support greater biodiversity.

Native to Australia's Great Barrier Reef, these coral-eating starfish have caused enormous damage during population explosions. Since the 1960s, the reef has experienced four major outbreaks, occurring roughly every 15 years. Declining numbers of natural predators, including tritons and several species of reef fish, have made the Great Barrier Reef and other marine ecosystems more vulnerable to these destructive events.

Scientists Discover That Coral Often Survives Starfish Attacks

In a study published in Ecology and Evolution, researchers investigated what happens to coral after crown-of-thorns starfish feed on it. The team examined feeding scars and remaining living tissue at the University of Sydney's One Tree Island Research Station, located on the Great Barrier Reef.

The study sites were within protected areas where healthy fish populations help keep starfish numbers under control. Unlike other parts of the reef that experience devastating outbreaks, these locations maintain relatively low populations of crown-of-thorns starfish.

The results revealed an unexpected pattern. A team led by Dr. Shawna Foo found that living coral tissue survived nearly 75 percent of the observed feeding events.

"At One Tree Reef, COTS appear to consume a relatively consistent amount of coral during each meal and move on, rather than demolishing the entire coral colony," said Dr. Foo, a University of Sydney Horizon Fellow in the School of Life and Environmental Sciences. "This meant live coral tissue remnants were frequently left behind."

How Coral-Eating Starfish Can Boost Reef Biodiversity

The discovery suggests that small populations of crown-of-thorns starfish may play an important role in maintaining the balance of coral reef ecosystems.

Some coral species grow quickly and can take over large areas, limiting the space available to slower-growing varieties. By feeding on these dominant species, crown-of-thorns starfish may create opportunities for other corals to survive and establish themselves.

The researchers found that surviving fragments of fast-growing Acroporidae corals did not regenerate over the areas damaged by starfish feeding. In contrast, regrowth occurred primarily among slower-growing Montipora and Porites corals.

"By feeding on fast-growing corals such as Acropora, low-density COTS populations create space for slower-growing coral species to persist, helping to increase coral diversity," Dr. Foo said.

This finding challenges the idea that all coral consumption by crown-of-thorns starfish is harmful. Under the right conditions, their feeding behavior may actually prevent a few dominant coral species from taking over the reef.

Why Eliminating Crown-of-Thorns Starfish Could Be a Mistake

Despite these potential benefits, researchers caution that large outbreaks of crown-of-thorns starfish remain a serious threat. When their numbers increase dramatically, they can destroy extensive areas of coral, leaving reefs struggling to recover.

The key difference is whether starfish populations remain at naturally manageable levels or grow into destructive outbreaks.

"It's important to distinguish between COTS populations performing their natural role as coral predators and outbreaks causing sustained reef decline."

Although the research was conducted mainly in protected areas with healthy fish populations and little risk of major outbreaks, the findings could help scientists and conservation managers improve strategies for controlling crown-of-thorns starfish.

In particular, the results suggest that removing every starfish may not be the best approach once an outbreak has been brought under control.

"The implications of our work can help us decide when and why culling should occur and the ecological endpoint of a cull. Once an outbreak is suppressed, the goal should not necessarily be to eliminate COTS entirely. Culling needs to be complemented by strong marine management to protect COTS predators and keep COTS populations in check."

Research co-author Professor Maria Byrne connected the findings to a well-established ecological concept.

"The results are consistent with the intermediate disturbance hypothesis, an important framework in ecology and conservation."

According to this hypothesis, ecosystems can benefit from occasional, moderate disturbances that prevent any single species from becoming too dominant.

The research suggests that crown-of-thorns starfish may be an example of this natural balancing process. While uncontrolled outbreaks can devastate coral reefs, smaller populations may help maintain the diversity that makes these ecosystems so valuable.

The time has arrived for another Arc Raiders update, and Embark has certainly delivered. Today’s patch, version 1.6.0, is among the smallest the game has received so far, focusing almost exclusively on disabling map exploits.

Perhaps more important than the patch itself, however, is the announcement the developer made around it.

Starting off with patch 1.6.0, it takes out a particular zipline on Stella Montis, the game’s most recent addition ot the map roster. Some players used said zipline to get out of bounds, something the game has been battling on several of its maps.

On Blue Gate, the patch fixes a collision issue that allowed players to vault through a wall, and fall to their death. The map fixes continue with another on Spaceport Launch Tower, which takes out a gap in collision that players have been able to shoot through.

The last change in this update affects gameplay feel around Arc enemies. Certain materials in the game’s world weren’t blocking their vision - or fire - when they should have, and this has now been fixed.

Alongside today’s patch, Embark also announced that going forward, we’re going to see fewer patches for Arc Raiders. The game has been getting updates almost every Thursday since it launched in late October.

Now that most of the major problems have been fixed, the studio is shifting to a slower patching cadence. Critical fixes will still be issued as soon as they’re developed, but don’t expect a patch each week going forward.

Embark also revealed that patch releases and in-game store rotations will now occur on Tuesdays. You should also expect the next few weeks to be quiet, as members of the team go on holiday breaks.

But, before everyone goes away, the game is going to get one more big update. The last item on Arc Raiders’ roadmap, revealed in early November, is the Cold Snap event. This is on track for Tuesday, bringing some new content alongside a few other fixes.

#4393. Hyundai Recalls 38K Vehicles Over Faulty Airbags and Seatbelts

The recall covers certain Veloster N and Kona Electric models and stems from a software error.

Hyundai issued a recall over a concerning safety issue that could affect as many as 37,901 vehicles, documents filed with the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) show. According to the recall paperwork, the recall covers some 2019–2022 Veloster N and 2019–2023 Kona Electric vehicles, whose airbags and seatbelt pretensioners may not deploy in a crash.

The recall population is split between 8843 Velosters and 29,058 Konas. According to the recall documents, the issue with the airbags and seatbelt pretensioners originates from a software error. Each of the affected cars comes equipped with an Airbag Control Unit, or ACU, that detects crash signals and instructs the airbags and seatbelt pretensioners to deploy. The NHTSA documents show that the ACU’s software may be corrupted when the system reboots while the ACU is writing data to its internal memory. At a minimum, there is a warning to notify drivers of the issue. If the ACU’s data is corrupted, the airbag malfunction indicator light will illuminate on the dashboard.

See all results for used 2022 Hyundai Veloster N for sale near 19355

The recall comes after more than a year of testing and attempts to recreate the issue by both Hyundai and the ACU’s supplier, following an increase in airbag warranty light claims that was identified in August 2024. As of October 2026, Hyundai was aware of 331 reported incidents alleging the recall complaint, though, thankfully, the company was not aware of any crashes, fires, or injuries.

Owners of affected vehicles will be instructed to bring their car to a Hyundai dealer, where technicians will update the ACU software. The update will be performed for free, and Hyundai will reimburse owners for out-of-pocket expenses incurred to get the fix before the recall was filed. Letters notifying both Hyundai dealers and affected owners of the recall will be mailed on January 1, 2027.
