#4330. After 15 years, The Sims' best spin-off finally gets its due follow-up in The Sims 4: Royalty & Legacy

The Sims Medieval had a short but powerful run back in 2011, and now many of its best features are finally coming to the main franchise.

The Sims 4 developers recently promised an exciting year for the game, and the franchise as a whole, and we just got an early look at one of those first events. After some light teasing, the developer unveiled Royalty & Legacy, the game’s next expansion.

Royalty & Legacy’s first trailer debuted on Thursday, revealing a February 12 release date, and showing off the expansion for the first time.

There’s a lot going on in Royalty & Legacy, which is priced $40. For one, it introduces a new world, Ondarion, which is going to be the setting for your kingdom, as you join a race for the throne. The expansion introduces Dynasty and Nobility - two new systems you can use to create your own world of royal shenanigans.

Ondarion is made up of three neighborhoods (regions). Each region has a unique theme and culture, and they’re each ruled by a Dynasty. Dambele is a place that prioritises art and community. Verdemar is a chaotic world of outlaws and nobles. Finally, Bellacorde is an extravagant region known for opulence and romance.

Speaking of building places, Royalty & Legacy also adds a new Lot type, The Backroom Lot. It serves two functions that change with the time of day. For instance, it can be a library or gym in the morning, and shift into a night club at night. Dambele has its own library-turned-rave, for instance.

At the heart of Ondarion are all the possible fantasy lives and stories you can live. The Sims calls them Powershifts, and they include some well-known Arthurian fantasies and other, more silly ones.

Swordsmanship is the new 10-level skill arriving with the expansion, which further plays into those fantasies by letting your Sims duel. There are even Swordsmanship Tournaments you can watch take place across every neighborhood in Ondarion.

Then there are Secret Passageways, which let you speed up moving across the new regions. They essentially let your Sims teleport between designated passageways, either on their own lots, or other lots in the world. Some of these are hidden for you to find, while others you can create.

In terms of new careers, there’s the Noble Career, where your Sim can rise through several Noble Rankings by doing basically what nobles had to do in the middle ages to earn favour.

The aforementioned Dynasty System is how you can join any of Ondarion’s existing families, or start your own. You actually have a lot of say in what goes on, including the usual business of appointing heirs.

Of course, no royal roleplay would be complete without scandals, which is where the Scandals System comes in. Through it, you can create stories to discredit others, or even topple an entire dynasty.

In November, you may recall The Sims 4 introducing new free items inspired by West African culture. In creating that content, EA worked with a group of Simmers who have direct ties to West African countries.

The group’s guidance was once again utilised to build the Dambele neighborhood in this expansion, and some of the lots around the world of Ondarion were even created by members of the group.

While you wait for Royalty & Legacy to actually arrive, there’s more in The Sims 4 you can jump in right now. The game recently kicked off a collaboration with fashion brand Coach that brought several free items to Create a Sim, and Build Buy. That arrived alongside a free update, which already makes for a busy start of the year for The Sims 4.

#4329. A surprising discovery could help aging muscles repair themselves

Muscles can begin losing their strength and ability to recover surprisingly early in the aging process. Over time, muscle tissue may develop scar tissue, accumulate fat, and lose some of the specialized fibers responsible for rapid, powerful movements. These changes can make everyday activities more difficult and gradually reduce mobility and physical independence.

Now, scientists in Japan have identified a promising molecule that could help protect the body's natural muscle repair system and potentially make it more effective. In laboratory experiments, the compound strengthened an important biological signal involved in muscle regeneration, increasing its ability to connect with a key cellular receptor by more than twofold.

The discovery comes from a team led by Professor Ryuichi Tatsumi at Kyushu University's Faculty of Agriculture. Their findings, published in Scientific Reports, suggest a possible new approach to addressing the cellular changes that make aging muscles increasingly difficult to repair.

How Aging Disrupts the Body's Muscle Repair System

Skeletal muscles are the muscles attached to bones that allow us to walk, lift objects, maintain posture, and perform other voluntary movements. Although these muscles experience wear and tear throughout life, they also have a remarkable ability to repair themselves.

Much of that repair depends on specialized stem cells known as satellite cells. These cells normally remain inactive, positioned alongside muscle fibers until they receive a signal that repair or regeneration is needed. Once activated, they can multiply and develop into muscle cells that help restore damaged tissue.

An essential part of this process involves a protein called hepatocyte growth factor, or HGF. Despite its name, HGF plays important roles beyond the liver, including helping activate the stem cells responsible for muscle regeneration.

Under normal conditions, HGF is stored within the supportive material surrounding muscle fibers. When muscles experience an injury or mechanical stimulation, such as physical movement or stretching, the protein can be released.

HGF then attaches to a receptor called c-met on the surface of satellite cells. Receptors are specialized proteins that receive molecular signals and trigger responses inside cells. In this case, the interaction helps awaken dormant satellite cells, allowing them to multiply, mature, and participate in repairing muscle fibers.

But this carefully coordinated system becomes less reliable with age.

A Hidden Chemical Change May Weaken Aging Muscles

The researchers' previous work revealed that HGF can undergo a chemical modification known as nitration. This process attaches a chemical group called a nitro group to particular locations on a protein, potentially changing its structure and interfering with its normal activity.

For HGF, the researchers identified two especially important locations, Y198 and Y250. Both lie within the region involved in attaching to the c-met receptor.

When these sites undergo nitration, HGF becomes less capable of connecting with its receptor. The result is similar to a key that has become damaged and can no longer operate its intended lock.

This disruption could have important consequences for aging muscles. Even if the body continues producing HGF, chemical changes may prevent the protein from properly activating the stem cells needed for tissue repair. The researchers believe this mechanism may contribute to age-related muscle wasting and declining regenerative capacity.

"HGF is not necessarily missing as we age," explains Tatsumi. "Rather, it can be chemically altered after it is made. That led us to wonder whether a compound with strong antioxidant capacity might protect HGF, either by preventing nitration or by compensating for the functional loss it causes."

Scientists Test Two Powerful Sulfur Compounds

To investigate that possibility, the team studied two compounds with strong antioxidant properties: glutathione trisulfide (GSSSG) and lipoic acid trisulfide (LASSS).

Antioxidants can help limit certain types of chemical damage caused by reactive molecules. Such damage can interfere with proteins and other essential components of cells, particularly when the body's normal protective systems become less effective.

The two compounds belong to a chemical family called trisulfides. Their defining feature is a chain of three sulfur atoms connected to one another. This arrangement gives them unusual chemical properties, including an ability to participate in reactions involving the transfer of electrons, known as redox reactions.

Because these reactions play important roles in cellular chemistry, trisulfides have attracted growing interest as potential ingredients in new medicines.

In the first set of experiments, both compounds reduced nitration at the two vulnerable sites on HGF. However, preventing this chemical modification did not completely restore the protein's ability to attach to c-met.

The scientists therefore increased the amount of trisulfide used relative to HGF. They changed the molar ratio, which compares the number of molecules of each substance, from 1:4000 to 1:8000.

That adjustment produced an unexpected result.

An Unexpected Discovery Creates "Super HGF"

At the higher concentration, LASSS did much more than protect HGF from chemical damage. It also dramatically improved the protein's ability to bind to its receptor.

Compared with untreated HGF, the protein exposed to LASSS showed more than twice the binding affinity for c-met. In other words, it could attach to its target receptor much more strongly, potentially enhancing a critical step in the muscle repair process.

The treatment also made HGF more resistant to the loss of function caused by nitration, particularly at the Y198 site.

Notably, the effect was specific to LASSS. Although GSSSG had also reduced nitration in the earlier experiments, it did not produce the same improvement in receptor binding.

"This exceeded our expectations," comments Tatsumi. "We knew trisulfides had diverse biological functions, but we never expected that simply mixing HGF with LASSS would produce such a striking effect.

"What this tells us is that LASSS does more than simply neutralize reactive molecules. It may interact directly with HGF and induce a subtle structural change, creating an enhanced 'Super HGF' form that binds c-met more strongly and resists nitration."

The researchers suspect that LASSS interacts with HGF in a way that slightly alters the protein's three-dimensional shape. Because a protein's shape helps determine how well it interacts with other molecules, even a small structural adjustment could substantially change its activity.

The result is what the team describes as "Super HGF," a potentially enhanced form of the body's existing muscle repair signal.

Importantly, stronger receptor binding does not automatically establish that muscle regeneration itself has improved. Additional experiments will be needed to determine whether this molecular enhancement translates into better muscle healing and strength.

Mouse Experiments Reveal Promising Protection

After observing the effects in laboratory experiments, the researchers wanted to determine whether LASSS could also protect HGF inside living muscle tissue.

They used mice subjected to tail suspension, an established experimental method for studying muscle atrophy. By reducing normal weight bearing and muscle use, this technique produces some of the changes associated with prolonged inactivity, including muscle deterioration.

Mice that received LASSS before the experiment showed significantly less HGF nitration than untreated animals. This suggested that the compound's ability to protect the muscle repair protein was not limited to controlled laboratory conditions.

Once again, GSSSG failed to produce the same protective result.

These findings provide early evidence that LASSS can influence the chemical processes affecting HGF within living animals. However, the mouse experiments demonstrated protection against nitration, not that LASSS restored lost muscle mass or improved physical strength.

The researchers emphasize that studies involving aging animals are still necessary to establish the compound's effectiveness and safety in vivo, meaning within a living organism.

A Potential New Strategy Against Age-Related Muscle Loss

The discovery could eventually contribute to treatments aimed at maintaining muscle function during aging or extended periods of inactivity.

Muscle deterioration is not limited to older adults. It can also occur during prolonged bed rest or other situations in which muscles are used less frequently. When muscle repair mechanisms become impaired, recovering lost strength and function can become especially challenging.

Rather than replacing the body's natural repair machinery, the approach explored in this study seeks to protect and enhance an existing biological signal. If the benefits can be confirmed in future studies, strengthening HGF activity could become one strategy for supporting muscle regeneration.

The scientists also believe that the underlying effects of LASSS on HGF may extend across species. That raises the possibility of applications not only in human medicine but also in veterinary care, particularly for aging companion animals such as dogs and cats.

For now, the findings represent an early step toward understanding how a naturally occurring muscle repair pathway might be strengthened. Whether LASSS can safely and effectively preserve muscle function during aging remains an open question.

Still, the unexpected discovery that a sulfur-based compound can both protect and enhance a critical repair protein offers a promising direction for future research, with the long-term goal of helping people maintain mobility, independence, and a better quality of life as they grow older.

Materials provided by Kyushu University. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.

#4324. Tomorrow's Battlefield 6 patch somehow makes jets more useless, improves armor bar visibility in Redsec

The first Battlefield 6 patch of the year is almost here, bringing a smattering of changes, including one that doesn't quite make sense.

Battlefield 6’s promised, season-extending update has been officially detailed. The patch, version 1.1.3.5, arrives tomorrow, January 20 right when Season 1 was supposed to end. Part of the update’s goal is to extend the current season, until Season 2 kicks off in the middle of February.

Update 1.1.3.5 does, of course, have a change log of its own that goes beyond just the season’s extension, but the changes fall somewhere between not very exciting, and a bit puzzling.

Patch 1.1.3.5 is, for all intents and purposes, a smaller update. When Battlefield Studios announced it earlier last week, the developer didn’t promise any major changes or fixes, so expectations never got out of hand.

The patch is mainly made up of bug fixes, but it does have three key areas of improvements to gameplay. There’s a big focus on melee combat, how responsive/unresponsive it is with the various melee tools, and how melee behaviour interacts with sprinting and other animations.

The end result should be faster attack speeds for the knife, and clearer wind-up animations for both the knife and the sledgehammer. The timing dictating when melee damage gets credited has also been made more consistent in different environments.

Interestingly, sprint is now only interrupted when the melee attack reaches its target. As it stands, sprinting is only interrupted after the full duration of the animation has been completed, which adds to the that perceived feeling of sluggishness.

The other major, and arguably most confusing is the nerf to jet cannons. The patch is going to make jets far less stronger against other air vehicles, requiring 40% more hits to destroy a target. This is puzzling because jets - and air vehicles in general - are already the least survivable in Battlefield 6.

And, considering how the rest of a jet's arsenal is either situational or nearly ineffective, the cannons were really the one guaranteed way of downing other air vehicles, so long as you manage to land your shots consistently. While the change is wellmeaning, the percentage will likely be reduced in future patches.

Finally, the update makes a few refinements to UI across the game, though mainly aimed at Redsec and modes where players wear armor. Armor bar visibility has been improved, and there’s a fix for the annoying bug that sometimes caused the armor bar to disappear every few seconds.

Read on below for the 1.1.3.5 change log.

It will be held at Avalon Hollywood on December 3, but it won't be livestreamed, so you'll need to grab a ticket to see the event. The press release states that people who signed up for updates from adhocstudio.com will be the first in line to purchase tickets.

#4321. Tenebris Somnia Review – A Hair-Raising And Entertaining Throwback

Tenebris Somnia channels the old-school appeal of classic point-and-click adventures, survival horror, and full-motion-video (FMV) experiences, then smartly modernizes them to create a creepy, entertaining experience. Surviving the twisted threats of a demonic dream world is a tightly packed adventure that rewards you with what’s essentially an impressive indie horror film peppered throughout. It’s a nightmare you may not want to wake up from.

The blend of live-action and in-game storytelling works well in Tenebris Somina’s adventure, which begins when protagonist Julia visits the apartment of her filmmaker ex-boyfriend, Ivan, after suffering recurring nightmares of him being massacred by monsters. What begins as a well-meaning check-in on his status spirals down an unsettling rabbit hole when Julia’s worst fears are realized and then some. The dialogue-free tale presents a scary but fascinating exploration of obsession, both in art and in romance, that constantly delivers surprising, and at times upsetting, revelations during its eight-hour runtime. While Tenebris Somnia sometimes leans a little too far into “tell, don’t show” territory when explaining the cool lore of its supernatural threats, I never felt lost or confused about the wild things that regularly unfold on screen.

FMV experiences are nothing new, but Tenebris Somnia’s live-action scenes are a highlight. They’re well shot, sport impressively gruesome practical effects, and even present visual clues that make them important to gameplay. These scenes are additive, never taking too much time away from the in-game action, and they feel well placed to elicit the strongest emotional response. I also appreciate how the live scenes fit thematically, as much of Tenebris Somnia’s tale centers on a horror film shot by Ivan and Julia that significantly impacted their former relationship; at times, it’s like watching a movie about the movie. While I enjoy smaller moments, like opening a door to trigger a live-action jump scare, the filmmaking succeeds in selling Julia's emotions and the cast's reactions. Seeing real fear, concern, and determination in Julia’s eyes as she navigates a dreamworld made up of Ivan’s memories helped endear me to what would otherwise be a featureless pixel sprite.

Gameplay may look unimpressive due to its old-school adventure game presentation, but Tenebris Somnia’s spin on familiar survival-horror mechanics hits the right notes. Taking place entirely within a dreamlike version of a four-story apartment building, you’ll traverse floors collecting and combining objects and deciphering clues to solve well-crafted puzzles. I’m impressed by how well the game’s puzzles make the most of its limited graphical presentation, including clever scenarios involving mirror/screen reflections I won’t spoil, and how consistently creative they are. One devious exercise even utilizes the game’s limited save points as an unexpected resource in a way that changes how you approach your adventure going forward. No matter how strange puzzles become, they are never opaque, requiring just enough out-of-the-box thinking to make me feel smart when I connect the dots.

Battling grotesque monsters (which, naturally, look even creepier in live-action) also feels good, with melee and gunplay sporting deliberate animations reminiscent of classic adventure games without feeling mechanically clunky. Taking on multiple enemies by swinging a pipe or blowing them away with a shotgun feels better than it looks, and the most intense encounters end just as they approach the line of becoming overwhelming.

Boss battles, perhaps most unexpectedly for a largely puzzle-focused adventure, are fun and distinct from each other, be it wave-based bouts against small gremlin-like foes, protecting a fragile effigy of yourself from a parade of demented house servants, or battling literal mirror images of a tentacled flesh monster the Resident Evil series would be proud to claim. Managing limited ammo and health strikes a good balance of feeling tense but not oppressive. Playing conservatively is rewarding, as few non-boss threats need to be engaged if you can evade them well enough. But when I did find myself down to my last bullet or on the verge of death, Tenebris Somnia lets you feel the pinch just long enough before dropping a box of bullets or a health vial at the right moment.

Tenebris Somnia mines the enjoyable nostalgia of playing the horror games of yesteryear without feeling dated in the worst way. Weaving a solid indie horror film adds to the experience rather than feeling like a gimmick. The result is a captivating, well-executed survival-horror romp that maintains a hair-raising atmosphere with a fraction of the pixels of other genre giants.

In case you missed the tragic news yesterday, EA laid off 400 employees this week, including all of BioWare. The studio behind Mass Effect, Dragon Age, Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic, and more, has been shut down, and its last remaining project was canceled. The game in question was a fifth entry in the Mass Effect universe, and BioWare shared very little about it – not even an official name. Following the studio's closure, however, a trailer for the sci-fi sequel started circulating around the internet.

While no official BioWare representatives have confirmed that the footage is real, Bloomberg reporter Jason Schreier claims that it is. Schreier has a history of credible reporting in the field, and was the first to break the news about the layoffs. IGN has also stated that it confirmed the trailer's legitimacy.

If you want to see for yourself, you can watch the trailer on Reddit.

"The following is in-engine footage form our small team," text at the start of the video reads. "It uses our pre-production assets." The footage shows no gameplay, but includes a good-looking CG cutscene of a new protagonist speaking with an asari woman in a crowded bar. As he tells her about his life, we see glimpses of him as a soldier, then as some kind of spy, traveling to several planets to track down conflicts and "stopping them before they start." After the asari woman reveals that she's been "starting the fires" he's trying to prevent, another woman behind her lowers a hood. This new woman reveals herself as Liara T'Soni, one of Mass Effect's most iconic characters.

Then, Liara and the protagonist team up to take out the woman at the bar and her henchmen, using guns and telekinetic abilities. The trailer fades to black, then fades back in to reveal the game's would-be title: Mass Effect Universe. It's a great-looking trailer – it's a shame the game will never see the light of day.

#4318. Metal Slug Awakening tier list and a reroll guide

While there are quite a few characters released right now, some of which are free to obtain from the story mode, not all of them are worth spending your resources on. Of course, it all comes down to your playstyle, so if you want to put together a team with a specific character, by all means, do that! Who are the best characters in Metal Slug Awakening? I can't exactly say that a character is 100% bad or 100% good, since it all comes down to skill and the synergy the characters have on the team.

You can have up to three characters deployed, which would mean one core character attacking and two supporters. During a battle, you can freely switch between them at any time, so making the right choice there is important.

You should always pick characters that complement each other. For instance, if you feel like you need some healing, then you should deploy a character that does that. Likewise, if you need a specific damage pattern, you need to think of a character that has that in their kit. It's really up to you and what teams you like and what characters' playstyles you enjoy, so take our Metal Slug Awakening tier list with a grain of salt. Can you reroll in Metal Slug Awakening? Is it worth it? Rerolling in Metal Slug Awakening is not something I would advise, since the entire process takes a while. Not only that, but obtaining the characters you want is not guaranteed, and since you can pretty much make any character work, it ultimately doesn't make any sense to reroll.

If you really want to, you can try binding to a different account where you can restart, but like I said before, rerolling is not a thing in Metal Slug Awakening.

#4317. Fortnite Players are Scrambling for an Exceedingly Rare Treasure

Daniel is a lifelong gamer with a love for various genres and gameplay styles who enjoys exploring games and playing from various angles.

In One Piece, the titular mysterious treasure left behind by the late Pirate King Gol D. Roger is said to be something of such unfathomable power, it could overturn everything people know about the world itself. Over 20 years later, we still don’t know what the One Piece actually is, but there have certainly been more than a few treasure hunts inspired by its legendary mystique. Rather fittingly, one of those treasures has manifested in the midst of Fortnite’s newest pirate-themed mini-season, and it's driving the internet bonkers.

On Sunday, following the end of the Fortnitemares Halloween event, Fortnite began an interstitial mini-season to tide players over until the next major content drop in December. This mini-season, Treasure Hunters, is most predominantly One Piece-themed, featuring a new map with various One Piece locales and a handful of One Piece characters in the shop and Battle Pass.

The people gave Sweeney and Epic all the attention and support it needed when it rose up to Apple. As a reward, players got a significant price hike.

However, in addition to that, outside of the actual announcements, a new element has been quietly added to the game, and following its discovery by the playerbase, a mad scramble to locate it on par with One Piece’s own Great Age of Piracy has begun. Players have set sail from all over in search of the Pirate Shop Token, the treasure that will make their (cosmetic-centric) dreams come true.

The Pirate Shop Token is a new item that has begun spawning in chests on the new map during Fortnite's pirate-themed Treasure Hunters mini-season. To put it succinctly, obtaining the Pirate Shop Token is a free pass to almost everything in the Fortnite shop.

Obtaining the Pirate Shop Token is a free pass to almost everything in the Fortnite shop.

If you happen to obtain the token, as the game will inform you after the fact, you can activate it at any time until its expiration on December 16, 2026. When the token is activated, any item in the Fortnite shop will become free to claim, even if you don’t have a single V-Buck to your name. From pickaxes to outfits to gliders, it’s all fair game. Not only that, but from the moment of activation, the Pirate Shop Token remains in effect for two weeks, which means you can keep helping yourself to the shop’s contents day after day until it expires. You’ll also receive a second token that can be activated at a currently-indeterminate point in 2027.

Following the arrest of a featured artist, Fortnite is allowing players to refund associated cosmetics.

There are some caveats here: real money offers, gifting and passes levels and rewards are excluded, and you can only claim one free sidekick that you don’t already own. Beyond those few bits, though, the rest is plunderable. We’re talking cumulative values in the hundreds of dollars in assorted cosmetics here, and suffice to say, a lot of people would very much like that.

Perhaps unsurprisingly, such a fabulous treasure isn’t going to be easy to find. The only way to obtain the Pirate Shop Token is to find it on the map after it randomly spawns in, for which there is no particular indication or notification. The actual odds of this spawn occurring are a black box secret held by Epic, though some rumors have circulated that they’re in the ballpark of 1 in 700,000. There have also been rumors that you’re more likely to find it if you’re lower-leveled, but these are probably bunk.

The only tangible thing you can do to improve your odds is grouping up. If one player in a party finds the token, everyone in the party gets it. This has sparked a new wave of mercenaries in the Fortnite community, with players offering their services to others to party up and systematically sweep the island for its chests in the hopes of finding a token.

On a less savory note, some users with alleged Pirate Shop Token access have begun attempting to sell their accounts on eBay, with proposed prices in the thousands, while others have attempted to circulate cheating tools to fudge the spawn rates. Epic issued a statement on these practices via the Fortnite Status X, formerly Twitter page, writing, “Buying an account or using fake tools is a scam. This is just like any of the chests in Battle Royale, so every player has an equal opportunity to find Pirate Shop Access.” Buying and selling Fortnite accounts is also a bannable offense, so don’t do that.

The group is seeking over €100 million in combined refunds and damages on behalf of underage players.

KRÜ Blaze dropped the first map and then took the next three on Saturday 31 October. The win reverses their upper bracket semi-final defeat to Shopify Rebellion Gold and sends the Argentine-based side into the final of the VCT Game Changers Championship 2026. Shopify Rebellion Gold’s campaign ends with the loss.

The result also cuts against the power rankings. Shopify Rebellion Gold arrived as the 10th-ranked team with a rating of 1782. KRÜ Blaze sit 20th on 1742, although their 63-21 record across 84 rated matches is the stronger of the two.

Shopify Rebellion Gold struck first, taking a 47-minute opening map. KRÜ Blaze levelled on the quickest map of the series, which lasted 37 minutes, and edged ahead with a 50-minute third.

The fourth map was by some distance the longest of the night at 70 minutes. KRÜ Blaze closed it out to settle the best-of-five without needing a decider.

The meeting on 27 October had been far more one-sided. Shopify Rebellion Gold won that upper bracket semi-final 2-0, which pushed KRÜ Blaze into the lower half of the draw. Before that, KRÜ Blaze had opened their playoff run by beating Gen.G GC 2-1 in the upper bracket quarter-finals.

Saturday’s victory was KRÜ Blaze’s third successive series win in the lower bracket. Both earlier wins were sweeps. They beat Team Liquid Brazil 2-0 in the quarter-finals, then dispatched MIBR GC by the same score in the semi-finals.

That run means they have won seven of the eight maps played since dropping out of the upper bracket. They also came into the event as winners of the Latin America regional final, where they beat Akave Esports Black 3-1.

#4315. Battlefield 6’s first big map in months is coming to Labs soon, but I'm more excited about BF4's Golmud Railway making its way to BF6

As promised, Battlefield Labs is coming back to bring us a preview of some of Battlefield 6’s upcoming Season 2 content.

Battlefield 6’s Season 2 was recently pushed back by a month to give Battlefield Studios time to polish up its content. Now, the developer has revealed how it plans to use some of that time, and the first port of call is Battlefield Labs.

As discussed in the initial delay message, BF Studios wants the community’s involvement earlier and more consistently in the development of future content. This includes Season 2, of course, and a big component of what it’s bringing to the game is headed to Labs.

The first Battlefield Labs session kicking off soon will focus on Contaminated, one of the new maps coming to Battlefield 6 with Season 2. BF Studios says the map falls between Eastwood and Mirak Valley, in terms of size.

The blog post even likened it to Battlefield 1’s St. Quentin Scar, and Battlefield 5’s Arras. Although we’ve yet to actually play it, the size and description do sound really well, especially in a game as starved of big maps as Battlefield 6 currently is.

Another thing BF Studios wants to test is the way ground vehicle gameplay and aerial presence interact with infantry combat, which is pretty standard for most Battlefield maps. Interestingly, there appears to be some sort of mechanic unique to Contaminated that the developer also wants to evaluate.

More Labs sessions are planned, including one that will show off new gameplay tools and vehicles. The AH-6 Little Bird helicopter was specifically namedropped, which makes sense given that it’s going to be part of Season 2’s content.

Battlefield Labs sessions will also extend beyond the biggest-ticket items of maps and vehicles. BF Studios said we should expect tests of upcoming features, like the Aircraft Radar, as part of a list of other air combat updates.

Ground vehicles, and they way the various rockets interact with them, will also be evaluated in a different session, with specific adjustments planned for RPGs and TOWs. And, of course, the work to improve and perfect hit reg remains ongoing, and future tweaks will go through Labs first.

There’s even more exciting news for fans of big maps, as the blog post also confirmed that Battlefield 4’s Golmud Railway is currently in the works, planned to go live in a future season. Golmud Railway will show up early in Labs, and you can expect it to evolve over multiple sessions.

For context, when it does arrive in Battlefield 6, Golmud Railway will be the largest map in the game, which is saying something. Though the map is beloved by vehicle players, it has its issues elsewhere, and BF Studios says it will be looking at all that when it creates the BF6, emphasising that it won’t be a simple port of the BF4 original.

Finally, the post throws a bone to Redsec battle royale players still waiting for a Solo mode. BF Studios continues to test the idea internally, but it’s taking a while. Needless to say, there are so many aspects that need to be considered. Game pace, balance, player survivability, match flow just to name a few.

Redsec BR was built with squads in mind, so that task is extra challenging. Though the developer didn’t say when we can expect Solos to arrive in Labs, players will get a chance to experience it before it enters the live game.

#4314. Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 Review - Silver Bullet

Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 arrives at a crossroads for the series, thanks in large part to the inconsistent quality of recent entries. With a shaky predecessor, Infinity Ward had a lot to repair and conclude, especially with 4 set to bookend the rebooted Modern Warfare series. Fortunately, backed up by a fun campaign, thrilling multiplayer, and loads of new modes and content, Modern Warfare 4 makes up for the past and then some.

Modern Warfare 4 continues after the events of 2023’s Modern Warfare 3, with Captain Price hellbent on stopping Makarov and his higher-ups. The story features shifting perspectives, from a new group of ragtag Korean soldiers to familiar characters like Gaz. The character dynamics harken back to the original trilogy, especially in the boots-on-the-ground missions with the South Korean unit, led by Park (played by Beef actor Young Mazino).

For a series that, at least recently, has been more spectacle than story, giving the stakes the time they deserve is nice. While it moves away from the stealthy and modernized elements, it makes sense for the matters at hand. The majority of Modern Warfare 4’s attempts at wrapping up the overarching plot of the rebooted series works, but it rushes through some character arcs and story beats in uneven fashion. Furthermore, much of the game’s cast, especially Mads Mikkelson’s Archer and Prisca Kim’s Ri Ju-Young, are underutilized, which is a shame since they both deliver great performances.

Despite the shortcomings of the campaign, Call of Duty's bread and butter, multiplayer, still delivers. While it doesn’t have the fluidity of Black Ops’ newer entries, the customization and design of weapons and maps make it worth digging into. From small, intimate shooting galleries with Mumbai and Nautical to wide free-for-alls like Coal and Reactor U92, the range helps maintain excitement, even if it gets repetitive over time.

The variety of multiplayer modes keeps things fresh on the battlefield. Returning modes like standard Team Deathmatch and Kill Confirmed continue that enjoyable competitive flair that made them the stars that they are. However, new modes like Combat Outpost and Hijack fit right into the already great lineup. In particular, Combat Outpost upscales your typical 6v6 player count to 24v24, leading to more action and teamwork. Hanging onto a team’s tank, shooting enemies from afar, and taking back outposts is exhilarating, even if it can all go bad moments later by a well-placed RPG shot.

Even after hours of gameplay, the variety of options to craft your perfect gun is impressive. Figuring out the best scope, ammo, stock, and muzzle, as well as the advantages and disadvantages of them, is a fun way of customizing your playstyle. Gunny, a mechanic that helps optimize your gun for certain styles, can help with decision paralysis, but I rarely used it. Not many FPSs go that far and Modern Warfare 4’s commitment to the feature makes it stand out.

The newest mode, DMZ, impresses out of the gate. After a few flat attempts in the past, this is the definitive Call of Duty extraction shooter, whether you play solo, or in duos or trios. Immediately, you’re thrust into the wide open world of Hajin and left to fend for yourselves with what you have and what you can gather and extract. Fans of Arc Raiders and Marathon should feel right at home as the gameplay borrows from the typical extraction shooter experience. Intense, action-packed moments keep you coming back after every win or loss. And the excellent gunplay and level design elevate it into something worthwhile, no matter how you play.

Despite not encountering many live players during my time in Hajin in DMZ, it still proves challenging, even for seasoned pros. The world is not your friend, and taking risks can come at a high cost. A good team, as well as a thoughtful loadout and traits, are required to survive. The unpredictability of it all keeps you on your toes, making for an exciting addition to the already strong multiplayer suite.

Regardless of the mode, Modern Warfare 4 is one of the best-looking Call of Duty titles to date. New York and Paris are lifelike, and it truly embodies the realistic, modern aesthetic the series has always aimed to achieve. However, I encountered a few technical hiccups, especially in the campaign. Slow framerate plagues some high-octane scenes and texture loading is frequent across the board. These distractions are far from game-breaking, but enough to be noticeable.

While the plot execution is a bit shaky, engaging multiplayer options, including DMZ, aptly demonstrate that Infinity Ward can still deliver compelling military-FPS experiences. Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 is a strong return to form that serves as a solid sendoff for the rebooted subseries.

#4313. Jujutsu Kaisen Phantom Parade tier list - Ranking every character

Updated on November 5th, 2026 - Version: 3.8.4 - Added:  [Effective Range] Mai Zen'in

After multiple delays, Jujutsu Kaisen Phantom Parade was finally released in Japan, and after much speculation, it made its way over to the West as well, allowing fans of Jujutsu Kaisen to try yet another anime-inspired mobile game. To keep our readers up to date on the game’s turn-based combat meta, we’ve created this Jujutsu Kaisen Phantom Parade tier list.

In this tier list, we’ll judge every character’s combat abilities and rank them. All the major characters appearing in the anime are playable, so expect to see some familiar names. However, there are some new faces too. The developers have created a few original characters exclusively for Phantom Parade.

You can find other similar content, including our Dungeon Hunter 6 Lieutenants tier list, One Piece Treasure Cruise tier list since you clearly love anime, and this Fruit Battlegrounds tier list, since that's a Roblox version of one anime that we won't name. But before you dive into any of them, here’s a quick explanation of how this tier list works and what the different tiers represent. Jujutsu Kaisen Phantom Parade tier list explained When making a tier list for Jujutsu Kaisen Phantom Parade, it'd be impossible, and somewhat pointless, to include every character.. So, naturally, this tier list will only rank playable characters. We’re using four tiers to rank them, and here’s a quick explanation of each tier:

With his immense cursed energy and powerful technique, Satoru Gojo has become the strongest sorcerer in the Jujutsu Kaisen universe. And it’s no different here. With skills like Six Eyes and Limitless, Satoru can annihilate enemies in a single blow. That’s something you need on your team during turn-based combat.

Yuji’s best friend, Aoi Todo, has some destructive moves and an even more devastating Ultimate that can deal five-figure damage. Yuji and Aoi make a great pair in the game. Get these two on your team and forget about losing.

Much like Satoru Gojo, the devs also see the potential in Megumi Fushiguro. That’s the only reason a Grade 2 sorcerer has the kind of stats and skills that Megumi has. Although his intelligence won’t be much help in this turn-based RPG, his shikigami and weapon expertise are.

Despite being a non-sorcerer, Maki Zenin has the skills and the combat prowess to hold her own against some strong sorcerers. If you love weapons more than jujutsu, Maki is your fighter.

Toge Inumkai is a one-off. With his cursed speech, he can crush, twist, and explode his enemies just by saying the words. Some of his skill animations are crazy, too. Masamichi Yaga might be the principal of the sorcery school, but he’s not really that strong, especially in the game. However, his ability to take control of corpses makes him a valuable asset.

In the anime, Nobara Kugisaki is a Grade 3 sorcerer. The devs almost copy-pasted her skills, hence tier B. Her weapons are fun to play around with, but she’s better at defense than offense.

Current and former students, a school director, and a sorcerer turned doctor, the C tier is a mixed bag of weak characters. Momo Nishimiya barely has jujutsu, and Kasumi Miwa has no skills apart from a sub-par jujutsu. You won’t get much out of these even after a fully upgraded card.

That’s it for our Jujutsu Kaisen Phantom Parade tier list. If the meta gets shaken up at any point, this tier list will be updated accordingly. Also, note that there are multiple variations of the characters. For instance, there's Hollow Purple version of Satoru Gojo. These variations come and go. That’s why we didn’t use them in our tier list.Stay up to date with what we know so far about the Jujutsu Kaisen Phantom Parade.

#4312. Amazon’s Mass Effect TV Series Is Reportedly Still In Production Despite BioWare Closure

EA shut down legendary RPG developer BioWare this week, canceling its in-development fifth Mass Effect game as a result. Despite the closure, Amazon Prime’s upcoming Mass Effect streaming series will proceed as planned, according to a report by IGN.

Amazon MGM Studios began developing a Mass Effect series in 2024. At the time, Mass Effect series executive producer Mike Gamble confirmed the show isn't a retelling of the video games, saying, “The show will explore a brand-new story within the universe's timeline, and will be set after the original trilogy. It won't be a retread of Commander Shepard's story – because after all... that's YOUR story, isn’t it?”

With BioWare’s closure, one would think the series would go up in smoke, but sources within Prime Video speaking to IGN confirmed that it remains in development. Furthermore, all of the creatives involved remain so. This includes showrunners Doug Jung (The Cloverfield Paradox, Star Trek Beyond) and Daniel Casey (F9: The Fast Saga, Wardriver), former Marvel Studios head Avi Arad, and Jessica Jones executive producer Karim Zreik. Mike Gamble was also involved, and this report suggests he still is, but it remains to be seen how his position on the project has changed with BioWare’s demise, given he served as a guiding voice from the studio. The Mass Effect series has no release window.

The Mass Effect series joins other video game adaptations Amazon has in the works, which include a third season of Fallout (with Aaron Paul joining the cast), a live-action God of War series starring Dave Bautista, a live-action Tomb Raider series starring Sophie Turner, as well as series based on Life is Strange and Wolfenstein.

#4311. Go Go Muffin tier list - Which class should you play?

The overall power of every class in the game depends on the build, so we have ranked each one on this Go Go Muffin tier list and included a build for each class.

Updated on November 5th, 2026 - Version: 1.2.4

If you've been wondering which class to pick in Go Go Muffin, you're in luck - I will shed some light on each of the classes and rank them all according to how strong they are, as well as how in-demand they currently are. Go Go Muffin Classes overview There are five classes in Go Go Muffin, each one fulfilling a specific role. Depending on the builds, each of the classes can be a damage dealer, but not all of them can be dedicated tanks or healers. At the moment, the basic classes are:

Each class will be broken down on the following pages, so if you're interested in finding out more about each one of them, I recommend you check them out.  Don't forget to redeem the latest codes for Go Go Muffin right here - we have Global and SEA codes too! Best class in Go Go Muffin - a tier list I have to start by mentioning that each class is good in its own way. They are all pretty well-balanced, and as long as you optimise their gear and skills, you can never go wrong with whichever choice you make. From a necessity point of view, we could create a tier list that ranks all the classes in Go Go Muffin. Tier Class Most requested (S+ tier) Acolyte, Swordbearer Extremely good for bosses (S tier) Shadowlash Great overall, can do great AoE damage (S- tier) Wayfarer, Scholar

Personally, I went for the Scholar class because I love their playstyle, and I still do extremely high damage in Rifts and Dragon, although I might have higher-level teammates or teammates with higher CP.  How to pick your class? My recommendation is that you pick the class you are most comfortable with. You shouldn't let a Go Go Muffin tier list decide which class you want to play, because at the end of the day, if you don't enjoy the playstyle of your selected class, there is no point in continuing with that character.

So, let's examine each Go Go Muffin class in more detail: Acolyte - Swordbearer - Shadowlash - Scholar - Wayfarer Original article by Cristina Mesesan. Updated by Mihail Katsoris.

The Acolyte class is the only one that can heal the party. They possess powerful spells that can heal allies, keeping them alive in battle for the longest time. They are essential to any party, which is what makes them so in-demand. They can also go for a DPS build, which is extremely powerful too.

Class change path: Acolyte - as the normal class, you will mostly have some heals and a little bit of damage. It is important to get past the first 80 levels quickly and reach CC 1 so you can have access to better skills.

Thaumaturge - this is the CC 2 class for the Acolyte, which is a beast in terms of damage. They are good for heals, too, obviously. Should you play Acolyte? If you want to play a role that is not as "AFK-friendly" as some of the others, you'd better play Acolyte. It is overall one of the best classes you can choose right now, since they are extremely in demand for the later stages. In most parties, they are accepted right away.

The Swordbearer class is the only one that can act as the tank. They are bulky, (unsurprisingly) wield a sword, and can also fill the DPS role. Although they are simple at first glance, there is a lot that goes into being a good Swordbearer.

Class change path: Swordbearer - as the normal class, the tankiness is there, the damage is there, and it's a really well-rounded class.

Swordmaster - this is the CC 2 class for the Swordbearer, which is extremely good in terms of damage in the story, and in parties, they can tank pretty much anything. Should you play Swordbearer? Do you like going head-first into action and not having a care in the world about the incoming damage? Then this is a great class for you. You will be able to tank anything and everything, and if you so choose to go for DPS, while you won't be the best of the best, you'll still tank long enough and deal plenty of damage. Self-sustain and damage for the win!

The Shadowlash class is an outstanding DPS class that has assassin-type gameplay. They are melee ranged, but can deal insanely high damage in a short amount of time. They are great against bosses, and they can do pretty well in story mode too.

Class change path: Shadowlash - as the normal class, they have one of the highest damage outputs among all the classes. They are only surpassed by the Wayfarer as CC 0 (in some situations).

Nightweaver - this is the CC 2 class for the Shadowlash, which can deal some of the highest DPS in the game. Most parties at the top of the leaderboards have Nightweavers since the damage they deal is just THAT good. Should you play Shadowlash? If you're a fan of the assassin class in other games, this is the right choice for you. Of course, it will be a long road getting to Nightweaver, but it is well worth it. It's a fun and flashy class, and they have a cool look too. They probably look the best in the game at the moment.

The Scholar class is the equivalent of a mage in any other game - they are a master of elemental magic, and they require combo after combo to deal continuous damage to enemies. It's a class for those who like a little bit of challenge, and seeing results when all the work they've put in yields results.

Class change path: Scholar - as the normal class, they are focused on Fire. The skills are not that great, but if you bear with them, at CC 1 they will become A LOT better.

Archmage - this is the CC 2 class for the Scholar, which uses the Lightning element. Their skills really shine through, and so does their damage. At this stage, most people who put up with Scholar's "weaker" kits will be extremely satisfied. Should you play Scholar? The Scholar is a class that rewards you for your patience. At CC 1, you start getting a glimpse of how strong they can be, and if you reach Archmage, you will be really happy with your choice. If you don't mind the wait, it's a great class for you. They are ranged, they can deal amazing AoE damage, and their weapon looks pretty neat too!

The Wayfarer class is the equivalent of an archer. They are exceptional at dealing AoE and single target damage, and they are extremely powerful all the way throughout - from CC 0 until CC 2.

Class change path: Wayfarer- as the normal class, they are great at DPS. They can deal both ST and AoE, which makes them great overall, regardless of content.

Eagle Eye - this is the CC 2 class for the Wayfarer. This class is great, they deal amazing damage, and even though they are not as powerful as the Shadowlash, they are still great since their core skill will make them shine. Should you play Wayfarer? If you like a class that is solid all throughout the game, from the beginning until the end, the Wayfarer is the one for you. Their playstyle is like an archer, so even though they are not that tanky, they can deal insane amounts of damage.

That's our whole Go Go Muffin tier list with the best build for each class. Fans of character rankings will love the fact that we have a Goddess Era tier list and a tier list for Maiden Academy. Of course, there are many others - just search for the game you're interested in!

#4310. Arc Raiders finally reveals early 2026 roadmap, but we’re not getting a new map for a while

The first couple of months of 2026 in the world of Arc Raiders look pretty promising, but the big guns are being held back for now.

After weeks of waiting, Arc Raiders developer Embark has officially unveiled the first few months of the game’s 2026 roadmap. The plan is split into four months, covering January to April, collectively dubbed Escalation.

We’re expecting a content update each month, with the majority of the biggest additions happening on the game’s existing maps. There is, however, at least one new map in the works, but it won’t be here until sometime in April.

While we wait for that, Arc Raiders is going to go through several events and other in-game changes, some more meaningful (and exciting) than others. January looks to be the lightest so far, which makes sense given that it’s just a week or so from ending.

January’s chapter is titled Headwinds, kicking off on January 27. This segment will see the addition of a new matchmaking option for players above level 40 - at or near the game’s endgame. We’re also expecting a new Map Condition, and a new Player Project for everyone to contribute to.

Things start getting interesting in February, when Shrouded Sky will begin. This chapter brings three exciting additions to Arc Raiders. There will be a new Map Condition, new Arc Threat, and the start of another Player Project.

Interestingly, we’re going to see some sort of map update during the month, but Embark didn’t share anymore details. The next Raider Deck will also deploy in February, alongside a new Expedition Window.

The Flashpoint chapter begins in March, when we’re expecting another new Map Condition, one more new Arc Threat, as well as another Player Project. March’s most interesting addition is an update to everyone’s trusty rooster friend, Scrappy.

Finally, April is when the big guns come out, because that’s when the first new map of 2026 will arrive in Arc Raiders. With it, comes a new large Arc, which is to be expected. A new Map Condition will debut then, too, likely starting off on the new map.

That’s pretty much it, but seeing as we’re just one day away from the start of the January stage, things are about to get exciting again in Arc Raiders.

#4309. Remedy Explains Control Resonant's Most Memorable, Unexpected Sequence And Its [REDACTED] Inspirations

Please allow the first sentence here to warn you that this interview discusses a portion of Control Resonant that takes place near the end of the game and is arguably the most unexpected and surprising sequence. I encourage you to experience it without spoilers. So if you haven't beaten the game yet, please do, and then come back to this page.However, if you have beaten the game, or curiosity has driven you to learn what game has been redacted from the headline and why (it's the 1995 Super Nintendo RPG, EarthBound, by the way), then please read on.

In the late-game of Control Resonant – basically right before you tackle the final confrontation – the game suddenly shifts timeframe and genre to become a 16-bit RPG. The nostalgic lens turns the game into something that feels like 1995's EarthBound, complete with turn-based battles, in order to explain the trauma that Jesse and Dylan went through at a young age after they came across an object of power: the slide projector. The whole sequence is funny, heartbreaking, weird, and importantly effective at making you feel you are seeing a part of their past. It was particularly effective on me as I have fond memories of playing EarthBound and games like it when I was young. To see and experience Dylan and Jesse's childhood this way felt accurate, as absurd as that sounds.

I reached out to Remedy to specifically discuss that portion of the game. You can find the full e-mail interview below with the team members who contributed to its creation.

The big RPG backstory sequence for Jesse and Dylan – why approach the storytelling that way?

Lead level designer, Anne-Marie Grönroos: The basis for the whole sequence is that the Hedron attacks Dylan's mind, breaks his reality apart, and he has to rebuild himself. We wanted the reality-breaking part to affect the game itself and have the player feel some of the confusion Dylan is feeling by breaking the fourth wall.

Who pitched that sequence, how did they pitch it, and was it difficult to sell to the larger team?

Grönroos: At Remedy, ideas rarely come from a single person or team, and we rarely do formal pitches, but rather discuss and workshop ideas cross-craft until they start taking the shape of something we like. The initial idea from the writer was for this to be a text-based adventure, to return to a very early form of a video game to show that the Patterning is devolving him, but an Alan Wake 2 DLC had already done that, and we wanted to find something else.

Independently, some months ago a level designer had suggested a sidequest with JRPG pixel graphics, but that had gone nowhere. I remembered that and suggested doing an old Final Fantasy-style JRPG here, which also felt more fitting since that’s the type of game Dylan and Jesse would have played in their childhood, and not a text-based adventure. People got excited about that, and after some concerns about feasibility, we went forth with it. It helped that the level designer who had originally wanted to do the JRPG side quest is a big fan of these types of games and has made them before. I wouldn’t have dropped something this crazy on someone who wasn’t passionate about it and ready to figure out how to do it with our engine that’s not built for anything like this.

Is EarthBound (Mother in Japan) the primary inspiration for that sequence? Are there big fans of those games at Remedy?

Senior level designer in charge of the JRPG quest, Arhi Makkonen:The whole Quest was born from that childhood feeling I had when playing old JRPGs – Final Fantasy, Breath of Fire, Chrono Trigger, Secret of Mana, Bahamut Lagoon, and yes, Mother. The most important thing for me was capturing that feeling of a time when games felt like magic. I think many people can relate to that nostalgia, and now Jesse and Dylan share that feeling in the game.Visually, Mother was a major inspiration of course. Juuso Anttila is the concept artist who did all the splendid pixel art for Rebuild quest. Mother's style fits the mysterious Americana small town vibe perfectly. We also couldn't pass up the pun about a story revolving around "Not-Mother" that was made in the style of Mother.

Was it difficult to implement the sequence into the game? Did Remedy's Northlight Engine need significant work to account for the sequence?

Makkonen: The Northlight engine was designed to work perfectly for third-person action games. Well, Rebuild Quest is pretty much the opposite of that. Northlight is a specialized tool rather than a general-purpose one, so we had to come up with some rather creative solutions to create a 2D JRPG.

First of all, we’re faking the 2D look. In reality, the entire JRPG Ordinary exists within a 3D world that the camera simply views from directly overhead. It occupies a tiny patch in a remote corner of the game world—a space where 3D Dylan would barely have room to stand. The entire game-within-a-game is written in Lua; our incredibly versatile game designer, Tommi Saalasti, created the underlying system, upon which I was then able to build the story.

Since we didn't really have the tools to create a game like this, I had to hand-code every single detail. Dylan takes one step up, Dylan turns left (where Jesse hopefully is at that moment), text box 1, text box 2. The Lua script for the Rebuild quest alone probably contains as many lines of code as all the other quests in the game combined. And then there were things like animations were restricted to a maximum of two frames, and some UI elements were created using static particle effects.

So yes, we faced all sorts of challenges and compromises, but at the heart of it all was a wonderful story – simply told in a somewhat unconventional way. We trusted that the narrative would make up for some of the imperfections.

Remedy has a reputation for big unexpected and often crazy singular moments. What are the conversations like around delivering those? In pre-production, are there conversations like, "What is the big moment for this one?" Or do they happen pretty naturally?

Grönroos: They both happen naturally and we also have conversations about what the big moments should be. Sometimes we like a section so much that we decide to put even more resources and importance to it, even if it wasn’t supposed to be all that important from the get-go. The Into the Sinkhole quest, for instance, is a quest that wasn’t planned to be a “tentpole moment” from the start, but we kept putting more effort into it when it was shaping up to be something very special.

But most setpieces in the game were planned to be such from the early stages of pre-production. In Resonant, we wanted to have multiple standout moments instead of a single sequence like the Ashtray Maze overshadowing everything else, and I’m happy to see that players have different favorites.

And a different approach from Control is that several of these memorable moments (Sinkhole, Underpass Fault, the JRPG section) are more emotional and subdued instead of bombastic action (although we also have big action setpieces), which was an interesting challenge itself.

Was there a fear that the visuals would limit the emotional impact of the sequence?

Grönroos: Yes, but we decided to trust the writing. Several other games have managed to deliver a similar emotional impact despite pixel graphics (and sometimes because of them, since the level [of] abstraction can make characters more relatable and up to the player’s interpretation), so we weren’t too concerned.

Was there a fear that action game fans would be frustrated by the RPG sequence?

Grönroos: Yes, this was the main concern about the sequence. It was a very polarizing sequence in the playtests: people either loved or hated it. We did discuss shortening it significantly, but in the end decided to keep it as it is but added some fast travel options and make some parts skippable. There were more fans than haters, and we didn’t want to sacrifice something we really enjoyed.

How concerned were you about the actual RPG mechanics of that sequence?

Makkonen: Since Rebuild doesn't feature a vast number of battles, we didn't need to build particularly deep RPG or progression systems. The combat served as an additional storytelling tool – illustrating how bullies torment Dylan, showing his first fight (against rats, naturally), and depicting his eventual abduction by the FBC.

Refining the combat to be simple, yet offer the player meaningful choices required a few iterations. In addition to standard attacks, the children can occasionally use special abilities: Dylan delivers a heavy blow to a single enemy, while Jesse fires at everyone. Enemies deal enough damage that defending becomes necessary when multiple foes target the same character.

The lightbulbs in The Underpass mission goes in similarly unexpected, animated directions. How did that mission come about? What was the pitch like for that one?

Grönroos: That one started with the idea of doing something comically mundane, switching lightbulbs, and adding a paranatural twist to it. The cartoon man wasn’t in the initial version, but instead we were going to do live action videos and have Dylan get stuck in that video as the end twist. They were supposed to be old-fashioned “work safety” videos explaining how to change lightbulbs, and as the quest went on, it became more and more obvious that the maintenance guy in the videos was too aware of what Dylan was doing. This all came out from a one-hour workshop.

There wasn’t really a pitch, but rather a back-and-forth like “could we do a quest about Dylan changing lightbulbs in a ritualistic way? We could have these sentient work safety videos explain how to do it and “Dylan could get trapped inside the video.” Much later, when the live action turned out to be a no-go, we pivoted to the current cartoon instead, and that was even funnier than our initial idea.

#4308. Heaven Burns Red tier list and a reroll guide

A tier list and a reroll guide for this phenomenal visual novel, featuring a massive pool of characters and a gripping story to tell.

Updated on November 5th, 2026 - Version: 4.0.2 - Latest Additions: [Welcome to the Nightmare Parade] Tama Kunimi, [Trick Or Trick, Meow] Sumomo Minase, [Banner of Victory Foretold] Yuina Shirakawa, [Glorious Blades] Ruka Kayamori, [Take Your Heart] Ruka Kayamori, [Unwavering Faith] Violet

"Humanity is dying, but I want to form a rockstar band" is the title I would suggest to Ruka if she decides to write a novel summarising Heaven Burns Red. It is a visual novel packed with humorous witticism, banter, and slice-of-life elements, even though the world is in peril, all of which are commensurate with Maeda's years of experience as a writer in this medium.

Thanks to Yostar, it's been freed from the purgatory of being region-locked to Japan. It was launched in a vastly different state compared to its original release two years ago. One noticeable difference is the large roster of 50+ SS memoria that is bound to overwhelm you at first glance.

Past the many charming incentives and login rewards during this honeymoon phase, the premium currency income dries up in a snap. So, once again, we stepped up to the task and pulled together this tier list that ranks each Seraph Style's performance. So you won't part with your quartz that easily on underperformers.

As the game's selling point is its quirky characters, don't let the Heaven Burns Red tier list discourage you from rolling for your favourite. Keep in mind, there are no PvP elements. Hence, our tier list is geared toward how a Seraph can make your playthrough a breeze. Footnote on deciphering our tier list

Original article by Anderson Han. Updated by Mihail Katsoris.

The jack of all trades. Class 31-A features Ruka Kayamori [RY], the airheaded main protagonist, as a class leader. It’s comprised of Izumi Yuki [IY], Aikawa Megumi [AM], Tsukasa Tojo [TT], Karen Asakura [KA] and Kunimi Tama [KT].

For support, Tama's Memorias - Angel Sailor's Valor is valued for her heals and DP revival; Elemental of the Magic Kingdom provides party-wide ATK boost, SP, and DP recovery with her second skill.

For attackers, Megumi's SS Style is highly valued for her capability of inflicting Fragile as well as stun to large areas. She's a godsend in farming content, such as those GP stages in the arena.

Ruka's Memorias - Cardinal Reverberations and Daybreak Impassioned Soul are robust attackers specialising in Light and Fire elements, respectively. They work wonders thanks to their high-hit count on top of being effective against a single target and AoE damage. Hence, a spot at the top of our Heaven Burns Red tier list!

It is composed of Erika Aoi [EA], Ichigo Minase [IM], Sumomo Minase [SM], Seika Higuchi [SH], Kozue Hiiragi [KH] and Byakko [B]. Most of its members are associated with Thunder-element.

Seika is love, Seika is life. Her Style - Exploration of the Universe deserves all the raving it gets. While her party-wide skill attack buff is invaluable, her greatest asset comes in the form of her targetable first skill capable of turning any attacker into a powerhouse - it sharply boosts Crit.DMG, Crit%, Skill attack, and heals DP. Casting these skills is also chump change for her, as it only costs nine SP. What solidifies her ranking is her versatility - she sees use in every mode.

Erika Aoi's Inspiration of the Heart is a Defender who doubles as a Healer. Should you face any powerful charged attack, just use Aoi's first skill to taunt and nullify any incoming attacks up to two turns, up to four uses per battle. In a pinch? She possesses an AoE skill with the bonus effect of restoring a teeny bit of DP on your side.

Masters of the Ice-element. They consist of Bon Ivar Yamawaki [BIY], Seria Sakuraba [SS], Miko Tenne [MT], Yayoi Bungo [YB], Adelheid Kanzaki [AK] and Mari Satsuki [MS]

Flickers of fortunes descend from the stars. Seira's Style, Fortune Teller in the Sea of Stars provides Crit% % buffs that last for three turns. Concurrently, her DP recovery skills from her lower rarity Styles also add to her valuation.

If the Ice-elemental team is your go-to, then shopkeep Mari Satsuki's Sweet Muzzle with Bon Ivar's Ebon Knight as the attacker is an honourable mention. The former's Ice Zone from her second skill complements well with Bon Ivar's expertise in dealing Ice damage to single or multiple targets.

Dark-element enthusiasts with the most negative outbursts. It is composed of Misato Nikaido [MN], Iroha Ishii [II], Fubuki Mikoto [FM], Risa Murofushi [RM], Akari Date [AD] and Aina Mizuhara [AM].

Notably, Aina's S rank Style triumphs in the merit of her attacks that pack DEF Down and Fragile, both of which make it easier to crush enemies. However, she has some deficiencies, and that's why we had to place her in the middle of the Heaven Burns Red tier list.

Other than that, Iroha and Risa's SS Style can be considered if you need an extra pair of hands. The former is the sole dark-elemental damage dealer with party-wide ATK boosting capabilities, while the latter grants some heals and stat value buffs.

A class made up of the Ohshima sextuplet. Comprises of Ichiko [IO1], Niina [NO], Minori [MO1], Yotsuha [YO], Isuzu [IO2] and Muua [MO2]. They focus on Fire-elemental attacks and are great for buffing benched characters in battle.

They have an array of generic buffs/debuffs that are still useful outside of a Fire team. Muaa’s Euphoric Danger’s usefulness transcends boundaries thanks to the Tactical Vision buff she provides. In hindsight, facing an enemy weak against an element, she doubles that damage output.

Dark-elemental attackers ladled with Charge buff. Features Mion Yanagi [MY], Kanata Maruyama [KM], Shiki Hanamura [SH], Chiroru Matsuoka [CM], Inori Natsume [IN] and Maki Kurosawa [MK].

To oversimplify Charge, it is a special kind of buff that strengthens skills. For attackers, Inari is one of the top DPS with a bonus of passive self-charge, especially towards enemies weak against the Dark-element. Tanaka's Style shouldn't be overlooked either, as she packs a punch with self-charge too. You can rely on both to down enemies in a few hits. On the support side, Mion Yanagi's S Style is a very consistent healer that can provide a Charge buff on the side.

A hodgepodge of gaijin with the unique ability to cast skills without regard to SP count. Features Carole Reaper (CR), Yingxia Li (YL), Irene Redmayne (IR), Vritika Balakrishnan (VB), Maria de Angelis (MA) and Charlotta Skopovskaya (CS).

Yingxia is another game-breaking support unit that's out of this realm. The hit count buff she confers to a comrade is the highest (at +5) and usable regardless of how much SP she has. Aside from dealing more damage per hit, it makes it easier to fill the Overdrive Gauge.

Keep an eye out for Irene's Azure Carbuncle. She is notorious for her second skill, which cuts through "truth". In short, it deals indiscriminate 400% critical damage to any foe. Best of all, she can cast it anytime.

The upper-classmen whose sole benefit is having an extra turn. Made up of Yuina Shirakawa [YS], Monaka Tsukishiro [MT], Miya Kiryu [MK], Chie Sugawara [CS], Hisame Ogasahara [HO] and Satomi Kura [SK].

Kiryu's Style has something called Enfeeble, which makes enemies weaker for two turns, enabling your other attackers to steamroll through them more easily.

Yuina's attack-centric Styles are not all bark and no bite. She’s blessed with high hit counts for her skills and the added effect of devastation. However, using her outside a specific team (Infernal Sanctuary for Thunder and Awakening Iris for Light) will limit her prowess.

Ideally, you would want to throw your quartz at the following banners: Beginner summon - aim to score a minimum of 3 SS Memoria in one go YingXia and Seika SS Memoria banner - these two Memoria will get you set for a good year.

That's our complete Heaven Burs Red tier list. If you love comparing characters and heroes, look into our Wizardry Variants Daphne tier list and this tier list for Legend of Kingdoms.
