#4307. 8 JRPGs That Came Back From the Dead

Murillo Zerbinatto is a JRPG enthusiast, writer, and editor. He has played over 300 RPGs during his gaming career, with 90% of them being JRPGs.

It feels like we have been living through a game renaissance for quite some time. While development costs continue to inflate, particularly in the Western market, one way to keep the fanbase engaged with a developer and its IPs is to bet on smaller games, or even on ports, remasters, and remakes.

Another approach is to play on older fans' nostalgia, investing in older IPs while modernizing certain titles to attract newcomers at the same time. One genre that does this frequently is JRPGs, and as you can see in the following list, there are several JRPGs that pretty much came back from the dead, titles that had not shown their face in years and returned either as a remake or a brand new entry.

When Square Enix started with their HD-2D games, it was pure happiness. A rescue of the pixel art that the developer understands so well, but better than ever, paired with traditional gameplay. What I didn't expect, and I think nobody did, was that they would leverage this graphical engine to remake some older titles, and among these, Live A Live.

Live A Live was a JRPG released in 1994 for the Super Famicom exclusively in Japan, so imagine everyone's surprise when a modern remake was announced for 2022. Seriously, no one could have expected that. But there is a good reason, and aptly so, why Live A Live is timeless and was so well received by the modern audience 28 years after its original release.

Lunar was one of the JRPGs Game Arts released for the Sega CD, and it quickly earned a reputation as one of the finest JRPGs of the fourth generation. The first two mainline entries also quickly followed on PS1, reaching a much larger audience and becoming classic titles for the console. Portables followed, including Lunar Legend and the critically offensive Lunar Dragon Song.

In 2009, the series tried a comeback with Lunar: Silver Star Harmony, a remake of the first game for the PSP, and while critics loved it, it didn't give the franchise a second wind. Well, me, you, and our moms thought Lunar was over. But then, out of nowhere, GungHo announced Lunar Remastered Collection, a compilation of Lunar: Silver Star Story Complete and Lunar 2: Eternal Blue Complete, bringing the franchise back after 26 years without a sign of life.

Nihon Falcom is really focusing its efforts on bringing its entire lineup to modern platforms.

NISA is one of the oldest Japanese developers around, but the studio really found its footing after releasing the tactical La Pucelle: Tactics. It went on to mimic that gameplay style across several other franchises, mainly the well-known Disgaea. In 2004, it released Phantom Brave, another tactical JRPG following the same NISA blueprint, but with its own distinct identity and slightly different gameplay.

Phantom Brave was a solid game. I enjoyed it, but I really thought it was a one-and-done deal. I was pretty surprised when NISA announced Phantom Brave: The Lost Hero, not only a game set in the same universe, but a direct narrative sequel. Okay, luckily the game included a recap because releasing a sequel to a 20-year-old game was wild, but it is what it is.

I have mentioned Brigandine a few times here on the site, including in my review of Brigandine Abyss. I discovered this franchise serendipitously, and it took a long time to find other people who were also familiar with it. Truth be told, I only found them when I started frequenting the depths of Reddit. I had even forgotten about it, only to be reminded when I stumbled upon Brigandine: The Legend of Runersia.

Reviving an old IP or a cult classic happens every now and then, as you can see with other titles here. But Brigandine was not a cult hit, a classic, or even mildly famous. It was obscure among obscure titles, so why Happinet thought of bringing it back baffles me, but they did. Brigandine: The Legend of Forsena came out in 1998 and Runersia in 2020. The game apparently did well enough to warrant a new mainline entry, Brigandine Abyss, released just this year.

There are more than a few JRPGs that are still stuck on older systems and deserve a port to modern platforms.

I have always preferred fantasy games over sci-fi, but if there was one franchise where mechas stole my heart, or in this case, Wanzers, it was Front Mission. I played and replayed Front Mission 3 so many times and never grew tired of it, especially since the game featured branching narrative paths and a degree of RNG when learning skills, making every playthrough feel fresh. Then came the fourth mainline entry, Scars of War, Front Mission Evolved, and ugh, Left Alive, which come on, is not a Front Mission game, so let us dismiss it.

Well, in 2020, Forever Entertainment said it was working on a remake of an established Square Enix franchise that had multiple releases. My guess was either Parasite Eve or Front Mission, and since the former is tied up in licensing issues, yeah, it was Front Mission. The first remake launched in 2022, the second in 2023, and the third in 2025. I don't know if the franchise will continue, but it was great to revisit it through modern releases.

I know this entry is a bit far-fetched and even a tad insulting. After all, calling Valkyrie Elysium a mainline Valkyrie Profile entry is a stretch, but closing our eyes doesn't make it less true. After years without a new entry, Valkyrie Elysium was announced and left many fans excited, especially the nostalgic ones who adored the mysterious adventures of Lenneth back on the PS1.

What we got, however, wasn't what we wanted. It is not a bad game per se. It's just too middle-of-the-road and doesn't reflect what Valkyrie Profile represented, whether in the first game, Silmeria, or even Covenant of the Plume. Still, Valkyrie Elysium arrived in 2022, 13 years after the last mainline entry, so it fits the topic. I'm also not considering the mobile game Valkyrie Anatomia.

The producer is giving us hope, or at least some more coping issues.

Mana was always such a cozy, colorful, and friendly series. I loved playing Secret of Mana with my brother or transferring my character from Legend of Mana onto a memory card to bring to my friend's house. Good times. Even so, for one reason or another, it never achieved massive mainstream success. In 2007, Heroes of Mana came out for the Nintendo DS, followed in 2014 by Rise of Mana, a mobile-first game that received a Vita port. It was an oddity.

The franchise faded for a bit, but returned with the remake Adventures of Mana, followed by Secret of Mana and then Trials of Mana. The success of the remakes, especially Trials, signaled something to Square Enix, because it didn't take long for them to produce a brand-new mainline title in Visions of Mana. Personally, I loved Visions! It was a modernized version of everything I liked about Mana. I don't know why the game didn't achieve the success it deserved, but it may have been the last time we saw a mainline Mana entry.

You have probably heard someone say that Suikoden II is their favorite JRPG of all time. It was one of the most remarkable titles on the PS1 and built a deeply dedicated fanbase. Three more mainline entries later, the series began to fade into oblivion, still receiving a few spinoffs like Suikoden Tierkreis in 2009 and the Japan-only Gensō Suikoden: Tsumugareshi Hyakunen no Toki in 2012, which was its latest release. It was a strange era for both the series and Konami, which had stepped away from the video game industry for a while.

Then, completely out of nowhere, Konami announced Suikoden I & II HD Remaster: Gate Rune and Dunan Unification Wars during Tokyo Game Show 2022. It was a pleasant surprise, made even sweeter with the arrival of Suikoden Star Leap, which released in 2026. And okay, I know it is a mobile game, but those who played it (still locked in Japan) say it feels like a full-fledged Suikoden game, so who knows, maybe this will convince Konami to produce an offline version of Star Leap or a brand-new mainline entry altogether.

The GOG Dreamlist aims to preserve classic games. Here are 10 JRPGs that I would love to see on the platform, and they just need your vote.

#4305. Nioh 3’s generous demo is out now, and your progress carries over to the full game

If you’re looking for a way to check out one of the biggest releases of early 2026, Team Ninja has made it easy for you.

Nioh 3 is one of the most anticipated games of 2026, and it’s easily among the biggest releases of February. We’re a few days away from the start of that month, however, but we don’t have to wait until then to actually play Team Ninja’s next major release.

The previously announced demo has arrived, and it’s one any fan of action games should check out, especially if you missed the PlayStation-exclusive beta held last year.

Unlike previous tests, the Nioh 3 demo is available on PC and PS5, just like the main game. This is pretty new for the series, which has typically launched first on PlayStation before coming to PC months later.

The Nioh 3 demo includes a decent portion of content from the beginning of the game. It’s enough to show off the core duality mechanic, letting you switch between the Samurai and Ninja styles at will. It also includes a preview of the game’s open field level design, which makes it sit somewhere between full open world and the more linear level design of past Nioh games.

Feedback from the previous beta has been implemented into the demo (and full release), so you may see some familiar faces, as well as areas you visited before - assuming you played that one.

Another big reason why you might want to grab the Nioh 3 demo is that your progress in it will carry over to the full version. This includes the character creator, too, meaning you can spend all day perfecting your character without having to worry about missing out on playing the actual game.

The demo even supports online multiplayer for up to three players, in case you come to Nioh for co-op. If you complete the available content, you’ll earn an in-game bonus in the full version. This is something Team Ninja has done with past Nioh titles, of course.

This time, your reward is the Twin-Snake Helmet. Just make sure you complete the demo before February 15.

Nioh 3 is out February 6 on PC, and PlayStation 5.

#4304. King of Fighters AFK tier list - Get your team fighting fit

If you want to make the best team of five possible, our King of Fighters AFK tier list is on hand to guide you through those otherwise difficult choices.

After countless KOF games, one that nobody really pictured made an appearance: King of Fighters AFK. This one has a pretty similar style to that of 7DS Idle (for which we have a Seven Deadly Sins tier list and a list of Seven Deadly Sins codes), where you can collect and upgrade some of your favourite fighters from the franchise, and send a team of 5 to battle enemies.

To make this KOF tier list, I divided the fighters into two major groups: the Uniques and the Legends. The Uniques are the ones with the "UQ" tag and colour-coded yellow, while the Legends sport the "LG" tag and a red background (or card pack when summoning).

There are good and bad fighters on both sides, but until you've summoned enough to get Legends reliably, you will have to work with the Unique options.

I haven't ranked anything lower than LG or UQ, simply because it's not worth using or upgrading any of them. On the following pages, you will find the KOF AFK tier list for the Legends, and the tier list for the Uniques - let's check them out! KOF AFK best Legends  |  KOF AFK best Uniques Original article by Cristina Mesesan. Updated by Mihail Katsoris.

Firstly, Orochi Leona and Orochi Iori are just otherworldly, landing them a place at the top of our King of Fighters AFK tier list. They benefit from the Owned Effect, which in Leona's case is additional ATK to all allies, while Iori heals allies back to 100%. These two fighters also belong to the Cosmos faction, which is pretty rare.

Meanwhile, KUSANAGI is a fighter whose style approaches that of a berserker. He can stun the enemies, but he will consume some of his HP when attacking. The damage dealt is proportional to the HP consumed, so you will have to partner him with a healer. He is S+ tier because once he reaches 7*, he will also be able to recover some of that HP, which makes him a beast.

While the Uniques are not that great, in the grand scheme of things, the ones that are listed under "best" can definitely be used and upgraded in the early game. You should, of course, upgrade them all whenever you get their dupes, just don't bother levelling them all up more than necessary.

Some noteworthy options are Athena (KOF XI Style), who shouldn't be confused with the Legendary Athena KOF '98 Style, who is in a league of her own. The Unique Athena is a fighter you will get from the start, and she can deal pretty good damage while also reducing the enemy's DEF.

And with that, we come to the end of our King of Fighters tier list. We've also got a list of KOF AFK codes, so be sure to check that out for some free goodies, including Rubies, Photo Card Tokens, and Gold.

#4303. The Video Games And More You Should Play This Weekend – October 23, 2026

This week has been home to some disheartening news. BioWare, the creators of games like Mass Effect and Dragon Age, is being shut down amid a flurry of layoffs. It's another frustrating story from a struggling video game industry. Below you will find some of our stories about the legendary developer, including our massive 2016 oral history. And then after that, you can read about our recommendations of what to play this weekend.

I spent the early hours playing Final Fantasy Resonance trying to figure out precisely why I couldn't put it down. I eventually realized that the game manages in a very purposeful way to answer that quiet need I've so frequently had: "I wish I could experience a game just like Final Fantasy IV or VI again, for the first time, but with a new cast and story." That's pretty much what you can expect here; Resonance is a very purposeful throwback experience that harkens to the early days of FF pixel adventures, but with several modern conveniences, graphical flourishes, and depth added into the mix. It's a big and refreshingly wholesome journey of entertaining party members, summoning giant creatures, flying an airship across the world, and fighting turn-based battles that include absurd spell effects. It's one of my favorite games of the year, and well worth the time it will take to explore. Read our full review for more.

Expect to hear a lot of people proclaiming this as "one of the good ones," as Modern Warfare came out swinging this week with a strong campaign, compelling additions to competitive multiplayer, and an impressive extraction shooter mode in the form of DMZ. I've already been impressed by the first few hours of the campaign, which offers a tense, harrowing, and often disturbingly brutal story that bounces between a number of character perspectives. The gunplay feels tuned in, the traversal and melee is satisfying, and the narrative beats grounded in excellent actin performances. Our reviewer has spent even more time with the full game, and can share their full perspective to help inform whether you want to take a dive into this year's installment.

The Nintendo Sports franchise, which began with Wii Sports in 2006, has never been about the single-player experience. That remains true 20 years later in Nintendo Switch Sports Resort. But this time around, Nintendo has boosted the amount of content beyond what the series has typically provided, appealing to all player counts, all while retaining its trademark approachability. Whether you're joining together with three friends for some friendly competition across the package's 12 sports or you're trying to climb the Island Crown ladder by beating increasingly difficult single-player opponents, Switch Sports Resort is a great motion-controlled collection.

Halloween is around the corner. As you’re buying overpriced candy, deciding which version of the Joker to dress up as, and debating between watching Obsession and Backrooms over a cup of cider, it’s the perfect time to replay old horror games or dive into new ones. 2026 has a solid roster of choices for the latter thanks to releases like Resident Evil Requiem, Paranormasight: The Mermaid’s Curse, and Silent Hill: Townfall, but Tenebris Somnia shouldn’t be overlooked if you’re looking for a cool indie throwback.

Part retro-inspired adventure game, part live-action indie horror film, you’ll uncover the mystery of a nightmare-induced apartment building and battle horrors to rescue your trapped ex. The gameplay is survival horror 101, but it’s executed well, with consistently clever and inventive puzzle-solving as a highlight. It may not be a graphical powerhouse, but Tenebris Somnia still maintains a creepy atmosphere thanks to solid scares partly delivered by effective and well-made live-action cinematics. If you’re going to binge horror films, you may as well play one too. You can read my full review here.

Full disclosure: I have not played One Piece: Grand Gourmet. I was trying to finish up Castlevania: Belmont's Curse when a review game landed in my lap that I've had to give my full attention. That said, I have watched a lot of the One Piece anime, have a cat named Nami, and dog named Luffy.

I don't know if One Piece: Grand Gourmet is any good, but I like the premise and pixel graphics. One Piece is a very malleable franchise (which is why its live action adaptation is pretty good), so the idea of managing a restaurant as Sanji feels like it could be a very good fit. I plan on climbing aboard with all my hopes and dreams soon. And it is out now, which is good to know.

Similar to the entry above, I have not yet played Stupid Never Dies yet (there are too many video games!), but we like to use this weekly article to call out the new video games of the week. I am eager to check out Stupid Never Dies primarily because of its pop-punk soundtrack and 2000s aesthetic. I think it has the potential to be a fun, nostalgic throwback to my youth when I was learning Blink-182's "Dammit" on guitar and playing Devil May Cry.

The Blood of Dawnwalker has been out for just over seven weeks now, but I wouldn't blame you if you haven't finished it – or even started it – yet. A lot has come out! But if you need a reason to jump back in, this week's 1.1 update is a great excuse – the devs have added hundreds of bug fixes and other minor improvements, so it should run better than it ever did before. There's also an even easier difficulty mode if you want to cruise through without worrying about combat, and a new in-game potion that lets you respec all your skill points. I stalled out about halfway through (when I started playing Wolverine), but I'm planning to jump back in this weekend.

Oh, and you can pet dogs and cats now. Maybe I should have led with that.

Multiplayer physics mountain-climbing game Peak became one of the most viral co-op experiences of 2025 (I refuse to use the term friendslop), but only PC players have enjoyed its wacky shenanigans. That changed this week as Peak is now available on PS5, Xbox Series X/S, and Switch 2. Either alone or, preferably, alongside up to three friends, you’ll try to ascend procedurally generated, absurdly unrealistic mountains riddled with dangers. Working together is key, a tricky prospect thanks to the in-game proximity chat that necessitates sticking together, but griefing each other, intentionally or otherwise, is just as entertaining – maddeningly frustrating at times, but entertaining. Peak on consoles includes all post-launch content and, best of all, supports crossplay for all platforms.

The original Azul remains one of my all-time favorite games even after many years, but it just misses the bar with its strategic complexity to be one I'd pull out to play with the kids. That why I was especially delighted to find that Azul Kids is one of those rare "adapted for children" projects that turned out extremely well.

Players take on the roll of creative young artists building mosaic displays with various colored tiles. The concept remains simple enough to work for even very young players of age five or six, but the whole family should have fun with the approachable strategy implications of choosing tiles and completing your masterpiece.

#4302. d4v41 and Jinggg leave Paper Rex after 7th–8th Champions finish, Pacific place secure

Paper Rex has parted with captain d4v41 and Jinggg, two Masters Toronto winners, after an early exit at Champions 2026. With its VCT Pacific partner place secure, the Singapore organisation is rebuilding by choice as free agency opens to every region.

Paper Rex has broken up the core of its VALORANT roster. The Singapore organisation is parting with its captain and one of its best-known players as the 2027 season approaches. d4v41 had been with Paper Rex since its founding in 2020. He played first on its CS:GO roster, then moved with the team to VALORANT. Jinggg joined on 28 September 2021.

Neither player has named a destination. In the farewell video Paper Rex released, d4v41 said he was moving to a new team. Jinggg wrote on X that he was excited about what comes next. d4v41 also asked fans to keep supporting the organisation after both have gone.

The split follows a season that faded at the end. Paper Rex were runners-up at both Masters Santiago and Masters London earlier in 2026. At Champions in Shanghai, they lost 2-0 to LOUD in the upper-bracket quarter-finals on 7 October. A 2-1 defeat to T1 in lower-bracket round one ended their run on 9 October. The event carried a $2,250,000 prize pool. LOUD went on to beat Team Vitality in the final.

The pair leave with a long record together. Jinggg helped Paper Rex to second place at Masters Copenhagen 2022. He was also part of the run to the Champions 2023 final, where the team were runners-up. Liquipedia lists both players in the line-up that won VCT 2025 Masters Toronto.

The changes are not forced by the league. The organisation is owned by IMPLS Entertainment Pte Ltd. Riot has cut the number of partner teams in each region from ten to eight for 2027–28. That leaves 32 across the four regions.

The Pacific format rewards that security. The eight partners receive seeded places at Kickoff in January 2027. Four further places go to teams that come through open qualifiers. Paper Rex can therefore reshape its roster without needing to qualify.

Two Masters winners on the open market could matter well beyond the Pacific. EMEA’s eight partners for 2027 are Fnatic, BBL Esports, FUT Esports, Team Heretics, Team Liquid, Gentle Mates, Karmine Corp and Team Vitality. Under Riot’s open qualifier rules, most regions require three of a team’s five players to come from that region. Teams must also keep three of five players between events to carry their progress forward. Those limits will frame how far any club can rebuild around new signings.

Khalish has been part of Paper Rex since our founding in 2020, starting first on our CS:GO Roster and transitioning with the team to VALORANT. We'll always remember the laughs, the op shots, and every achievement through the years.

From everyone at Paper Rex, we wish @d4v41vlr… pic.twitter.com/UgWKD4QfOj

Later in November, open qualifiers get under way. The season’s first Masters event follows in February 2027.

#4301. The definitive tier list on Fruit Battlegrounds: sweet succulents, ranked

At the very top of our Fruit Battlegrounds tier list, you'll find only Mythical fruits, which is not surprising considering how hard they are to obtain

Updated on November 5th, 2026  P O P O has shaken up the Fruits Battlegrounds meta with the Magma + IceV2 update. Two more Legendary fruits have been added - they aren’t new, but they will definitely impact the gameplay and strategies. So, a new meta calls for an updated tier list.

This Fruit Battlegrounds tier list will rank all the fruits using six tiers: SS, S, A, B, C, and D. Tier SS is all about the OP ones - luckily, there are not too many of those. On the contrary, Tier S and A are full of powerhouses that can give the OP ones a good run for their money.

B tier has average entries - these just slack behind in certain aspects, but they can take the reins in some scenarios. And towards the end are tiers C and D. While the C tier isn't bad, it's not the best either. Beginners have to make do with these at the start. However, they are not worth hanging on to for too long. The same goes for tier D - once you have enough gems to buy better options, get rid of the C and D-tier picks ASAP.

And as if on cue, we have already listed all the Fruit Battleground gift codes in one place. Redeem these to get your hands on some gems for free.

Original article by Shah Zaib. Updated by Mihail Katsoris.

It should come as no surprise that the top of the Fruit Battlegrounds tier list is full of Mythicals, as they are hard to come by. But once you get any of these, hang on to them. All three are massive damage dealers and perform great in every mode.

Nika, for instance, deals massive damage, has great AoE, does burn damage, and even stuns the enemies in place. On top of all that, some of the skills can break enemy shields as well. Also known as the Sun God, Nika is the strongest pick in the game right now.

However, Dragon V2 might have taken over as the strongest if it weren’t for the recent and much-needed nerf. Still, the quick recharge, special weapon combos, and easy spam-ability make it dangerous to fight against. And in the right hands, it can blow Nika users out of the water.

One Piece fans saw Venom in action during the Marineford arc. It was one of the deadliest in the anime that nearly killed Luffy, and it’s not too different in Fruit Battlegrounds. Venom has good damage, some block-shattering moves, and a decent stun to keep the enemies down.

Much like the SS tier, the S tier is also ruled by Mythicals. But the TWO new Legendary entrants are worth highlighting, too. If you are tired of waiting for your Ice to awaken, roll and pray you get IceV2.

IceV2 is the awakened form of Ice and “unleashes the true potential of the inner Ice abilities.” Every IceV2 move freezes enemies and opens up a combo window. Despite a smaller move set, IceV2 makes it to the S tier because of its ease of use and all-around performance in every mode.

Aside from the obvious difference in powers, MagmaV2 is not all that different from IceV2. MagmaV2 also has a 5-skill moveset. It’s also the awakened form of an older one (Magma). And MagmaV2 performs equally well in Bounty Hunting as well as PvP battles. While these two new entries might seem lacklustre due to their smaller move set, they have their perks, making them a worthy challenger to some Mythical powerhouses.

Although in the same tier, Ope-Ope is far more powerful than IceV2 and MagmaV2. In fact, it might just be the strongest in the S tier. The only reason it doesn’t make the SS tier in my list is because of the limited range and the fact that certain moves are dependent on Room.

Lightning has no such problems, though. It has SEVEN skills. All of these have crazy stuns, making them easy to chain together and create combos. The only thing keeping Lightning from becoming top-tier is its high stamina consumption. Every other caveat is manageable. With FOUR base and FIVE transformed skills, you’d think Leopard is pretty strong, and you’d be right. Most of Leopard’s moves are unblockable. It transforms you into a leopard that can dish out some serious amounts of damage, regardless of the mode. The base form damage isn’t too shabby either. Leopard might just be the most well-balanced pick in Fruit Battlegrounds right now. The same as Dough, too. Dough allows you to create and manipulate dough. It might not be cool, but it’s effective and powerful. It's also very easy to create combos, and the damage output is high as well.

With the MagmaV2 + IceV2 update, the OG Magma became the only Epic with an awakened form. But that doesn’t mean the base form is no good. Used right, some of Magma’s moves can deal high initial damage and very high burn damage as well. Although it slightly struggles against fast enemies, you’ll know what to do once you level it up enough.

With its massive AoE, decent stuns, and great combo potential, Dragon has to be one of the best options for boss farming and bounty hunting. The flat learning curve and impressive damage stats make it a treat for beginners.

That said, Dragon does struggle in PvP. Flame, on the other hand, has no such problem. It allows you to generate and manipulate fire and even transform your body into fiery flames. Flame has SIX moves, all of which are spam-able, and most of them deal damage per second by burning enemies.

Quake isn’t as OP in Fruit Battlegrounds as shown in the One Piece anime, but it’s still a decent Legendary that has been here from the start. You can pull off almost all of Whitebeard’s moves with the Quake fruit, including causing a tsunami. If only its moves dealt more serious damage, though. Magnet is based on Eustass Kid’s devil fruit called the Jiki Jiki no mi. This allows players to generate magnetic forces and control metals. Most of the moves deal great damage, but at the same time, some of them are easily blockable. Plus, don’t expect to chain together too many combos.

If four out of its six moves weren't blockable and it offered a bit more mobility, Darkness would have been in a higher tier. Kurozo is an OP move, but it is blockable too. That said, Darkness can pretty much suppress every other option. And once you unlock all its moves, you will have enough mastery over it to do so.

While creating this Fruit Battlegrounds tier list, even I was surprised by the number of Legendary elements that ended up in tier B, but it is what it is. Either through nerfing or other fruits getting insane buffs, TS Rubber, Gravity, and Phoenix have fallen behind. They are not the worst options, but they are no longer worth building upon. Icks like long cooldowns, easy dodges, and lesser damage have reduced them to mere gem farmers. Just as there are some underperforming ones, some are punching above their weight.

Epics like Paw and String are great all-rounders with good damage dealing and decent range. Plus, they do well in every mode. The same goes for Light, one of the fastest. If it wasn’t for the weakness against airborne enemies, Light would easily be in tier A.

Falcon is surprisingly good for an Uncommon one, hence tier B. It has decent combo potential, flight is quick, and most attacks have multiple hit points. It's also super easy to get. There aren’t many better options to get started with in Fruit Battlegrounds than Falcon.

Similarly, Ice is also a beginner-friendly pick that’s easy to level up and deals above-average damage too. A limited skillset and poor performance against airborne enemies dents Ice’s reputation.

Using Bomb, you get the ability to generate explosions at will. While it sounds devastating, the destructive prowess is average, to say the least. All FOUR of its moves deal AoE damage.

But since most of these are charge moves, you’ll feel sluggish and always open to enemy attacks. Smoke and Gas are Uncommon fruits that are equally bad, especially Smoke. Every move Smoke will stun the user instead of stunning the enemy. Gas does have high-damage dealing, but the stamina drain is crazy. Plus, it’s one of the slowest - not good for PvP at all.

Rubber is the main character’s Devil Fruit in One Piece, but it’s one of the worst in Fruit Battlegrounds. Its move set consists of all of Luffy’s basic moves, like Bazooka and Pistol. However, they are not nearly as devastating as in the anime. The only decent move of Rubber is the Gear 2 transformation, which depletes stamina in no time.

The other three in tier C - Barrier, Chop, and Sand - are Common. With subpar damage and blockable moves, these have more weaknesses than strengths. Chop is fun, though. Flying around in pieces looks as good as it does in the anime.

And that’s our Fruit Battlegrounds tier list. As the devs introduce new or better versions of the current ones, this tier list will get updated accordingly.

We also have a Blox Fruits tier list. Although the entries might look similar, the power meta is completely different over there. So, if you ever decide to have a look at something similar-but-not-quite, check out Blox Fruits - or perhaps this Haze Piece fruit tier list that's quite fresh, if we say so ourselves!

#4299. Phantom Blade Zero Review In Progress – Shaping Up To Be One Of The Best Action Games I've Ever Played

Phantom Blade Zero is an astounding achievement for the action genre. So astounding that I feel pulled to experience everything it has to offer… and that means instead of rolling credits, I’ve been busy completing story-critical side quests and more to get the most complete ending. That’s another way of saying I am enjoying this game very, very much but still need more time to render a final verdict, which is why you’re reading a review-in-progress of Phantom Blade Zero rather than a scored piece.

Though I’m not interested in guesstimating a score right now, I know it will be high because Phantom Blade Zero impresses and then some. It is one of the best action games I’ve ever played, and I’m shocked to be writing that. This is a debut of sorts for developer S-Game, which has dabbled in mobile games and smaller-scale titles; it’s the team’s first triple-A release, and its first game of this kind. This studio is so clearly a dedicated student of the genre, analyzing what works here and what works there in other action greats to create something of its own. It looks forward at what action games can do, can play like, can look like, while looking back at the games before it and understanding why those games – games like Devil May Cry, Elden Ring, Sekiro: Shadows Die Twice, Bayonetta, and just about every other quality action game you can think of – continue to be ones we hold so highly. Should it stick the landing, Phantom Blade Zero will join that echelon of action pedigree.

Protagonist Soul is a quiet, mostly stoic martial arts master who prefers to let his blades (of which there are so, so many) do the talking. The Order he’s sworn his life to betrays him, and, in an effort to right wrongs, he discovers a villainous conspiracy to seize full power of the blood-soaked Chinese martial underground known as Wulin. As a result, puppets, secret sects, powerful god-like creatures, monstrous beasts, and much more prowl Wulin’s various biomes. I haven’t kept count, but there are a massive number of enemies to take down, both standard mob variants and bosses, and the game stays fresh throughout. It's even fresher when you consider how many weapons you can acquire on Soul’s journey.

Every weapon is wholly unique, like picking up a new character in a fighting game, each with its own moveset and abilities. Upgrading these weapons through various tiers unlocks additional abilities, and you can even Soul Temper weapons to add one final, game-changing ability or perk. A fully upgraded weapon can have a moveset that uses the majority of buttons on your controller. You can do the same with Phantom Edges, special tide-turning weapons with limited uses (before you build up additional charges). Combined with different accessories and medicine types, Phantom Blade Zero offers hundreds, perhaps thousands, of combat kit permutations. You can play as a drunken fighter who switches between sober, tipsy, and drunken states, with his range and damage output changing as a result; you can focus on a bleed build, ripping enemies to shreds with charged attacks that utilize Soul's own HP to deal extra damage (that can then be earned back with bleed); you can use lightning, wind, fire, and ice to create elemental storms against enemies, and you can use a sword that switches between different elemental states on command as well. You can also just pound enemies to pulp with Phantom Edge fists, too. I’ve struggled to stop using these fists since acquiring them because they’re so satisfying.

Forty-plus hours into Phantom Blade Zero, it feels like I’ve played as dozens of different Souls because I've discovered so many build types. S-Game smartly pushes you to try new builds and weapons as you get them, doling out generous upgrade materials and currency; it encourages you to try everything, and the next weapon might just become your new favorite.

Finding these materials (and additional fights) is great fun, too, because Phantom Blade Zero’s various open-area biomes are a genuine joy to explore. You are always rewarded for taking the optional path, and those rewards are always worthwhile. You might find a healthy pile of upgrade materials, or a boss with a weapon you’ll fall in love with. The way buildings, alleys, caves, cliffsides, and other environmental features weave in and out of each other evokes FromSoftware’s architectural design and the subsequent shortcut “aha!” moments.

That said, Phantom Blade Zero is definitively not a Soulslike, though you’d be forgiven for assuming as much given its challenging suite of bosses, interconnected world, and Phantom Bell checkpoints, which are this game’s equivalent of bonfires. However, its challenge is much more surmountable (with various difficulties and accessories to ease parry and dodge timing), and its world progression is materially different. Kill an enemy and it’s dead for good, which to my surprise, adds a sense of worldbuilding I didn’t know I wanted. Progression through this journey feels tangible because I’m actually removing traces of evil with my weapons, traces that don’t respawn when I interact with checkpoints. It’s a nice change of pace that narratively speaks to Soul’s efforts.

Along the way, countless reading materials shed light on Phantom Blade Zero’s intertwining stories, and tracking down the next memory, scroll, or book entry rewards you if you’re interested in the full picture of this Wuxia story. I’d argue the game’s story is its weakest element, but only when compared to the rest of the package. It doesn't break any new ground narratively, but it provides enough mystery and thrill to keep things moving. And while performances are great, talking to characters is still mostly just two people standing across from each other talking through a new quest. Fortunately, cutscenes pick up the slack with dramatic villains, heartfelt revelations, raw tension, and more.

Production value is high across the board, thanks to incredibly impressive animation and a beautiful rendering of this dark fantasy China. Faces are lifelike, nudging up just shy of the uncanny valley as close-ups reveal porous details, lip quivers, and more, bringing an excellent cast of Chinese performances to life. The English voice acting has its standouts, but Soul’s voice is boring, so I highly recommend the Chinese vocals.

Boss fights draw clear inspiration from Chinese cinema and boast a wondrous sense of awe and scale that only the best in the genre typically offer. There are a ton of bosses, too, with very few repeats (repeats do happen in segmented challenge trials), and it’s impressive to think back on just how many I defeated, and just how many of them delivered a unique fight. I appreciate the checkpoints between boss phases as well. There are so many bosses – nearing 100 or more if I had to guess – and having my progression saved through phases removes some of the repetition I often feel when, say, phase two of a boss continues to kill me and I have to blitz through phase one again and again before taking another stab at it.

That scale and on-screen excitement carry through almost every fight in the game, down to even the simplest mob fights, though these are starting to feel a touch repetitive as I’m barreling toward the game’s end. Soul moves like the world’s greatest martial artist, but your controller inputs make it happen. If you mash the attack button, it looks nice… but if you use each weapon’s prescribed inputs and abilities, Phantom Blade Zero delivers a level of detailed action I’ve seen in few other games. You direct the game’s action, and this lets you turn what might otherwise be just another group of fodder enemies into an electric bout of spectacle.

To say I greatly enjoy this game greatly undersells my feelings – writing this review-in-progress is frustrating because I want to get back to Phantom Blade Zero. I expect to reach credits in the coming days, so please be on the lookout for my final verdict this week.

#4298. Fragmentary Order Looks Like Sci-Fi Escape from Tarkov, And You Can Play It This Year

Covering the video games industry since 2017, with experience in news, articles, and reviews. Currently a writer at DualShockers and gaming magazines.

If you've ever wondered what Escape from Tarkov would look like if its brutal firefights took place somewhere beyond Earth, Nikita Buyanov might have just the answer. The game director behind the popular hardcore shooter has finally offered a proper look at his next project, and it seems he's not planning to make things any easier for players.

Called Fragmentary Order, the upcoming sci-fi tactical shooter just received its first gameplay reveal, featuring an impressive 14 minutes of in-engine footage. And if you're curious to see what Buyanov has been working on, you can watch the full gameplay reveal on YouTube!

Escape From Tarkov's creator reveals that his upcoming game is 'almost there.'

Set across the Solar System in 2251, Fragmentary Order imagines a future where warfare has become an outsourced business. So, instead of putting their own lives on the line, players control remotely operated clones known as RepEnts, which are deployed across large combat zones to carry out all sorts of dangerous missions.

Interestingly, losing one of these clones isn't necessarily the end of the road. In this world, death is simply another business expense, but that doesn't mean players can afford to be careless. The game features large-scale environments, changing environmental conditions, vehicles, drones, and advanced technological systems, with squads of up to four players expected to coordinate their operations.

If you've ever wondered what Escape from Tarkov would look like if its brutal firefights took place somewhere beyond Earth, Nikita Buyanov might have just the answer.

Buyanov is also taking a more grounded approach to its sci-fi setting (as you should expect from the same mind that created Escape From Tarkov). Rather than relying on futuristic gimmicks like wall-hacks, the upcoming hardcore shooter features electromagnetic sensors that can expose players' positions, meaning every encounter requires careful planning and an understanding of the battlefield. In other words, running around without thinking twice probably won't get you very far!

Battlestate Games boss Nikita Buyanov opens up about his creative vision for his upcoming game, Fragmentary Order.

Alongside the gameplay reveal, Buyanov also announced “Prime Batch”, a paid program that gives players access to the game's upcoming closed testing sessions. So yes, some dedicated fans won't have to wait until the game's full release to get their hands on it, as closed testing sessions are expected to begin later this year.

There are two available tiers: Candidate ($44.99), which includes access to alpha sessions and major technical playtests, and Founder ($79.99), which adds earlier access to experimental builds, roadmap updates, and a private community with direct developer access. The first closed alpha wave is planned for later this year, and you can check out more about it on this page.

For now, Fragmentary Order doesn't have a confirmed release date, but its first gameplay showcase has certainly given fans plenty to discuss. If Buyanov manages to capture the same long-term appeal that made Escape from Tarkov so popular while introducing a compelling sci-fi setting, his next project could be one worth keeping an eye on.

Fragmentary Order is a next-generation multiplayer combat tactical simulator.

Sucker Punch, the team behind Ghost of Yōtei, Ghost of Tsushima, Infamous, and Sly Cooper, has been hit with layoffs, according to a report by Aftermath. The outlet states that 26 roles have been affected as the studio prepares its next project.

This game has over 4000 characters. New players will get intimidated by it, and that's why there's a great need for this One Piece Treasure Cruise tier list.

Updated on November 5th, 2026 - Version: 16.2.2 - Added: St. Sommers - Shepherd Family Holy Knight, St. Killingham - Rimoshifu Family Holy Knight, Saintess Gunko (Imu Possessed)

One Piece Treasure Cruise is a mobile RPG that’s been going strong since 2014, and has been constantly updated with the new characters added to the Straw Hat Pirates since. But, with such a massive roster, picking the wheat from the chaff can be difficult, so we’ve done our research and compiled our One Piece Treasure Cruise tier list, ranking the different crewmates and captains!

For this One Piece Treasure Cruise tier list, we’re going to come at it from the angle of characters with the most potency, the best synergy and evolutions, not all of them! To keep things at least somewhat feasible, we’ll name the characters in general - assume that this covers their evolutions and unique variants as well. So a character with one very good variant may not be ranked high, even if their one variant is extremely good, but won’t rank bottom based on their lacklustre variants either.

Essentially, we’re grading on average with each tier set out in no particular order, so don't worry if your favourite is the bottom of S tier because they're still S tier. Anyway, without further ado, let’s set sail!

It shouldn’t be surprising that the Straw Hat Pirates and their close allies are mainly at the very top of the One Piece Treasure Cruise tier list. Given the iconic nature of the series, Luffy, Nami, Zoro, and the others are constantly receiving new variations.

Not only that, but the fact that the crew is canonically so close means that the synergy behind their different slot types (STR, INT, and PSY) is incredible, so if you want a simple and effective set of characters to shoot for, the Straw Hats are a great choice.

Not only that, but since you acquire Luffy and the others to begin with, evolving them - and in some cases needing them for story progress - is basically your default progression path anyway.

As for Gol D. Roger - he’s the king of the pirates, where else do you expect him to go? Right, in all seriousness his abilities of his default variation - causing true damage and ignoring any effects to the contrary - has earned many cries of OP, congruent with his rarity.

A tier is where you’ll find a large number of characters; One Piece boasts a massive cast, and many of them are fan favourites who are well-represented in Treasure Cruise.

The Admirals in particular boast a vast variety of evolutions and variant cards, while the famous pirates (Shanks, Mihawk, and Buggy) outside the central Straw Hat crew boast unique cards and evolutions too.

If you want to move outside the comfortable familiarity of the Straw Hat Crew then exploring the options these characters open up is a great pick.

Characters relegated to this tier either have convoluted evolution paths, or simply not straightforward ones and lacklustre lower-rarity cards.

Coby and Helmeppo top this list, as despite having interesting career paths in the series - going from background characters with the more cartoonish designs seen earlier in the series to genuinely capable fighters on their own - their evolution paths only go up once.

They still have strong variants, but not necessarily as easily acquired, or worthwhile on their own, as upper-tier characters.

This tier is where you’ll find characters that are named and are useful if you pull them, but can be superseded by better characters or are only useful in certain circumstances. They’re still useful in areas like the early and mid-game and are well worth using, although they aren’t exactly exciting to pull.

Nevertheless, they’re not instant sales, and if you’re interested in gathering as many named characters as possible, it’s more than worth knowing that these are available for completion's sake. It’s also strangely fitting for Usopp that his absentee father only has a single variant in Treasure Cruise, even compared to other Red-Hair pirates like Roux.

Characters in this tier are somewhat more useful than the ones relegated to the E tier. They’re still likely not going to be a lynchpin or even journeymen characters you use for any significant length of time, but they’re not immediate sells and can be useful in special circumstances or are needed for story missions.

Note: Characters in italics are part of a series - for example; there are different variations of the navy ensign with damage types, but they all fall under the same ranking. The Mr-series are individual agents of Baroque Works, and have their own independent variations but fall under the same category for the purpose of brevity.

Characters at the bottom of our One Piece Treasure Cruise tier list are, to use the nomenclature of fandom, “trash”. These are functionally useless with next to no levelling potential and are simply there to fill out rosters and provide synergy before you get a named character that can then be used for that space in your crew, if that. Advice is to sell, sell, sell, as these characters can’t even be used for evolutions.

Generally, any generic tier character that’s part of a series is useless except if you’re just starting out, although even then, you’re likely to roll at least one much better character before you leave the tutorial.

This includes lower-tier generic characters, but as you can see in the next tier up, there are generic characters that have utility. However, characters in this tier are rarely, if ever, needed even for story missions. Generally, many animal characters that aren’t named fall under this category too.

Note, the world nobles, the Saints, have an extremely high sell value compared to the usual fodder. So they can be an easy way to big money.

Of course not every character in One Piece Treasure Cruise fights solo. Many of them are paired up into a single character. These are especially useful since you can switch once per turn between characters with different abilities, and special abilities when they switch to boot. Here are a few you can shoot for, naturally Luffy’s got more than a few partner variants… Characters Luffy & Law - Those Who Destroy the Facade of Peace, Luffy & Ace - High Seas' Pirate Luffy & Law - Miracle-Making Generation, Kizaru & Fujitora - Admirals After the Diva Shanks & Buggy - The Same Old

While 4000 characters sounds impressive, a significant portion can be discarded from our ranking. In this case, the evolution and booster characters, such as the Crabs, Penguins, and Pigs. These characters are acquired solely to use for evolving your other characters or boosting their level, and won’t factor into any team build. However, it’s worth looking these up regardless to gauge their rarity, what they’ll contribute if used for evolution and whatnot - so you know whether to save them, there are numerous fan resources that list elements such as the materials you can use for certain evolutions so you don’t miss out on a preferred character.

Fortunately, with almost ten years of development and fandom growth under its belt (makes you feel old doesn’t it?) One Piece Treasure Cruise has a wealth (pun intended) of resources available. Check out sites like the One Piece Treasure Cruise wiki for a comprehensive overview of the currently available characters and notes on their utility.

Also, with our One Piece Treasure Cruise tier list in mind, remember that with many gacha games, older characters are likely to drop in usage as you get to higher-tier content or newer content. Meanwhile, characters which will likely be lacklustre in a few years still have their niche. So give newer characters a chance if you don’t find their placement on this list agreeable.

Naturally, since these are fan resources, we can’t guarantee they’ll always be correct, but given the mind-bogglingly huge variety of things to do in the game, they’re a great place to get started.

Fans of similar games will be pleased to know that we have a tier list for Sea of Conquest, and a Reverse 1999 tier list where every girl has her place.

#4295. Infinity Nikki ushers in the Year of the Horse with... a deer-themed Version 2.2

Chromatic Beings Everbright, the latest major Infinity Nikki update, has arrived, bringing Chinese New Year celebrations vibe to the game.

Infinity Nikki, the free-to-play, open-world dress-up RPG, has delivered yet another big content drop in the form of Chromatic Beings Everbright. The latest update brings the game up to version 2.2, and introduces a new narrative chapter, and gameplay taking place around a festival narrative.

If you couldn’t guess already, the new theme is Bloom Festival, inspired by Chinese New Year celebrations.

The big new story chapter takes place in the Infinity Nikki’s Wanxiang Realm. This deceptively serene and blissful region hides a dark secret, however. Chromafaces, the mythical inhabitants of the realm, have to embody fixed identities that dictate how they live and work.

These are doled out through Character Tokens, which are used to assign roles to each individual. The story follows Nikki as she uncovers the script that runs the realm and the facade it props up. Nikki will help free Chromafaces and dispel the illusion.

The Wanxiang Realm is split into three areas. Cai Ye is your typical lantern-lit district, where festivals and fireworks happen. Kongming Gorge is almost the opposite of that; a quiet and cold place. Finally, Jiuhua Pavilion literally floats above the region, and it's home to neverending music and dance.

The other big addition in 2.2 are the two new 5-Star Resonance Outfits with some interesting gameplay implications. Where Wanxiang Weaves Life is inspired by wuxia aesthetics, and true to its inspirations, it lets Nikki shapeshift into different Spirit Personas - and automatically collect resources in her vicinity.

Chroma's Mortal Heart, on the other hand, allows Nikki to fly around the Wanxiang Realm, drawing on the power of the Celestial Deer. This outfit also uses Celestial Deer Vision to automatically ping and mark treasure chests around her.

You can also look forward to Nefarious Shadows, a new Ability Outfit, which lets Nikki see through disguises, and reveals hidden paths in the world.

As with every major update, of course, there are themed activities and limited-time events throughout. Hotpot House is a cooking minigame where you attempt to run the eponymous restaurant, whereas Flavor Frenzy is series of platforming challenges that tasks you with gathering ingredients. Fortune Mahjong is a little more straightforward, with support for solo and multiplayer play.

If you’re jumping back into the game soon, be sure to hit up our Infinity Nikki codes page for some freebies.

#4294. Grammy Award-Winning Composer Austin Wintory Shares His Early Musical Drafts Intended For Mass Effect 5

Last week, EA shut down Mass Effect and Dragon Age developer BioWare, which resulted in the cancellation of the fifth Mass Effect game that was announced in 2020. As the fallout from this closure settles, famed video game composer Austin Wintory has shared that he'd been working on a potential soundtrack for the now-canceled game and has publicly released early versions of this score.

In a Bluesky thread, Wintory, who has composed soundtracks for games such as Journey, Sword of the Sea (for which he won a Grammy), Assassin’s Creed: Syndicate, and The Banner Saga trilogy, writes, “Mass Effect was my ultimate white whale, my all-time dream project. For the last couple years I'd been in discussion w/ BioWare & EA to take on the project & as part of that I wrote close to 20 minutes of music to explore where the franchise can go next, may as well share it!"

Wintory uploaded a 20-minute video consisting of eight tracks to his YouTube channel. The video begins with a message further elaborating on the partnership between BioWare, EA, and him. “For the past several years, I’d been in dialogue with people both at BioWare and EA to potentially jump into Mass Effect 5. As part of these conversations, I decided to surprise the team by writing/recording a gigantic love letter to the franchise, with my idea of where it can go next.”

Wintory adds that he composed the music in 2025 and that he “knew nothing” about what Mass Effect 5's story entailed when he did. As such, he describes the music as “narratively speculative.” He adds that this conceptual soundtrack was a direct homage to Jack Wall and Sam Hulick’s soundtrack on the first Mass Effect “while leaning even harder on true analog synths, and a more complex integration of the orchestra (almost akin to the hybrid nature of The Matrix),” he writes. Each music track features a message by Wintory explaining his inspiration for its production.

“Receiving the news alongside everyone else that EA had decided to not only cancel the project but shutdown BioWare entirely was a deeply felt loss," Wintory writes in the video's description. "It's been hard to see dear friends lose their jobs, and this beloved franchise seemingly vanish forever. Thank you nonetheless to everyone at BioWare and EA's music department for gifting me the chance to dream in your sandbox. It was a privilege to do even that much.”

Wintory's music is the latest piece of potential Mass Effect 5 content to emerge since BioWare’s closure. A day after the shutdown announcement, an unreleased but reportedly legitimate cinematic trailer for the canceled Mass Effect leaked online.

In the late game, it will be a little tougher, but if you give it enough time and do all of your dailies (and everything else you can), you will get enough heroes - maybe even some of the best heroes in Legend of Kingdoms. Who knows?

#4292. TYLOO’s Lisbon forfeit dents Singapore Major hopes as 100 Thieves edge out fnatic

TYLOO's withdrawal from a HyperX Retake Season 13 quarter-final in Lisbon has left their PGL Major Singapore invite in doubt on cutoff day. In Europe, fnatic are shut out of the last CS2 Major of 2026 after the final weekend's results went against them.

One walkover in Lisbon looks set to decide Asia’s line-up for the PGL Major Singapore.

Neither TYLOO nor Lynn Vision is expected to play again before the cutoff. That leaves the Asian race effectively over.

The Lisbon event was a Valve Tier 2 tournament run by Hyped and PEW PEW. It ran from 29 October to 1 November with 13 teams and a prize pool of €12,187.50. Groups were GSL-format best-of-threes, followed by single-elimination best-of-three playoffs. TYLOO are listed in joint fifth to eighth place.

IEM Beijing is a far bigger draw on paper. ESL is staging it from 2 to 8 November at the Bloomage Biotech Biohyalux ECM Arena. It is S-Tier and Valve Tier 1, with 16 teams playing for $1,250,000.

TYLOO were not alone in stepping away from Lisbon. Natus Vincere also withdrew, and the organisers cited the same Beijing commitment for both teams. For NAVI, the withdrawal leaves their Major chances unchanged. They had until 19 October to pull out, but were still registered after that deadline. The Lisbon event overlapped with PGL Masters Bucharest and finished less than a day before IEM Beijing began.

After the win over 9z, the team’s points already looked sufficient, according to TYLOO coach WeiJie ‘zhokiNg’ Zhong. By that stage, they had no choice but to play the Retake event. Before IEM Beijing, he also spoke about Dongkai ‘Jee’ Ji’s recovery and the problems the team has faced this season.

Europe holds 18 of the 32 Singapore invitations, one more than it had at Cologne. The six highest-ranked eligible European teams in the 2 November standings go straight into Stage 3.

The fight for the final European spot went to the last weekend. 100 Thieves beat Wildcard 2-0 in Sunday’s FiRe Last Chance final, and the European VRS now places them 18th. Elsewhere, HOTU finished second at GLuck Moscow Cyber Games.

That was bad news for fnatic. Before the final, they sat 18th in Europe with no matches left. Their only route in was a 100 Thieves defeat and recalculated standings falling their way. Neither happened.

Zenless Zone Zero’s latest Special Program has delivered a tonne of information about the game’s big upcoming update, Version 2.6. This latest addition kicks off celebrations in New Eridu, and it’s dubbed Encore for an Old Dream.

Version 2.6 is not far off, either, arriving in ZZZ on February 6 - exactly one week from today. Encore for an Old Dream is something of an in-between story that takes place after the end of Season 2.

The narrative of 2.6 sees the Proxies’ return to Sixth Street for New Eridu's annual Gilded Carrot Day. At the centre of the celebrations is the debut of idol group Angels of Delusion at the 404 Error music venue, but not all is as it seems.

The story follows the Proxies getting invited backstage to support the group, which also includes helping them set up practice schedules, organise events and manage social media activities. There’s a rhythm minigame as part of that, along with new maps and mechanics for Marcel Adventure.

Angels of Delusion is also the group that the two new Agents being introduced in this update belong to. Members of the same group are capable of performing coordinated attacks. The new arrivals are Sunna and Aria.

Sunna is a an S-Rank Physical Support Agent who specialises in boosting teammates using Attack and Anomaly. Her Ultimate sees her pull out a giant hammer to land heavy damage, and bring teammates into combat using Quick Assist. Sunna’s companion, Bubblegum, can cast Cat's Gaze on enemies, marking them for detonation. Bubblegum can also buff the squad’s attack.

Aria is the other new arrival, the group’s lead vocalist who can shift between two forms, idol projection and construct. Aria is an Ether Anomaly Agent who also deals high burst damage, specifically against enemies who suffer from any Attribute Anomalies.

Sunna and Aria also benefit from the support of the amusingly named Bangboo Biggest Fan, a fan club president who can heal them over time, and boost the squad’s Attack any time two or more Angels of Delusion members are present.

Version 2.6’s S-Rank re-runs are Yixuan (Auric Ink - Rupture), and Yuzuha (Physical - Support), who you can look forward to as part of the banners.

Version 2.6 will also expand Hollow Zero with a new game mode, Operation Matrix. The mode offers themed stages that rotate weekly, each offering new mechanics. You can now also Sweep in Hollow Zero.

Beyond all the celebrations, this update also brings combat kit overhauls to a couple of older S-Rank characters, Lycaon and Harumasa. You can look forward to multiple limited-time events, too, including one where you can earn a new outfit for Pan Yinhu.

The big event is naturally going to be themed around Gilded Carrot Day, and it actually starts today. There’s the usual run of login rewards (about 3,300 Polychromes), as well as daily activities. Yet another login event - Gilded Surprise, Wonderful Boo-ns - will be available February 14-23, offering daily draws from a pool of 4 billion Polychrome.

#4290. Free-To-Play MOBA Pokémon Unite Is Shutting Down In March

The free-to-play MOBA Pokémon Unite will shut down in March, over five years after its 2021 launch. Although a gradual suspension of services begins today, fans will enjoy one last hurrah thanks to a big in-game event running for the remainder of the game’s lifecycle.

Launched in July 2021 for Switch before migrating to iOS and Android later that year, Pokémon Unite was billed as a friendlier take on the MOBA genre popularized by Dota 2 and League of Legends, thanks to its short matches (10 minutes) and simplified mechanics. Despite its initial popularity, the game is winding down and will go offline for good on March 23, 2027.

An End of Service notice on the game’s website reads,

“We offer our sincerest gratitude to the many Trainers who have played since service started for the Nintendo Switch version on July 21, 2021. We would like to express our thanks to everyone by holding a special event until service ends. The Pokémon Unite Aeos Crown 2027 Tokyo competitive tournament (an event for Pokémon Unite only) will also be held as previously announced. We hope you continue to enjoy Pokémon Unite until the final day of service. After service ends, the 'Pokémon Unite Game Content Guidelines for Online Platforms' will no longer be published or maintained, and we will no longer provide support regarding use of Pokémon Unite videos and images.”

As of today, in-game sales of Aeos gems and Unite Club memberships/renewals have been suspended. Existing Unite Club members will continue to use their benefits until the end of the membership period.

On November 12, an update will kick off the aforementioned final special event, where players can obtain items such as all Unite licenses and Holoware that have appeared in the game up to that point. A library feature will also be added, letting players view certain records and in-game content even after the game shuts down on March 23. Those who don’t download the library feature before the shutdown date will not be able to get it afterward.

Qualifiers for the Aeos Crown 2027 Tokyo Competitive tournament will take place as planned on December 5. After the game shuts down on March 23, players won't be able to log in to Pokémon Unite or play any battles. Only the library feature will remain accessible.

We enjoyed Pokémon Unite when it launched, with executive video editor Alex Van Aken scoring it an 8 out of 10 in his review, writing, “The game eats away the hours of my day as I reassuringly say to myself, 'Just one more match.' Battles play out with the spectacle that the Pokémon series is known for, and with so many abilities to choose from, no match feels the same as the last. The game’s simple mechanics and recognizable characters make for an approachable MOBA experience, and with a potential catalog of nearly 900 Pokémon to pick from, my hopes are high for the future of Pokémon Unite.”

#4289. Epic Adds Features to Fortnite Crew Subscription, Removes Others

Daniel is a lifelong gamer with a love for various genres and gameplay styles who enjoys exploring games and playing from various angles.

Fortnite’s self-perpetuating freemium economy is built around several forms of transactions and subscriptions. The most prominent of these are the Item Shop, where you buy cosmetics piecemeal for V-Bucks, and the Battle Pass, which you buy once per season to gain access to a set sequence of unlockables by leveling up.

In addition to these, though, Fortnite also offers the Fortnite Crew subscription service which, for a recurring monthly fee, gets you access to the current Battle Pass, other content passes like the OG Pass, Music Pass, and for fans of video game LEGO kits, the LEGO Pass, plus a monthly payout of 800 V-Bucks. It costs more than the Battle Pass by itself, but all the extra content is very attractive, especially if you don’t already have a bunch of skins to flip through.

During the Treasure Hunters event, players have a chance to uncover a token that gives near-unfettered access to the item shop for two weeks.

As Epic Games announced on the official Fortnite news blog today, though, some changes are coming to the Crew Subscription starting on December 5. Some of these changes are additive, and may help to improve the value of the subscription gameplay-wise, but they’re accompanied by some subtractions, which could harm the overall bang-for-buck depending on your perspective.

Let’s start with the good news. Firstly, the price of Fortnite Crew is staying the same at $11.99 monthly, and you’ll still get access to the current Battle Pass, Music Pass, LEGO Pass and Rocket Pass Premium.

The price of Fortnite Crew is staying the same at $11.99 monthly.

The people gave Sweeney and Epic all the attention and support it needed when it rose up to Apple. As a reward, players got a significant price hike.

In addition, all Crew members will begin receiving a flat 20% bonus to all XP earned while playing the game, with a 10% XP bonus also given to any squad members in your party, even if they’re not Crew members themselves. These boosts don’t stack, though, so you won’t get any additional XP even if you have other Crew members in your squad.

So, that’s the good news, now what’s the bad news? The first piece of bad news is that Crew Pack Outfits, one of the most distinctive benefits to getting a Crew sub, are being discontinued. The final Crew Pack Outfit will be distributed in December, with no further packs to follow. On the bright side, if there were any Legacy Styles you didn’t have for your Crew Pack Outfits, which would normally be obtained by staying subbed for sequential months, they’ll instead just be given to you in bulk.

The second piece of bad news is that, at least for the time being, OG Pass is ending, with an apparent “dramatic conclusion” occurring on December 5 with the end of Chapter 1: OG Season X. This means you won’t be able to redeem the large quantity of skins and other assorted cosmetics that this pass would normally provide.

That’s definitely a big blow to the overall value factor of a Crew subscription, though according to Epic’s news post, “The Next Era of Fortnite OG drops in late 2027,” so perhaps the OG Pass will make a comeback at some point.

Epic Games has laid off over 1,000 employees and cut three game modes from Fortnite, raising questions about the company's (and Fortnite's) future.

Nintendo has announced that a new Indie World presentation will air tomorrow, October 28. The event will run for roughly 15 minutes.

Kicking off at 7 a.m. PT/10 a.m. ET on Nintendo's YouTube channel, the presentation will spotlight upcoming indie games and related updates coming to Switch 2 and Switch. The announcement does not specify any updates. In terms of games showcased in the previous Indie World from March that have yet to release, we could get updates on Drinkbox Studios' Blighted and the murder mystery farming sim Grave Seasons, both of which were recently delayed to 2027.  Other notable indies coming to Switch platforms that could appear include The Eternal Life of Goldman, Witchbrook, Hoa 2, Human Fall Flat 2, and SacriFire.

However, in a presentation once defined by cries for Hollow Knight: Silksong, which launched last year, fans are now waiting for the game’s previously announced free expansion, Sea of Sorrow, which is slated to arrive this year. #4286. Starsand Island is a life and farming sim that isn't gacha, and it's out next week

Starsand Island officially has an Early Access release date, and it sounds like it won't stay there for years.

Though it may seem like we just had a big life sim release in Heartopia, 2026 actually has more than one highly-anticipated release in that particular subgenre of cozy game. The next big one on the horizon is Starsand Island, the life and farming sim from Seed Sparkle Lab.

The game has been gaining momentum since the launch of a demo in October last year, but the developer never quite managed to commit to a date for its debut title. Until now.

Seed Sparkle Lab announced today that Starsand Island will enter Early Access on February 11, which is only a bit over one week from now. This goes for Steam and the Xbox Preview Program version.

The developer said to expect a fairly short Early Access run, as the full launch is expected in the summer of this year. When the full release arrives, the game will also make the jump to PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series, as well as Switch 2.

The full release is also expected to bring Steam Deck support and introduce the multiplayer mode, which will not be available during Early Access

Starsand Island has something of a unique look compared to other games in the subgenre. The storybook, anime-inspired aesthetics are popular in the realm of gacha games, of course. However, seeing as this particular game isn’t gacha, being a premium product means it’s going to offer something free-to-play games aren’t designed to.

Speaking of which, the game will be available in two editions: Standard and Deluxe, with the latter including Romanticism-inspired outfits, furniture, and other customisation items. If you buy either during launch, you’ll also get a Chinese New Year bonus with even more outfits and furniture.

On top of the usual systems of farming, mining, and making friends with adorable characters (and animals), the game also has combat that pits you against ancient guardians. You can, of course, also build a home in it, and decorate it to your heart's content.

Seed Sparkle Lab says you can expect about 100 hours of content in the Early Access launch build, and more features will arrive over the course of the next six or so months, including a crossover event with My Time At Portia.

You can look forward to more Starsand Island coverage from us in the near future. Until then, you can get started by planning who you’re going to date now.

#4285. God of War: Laufey has Been Delayed for Additional Polishing

Michael Manning (He/Him) has been enamored with video games since he first played the Sonic Classic Collection as a child. With decades of experience in gaming and a full tour as a Gaming Journalist, Michael is ready to step up to the plate. From AAA to the smallest passion projects, his motto is that every piece of ar

February 2027 is set to be a massive release window, with remakes and new releases of all kinds of major series hitting one after another. Because of this, a few titles have pushed their release dates back, opting instead to give February releases their time and allowing gamers' wallets a bit of time to recover.

Wuthering Waves is one of the biggest Gachas on the planet, and they do far better than most at answering player complaints. Let's go over exactly how!

Santa Monica Studio joins the teams leaning away from February 2027, as the previously planned God of War: Laufey has been delayed to May 20th, 2027. With how important Laufey’s individual performance needs to be, Santa Monica Studio is making the most of the time they have, refusing to fall for the age-old pull of rushing release in order to present the best game possible.

Santa Monica Studio is easily one of the most prestigious teams under Sony, releasing banger after banger with the God of War series. Coming off the announcement of remakes of the original trilogy, Santa Monica revealed a major gamble with God of War Laufey, the first title in the franchise without Kratos as the central playable character.

The game focuses on Kratos’ wife and Atreus’s mother, Laufey, one of the last Norse giants present in the new God of War’s setting. Trapped within a mystical realm of the afterlife, Laufey seems to be taking major notes from the PS2/PS3 God of War titles, pitting its protagonist against a truly magical set of foes with only one way out.

After some of the more grounded presentation and general combat of the last two God of War titles, Laufey seems like a perfect return to form, one that the team is making sure hits as hard as possible. The release date change is disappointing for eager fans, but it does wonders to dodge some other heavy hitters dropping in February.

If Laufey stuck to its original release plan, the game would be battling titans like Fable, Persona 4 Revival, and Metro 2039, all major releases gamers are setting aside cash and time for. Not that God of War Laufey wouldn’t be able to hang, but it's worth taking a step back if the team could afford to.

Being one of Sony’s flagship studios doesn’t mean that Santa Monica is free of danger, if their recent treatment of Suckerpunch is any indication, but ensuring a good release is best both for the team and the consumers. Laufey doesn’t have the immediate pull for long-time players who haven’t kept up with the new God of War titles, so it needs to stand on its own as strongly as possible.

Santa Monica is a team known for absolute polish, and their refusal to be rushed is a great sign that maintaining this quality is a top priority. Too many games have been released in recent years only to be cannibalized by post-launch patches that add functions that should already be there, a mistake Santa Monica Studio is being careful to avoid.

After some of the more grounded presentation and general combat of the last two God of War titles, Laufey seems like a perfect return to form, one that the team is making sure hits as hard as possible.

May is also a much cushier release month in terms of competing releases, with no major drops ready to clash with God of War Laufey’s acclaim. The new title by Santa Monica Studio may feel like a spinoff meant to buy time, but the opportunity to learn more about Laufey, such an impactful character in the new God of War series, is incredibly exciting for any fans of that saga.

Finally getting her side of the story is a phenomenal way of closing the saga for now, allowing Kratos to rest on his laurels while expanding the wildly fantastical side of not only the Norse saga, but the entire worldwide mythos of God of War.

Vlad Dracula is a Champion and Infantry hero. He has the Vampiric Essence ability, which essentially summons bats to bleed enemies and leech their life. For each instance of damage he does to enemies, he will regen a percentage of it.

With Robin Hood, you might want some additional support that reduces the enemy DEF, since Robin Hood's Sherwood's Vengeance ability will also inflict a burn, dealing additional damage over time. I'd recommend having a good tank to hold the front line until his burn takes effect..

Albert Einstein is a Genius and Siege hero. With his Everything is Relative ability, he can summon a black hole that moves around the battlefield, continuously dealing damage to enemies. He is one of the best Siege heroes you could possibly summon, and that's how he's earned a spot at the top of this Heroes of History tier list.

He is an absolute beast in terms of heroes, and once you get him to Awaken IV, his ATK will greatly increase. At Awaken V, he will cast the ability much more often, but that is not easy to achieve.
