#4283. Jordan Esports Federation signs MoU with King Hussein Business Park to host more events

Priya Venkatesh has been following the money in esports since before brand deals were considered legitimate marketing. She got pulled into the scene through competitive fighting games and eventually found herself more interested in the contracts and partnerships behind the tournaments than the matches themselves. These days she focuses on how brands navigate esports sponsorships, where the smart money is going, and which deals are actually built to last versus the ones that look good in a press release.

The Jordan Esports Federation (JEF) has signed a memorandum of understanding with King Hussein Business Park (KHBP) in Amman, giving the national body a formal framework to stage more tournaments and events at the site it already calls home.

KHBP announced the deal on Sunday in a statement published on its website. Prince Omar bin Faisal, who is President of the JEF, attended the signing.

Under the MoU, the federation and the business park will jointly host and organise specialised competitions on the KHBP campus. They will also receive the international delegations and official guests that travel to those events. Beyond the competitive side, the two organisations plan to cooperate on media and marketing, look at shared education, training and community projects, and swap knowledge and expertise.

Neither party has disclosed financial terms or the length of the agreement.

KHBP CEO Eng. Ammar Ezzeddin presented the MoU as part of the park’s wider ambitions. “This partnership builds on our ongoing efforts to create an enabling environment for institutions, initiatives and high-potential sectors, and to establish KHBP as a hub for innovation and technology,” he said.

He added: “We look forward to helping the sector thrive and to hosting more tournaments and events that put Jordanian talent in the spotlight and raise the Kingdom’s profile in this field.”

JEF Vice President Hazem Bawab focused on the competitive and grassroots goals. “This partnership is a significant step in our drive to develop the esports industry in Jordan and elevate the standard of local, regional and international competitions and activities,” he said.

Bawab continued: “We look forward to drawing on the setup and capabilities that KHBP offers to scale our work, nurture young talent and launch joint programmes that help the industry grow and encourage greater participation.”

The deal formalises a relationship that already exists on the ground. According to The Esports Radar, the JEF, which is the government recognised regulator for esports in the country, is based at the park in West Amman.

A lot of that work happens at THE ARC, the arena and gaming dome inside the park. The same report lists past events there including the fourth Arab Esports League, a Women’s Esports Championship and Red Bull Login, which doubled as Jordan’s national final stage in Dota 2 and Counter-Strike 2. The venue is also an incubation centre supported by the federation and the Ministry of Digital Economy and Entrepreneurship, and runs training camps for players hoping to turn professional.

KHBP has been a destination for esports investment for some time. In 2024, lounge operator True Gamers announced plans for an esports venue in Jordan at the business park, a project in which its CPO publicly thanked the JEF and Prince Omar.

The timing also puts Amman in the industry spotlight. PocketGamer.biz points out that Pocket Gamer Connects Jordan takes place on 7 and 8 November, bringing many of the region’s games industry stakeholders to the city later this week.

#4282. Phantom Blade Zero Review – Wuxia Wonder Abounds

Rooted in Wuxian storytelling and scale, built on an impressively detailed combat system, and wrapped in a bloody Chinese martial underground that’s a genuine joy to play in, Phantom Blade Zero is a feat. It joins an echelon of action pedigree that includes Sekiro, Devil May Cry, Bayonetta, and just about any other action game you hold in high regard. It hails from developer S-Game, which has dabbled in mobile and smaller-scale games, and I’m shocked by what it’s pulled off with its triple-A action inauguration. But make no mistake: though Phantom Blade Zero is this team’s first crack at a game like this, it is an incredibly confident, strong debut.

Protagonist Soul is a stoic martial arts master betrayed by the Order he’s sworn his life to; he dies and returns to life with only 66 days to live. That’s enough time to settle his debts, repay his betrayers, and end a villainous conspiracy to seize full power of the Wulin realm. This narrative is Phantom Blade Zero's weakest link, but its premise adds enough mystery and tension to keep this Wuxian journey exciting through to its final, realm-shattering moments. Narrative bombshells drop not just through the game’s general fantasy-realism art direction, but also through anime scenes, opera puppet shows, animated brushstroke sequences, and more, highlighting Chinese culture and its integral place in Phantom Blade Zero.

The game features a staggering number of unique enemy types, and though the final hours get a bit repetitive, it’s admirable how long S-Game maintains such a high level of combat-oriented ecstasy. Soul’s access to weapons drives that exhilaration. Every weapon is wholly unique. Because the combat is combo-based, picking up a new weapon feels like unlocking a new character in a fighting game. Each has its own moveset and abilities, with later-game weapons featuring combo lists that look more at home in a Street Fighter menu. Add in the special, tide-turning weapons known as Phantom Edges, with limited charge-based uses, and there’s no shortage of permutations to delightfully experiment with.

Drawing on Chinese cinema, Phantom Blade Zero's setpiece bosses boast a sense of awe and scale only the genre's best typically offer. With virtually no repeat bosses, save for a few in separate trials, it’s impressive how many powerful figures I flayed, and how many delivered a unique fight. I also appreciate the checkpoints between boss phases, as they remove the frustrating repetition of replaying phase one again and again just to take another stab at the second phase I’m struggling with.

You’d be forgiven for assuming Phantom Blade Zero is a Soulslike, given its challenging bosses, interconnected world, and Phantom Bell checkpoints, this game’s equivalent of bonfires. It definitively isn’t, though. The challenge is much more surmountable; the game isn’t interested in making you die over and over, there are difficulty options, and you can equip accessories to make parries and dodges easier. World progression is materially different, too, as enemies don’t respawn after you kill them. It’s an interesting, perhaps blasphemous, choice for the genre, but it's surprisingly effective, adding a sense of worldbuilding and tangible progression I didn’t know I wanted from my action games. Soul is on a mission to remove evil, and mechanically, I’m doing just that. Enemies don’t respawn incoherently just because I heal and save.

Environmental features weave in and out of each other, and the architectural design and layout of these regions lead to many subsequent “aha” moments. S-Game infuses search-action elements into this exploration through the aforementioned Phantom Edges, some of which double as tools to unlock surprising new areas in both new and previously visited biomes. As a result, backtracking and exploration remain fresh. A lot of it is optional, as are some of Phantom Blade Zero's most rewarding elements, including its demanding “perfect” ending. Sadly, this renders other endings unsatisfying, with clear chunks intentionally missing.

Despite forays into the Uncanny Valley, Phantom Blade Zero is visually striking, and the action is brilliantly animated. It’s all set to genre-breaking music, too, with original metalcore songs, operatic choirs, 808s, and traditional Chinese instrumentation, creating a score as illustrious as the action it enhances.

Phantom Blade Zero is an astounding action achievement, almost unbelievably so for a game that is essentially a studio’s genre debut. It is one of the best action games I’ve ever played, one that recognizes the genre’s strengths and weaknesses and addresses both with fantastical Wuxian style. Though the action genre is always jam-packed with new releases, few are as special as Phantom Blade Zero.

#4281. Nioh 3 launches, immediately becomes the most played Nioh ever on Steam

Just a few hours after launch, Nioh 3 is already the biggest release in series history on Steam.

It sounds like Koei Tecmo’s decision to finally release a Nioh game on PC day-and-date with PlayStation has paid off. The highly-anticipated Nioh 3 has gone live across both platforms, a first for a series that typically spends its initial release months as a console exclusive.

On Steam, and despite having only been available for just a few hours, the game has broken series records, and it continues to climb.

At the time of writing, Nioh 3 has peaked at 42,822 concurrent players on Steam (via SteamDB), and the number keeps going up. Because it’s in the middle of day in Europe and everyone is at work, it’s entirely possible - if not likely - that this figure will get much higher. A weekend bump is also possible, as we’ve seen with several recent releases.

As it stands, the current peak concurrent is enough to get the game in Steam’s top 20 most played games.

This already puts it ahead of all other Nioh games on Steam. The original Nioh peaked at 10,649 when it released in November, 2017. Nioh 2 fared much better, peaking at 41,325 concurrent players in February, 2021.

Of course, you could see that success coming a mile away. The game is currently number one worldwide in Steam’s list of top sellers. This is a jump of 46 positions, for a total of three weeks Nioh 3 has spent in that list.

There are many reasons as to why Nioh 3 has done as well as it has. Word of mouth coming off last year’s PS5-exclusive demo, and the more positive coverage that followed since are just two.

Just last week, Team Ninja released a pretty generous demo across both platforms, which has been well received by players, and likely contributed to sales, in no small part because progress in the demo carries over to the full game.

Critical reviews have been incredibly positive, too. We awarded the game four out of five stars, calling it “Team Ninja’s most accomplished action game, and the series’ most accessible.” It will be interesting to see what number the highest peak concurrent actually settles on over the weekend.

Until then, if you’re jumping in yourself, our Nioh 3 guides are essential reading. Start off with these useful and actually informative gameplay tips, and don’t start playing until you’ve changed these settings. Once you’re ready to get deeper, be sure to read up on how to play co-op with other players, and how to summon AI Acolytes to help you out.

#4280. Honkai: Star Rail Version 4.0 brings a new world, and a Fortnite collaboration

Honkai: Star Rail's next major update introduces a whole new planet to the RPG, and way more besides.

HoYoverse just wrapped up a big Honkai: Star Rail Special Program. We’ve been waiting for this one for a couple of weeks now thanks to a delay, but the developer has finally delivered all the news on Version 4.0, which will arrive February 13.

The upcoming major release is dubbed No Aha at Full Moon for a very good reason. Aha's Planarcadia is the big new world headlining Version 4.0.

Planarcadia is a place whose description sounds a bit like a Warhammer 40,000 Eldar homeworld, and is quite open about its cyberpunk inspirations. In-universe, however, it was born out of the pages of an art canvas, and it’s a world where pleasure is king.

The squad’s host in this chapter is Madam Pearl, who will oversee the the Astral Express’ return to the place where they first began their journey. Duomension City is where you’re going to land, and meet the creatures that dwell in this world.

The imagenae of Planarcadia require attention to survive, and they feed off people’s Wishpower. If they don’t get any attention, they perish, which does tie into the general themes of the place. Duomension City has other interesting locations that you’re going to visit, such as the Graphia Academy art school, the commercial district of Dovebrook, and a few other places hidden behind mysterious entrances.

The Phantasmoon Games is another highlight of Planarcadia, a competitive spectacle where you’ll have a chance to compete to become Aeon for a Minute. If you make it to the final stages, you may earn an audience with The Laughter.

Much like the world where the games take place, the whole point of the competition is to attract the most attention, so rules are a bit loose as to how you manage to do that. The event will bring together several of the game’s factions, though not everyone is there for the competition.

As you explore Planarcadia, if you have characters on your team who are on the newly-playable Path of Elation, you’ll earn Punchlines. The more you accumulate, the closer you get to catching Aha’s attention, which triggers Aha Instant.

Version 4.0 introduces two new 5-Star characters to Honkai: Star Rail. General Yao Guang (Madam Yao) is one, a Seer Strategist from the Xianzhou Alliance's Yuque. If you’ve been playing the game, you may already be familiar with her voice, as she's previously been in touch with our heroes via radio link. But V4.0 marks her first on-screen appearance, as well as her playable debut.

General Yao Guang is a Physical character on the Path of Elation whose specialty is using Weal and Woe Lots in battle, which she uses to increase Elation for allies, and grant everyone Punchline any time she uses a Skill. If an Aha Instant is triggered, she casts Woe Lots, which debuff enemies, causing them to take increased damage, all while regenerating Skill Points for the rest of the team.

Her aptly named Certified Banger buff adds one extra instance of Elation to teammates’ attacks. And her Ultimate grants the team Punchline, and triggers an extra Aha Instant.

The other new arrival is likewise a Path of Elation devotee. Sparxie is a suspiciously familiar streamer who uses her influencer skills in combat. When she fights, she turns the fight into a battle for attention, as she forces enemies to engage in a race for upvotes.

When you consume Skill Points, Sparxie will get gifts, which in turn cause her to regenerate Skill Points and Punchlines for the team. You can continue doing this to increase your damage. When Aha Instant is triggered, Sparxie unleashes a lucky draw that deals damage to enemies with each bounce.

She also benefits from the Certified Banger state, which causes the gifs she receives to deal more Elation damage to a random enemy target. Her Ultimate also deals more Elation damage.

Version 4.0 will see a few re-runs, too. Black Swan, Evernight, and Hysilens will be part of the first half's Warp events. The second half will see the return of Sparkle, Cerydra, and Rappa — that's right, HoYoverse have finally remembered Rappa exists, after one of the longest rerun waits in the game's history! Both Black Swan and Sparkle are getting a few tweaks to their kit with this version, too, so the timing works.

If you log in after launch, you’ll get 20 free pulls and a new free outfit for Ruan Mei. If you play while the Yao Guang fortune event is active, you could earn 1,600 Stellar Jades. You can also expect a free 5-Star character selector to arrive at some point after launch, giving you a free choice between popular (but admittedly a bit old for the meta these days) limited-banner characters Jing Yuan, Kafka, Dan Heng • Imbibitor Lunae, Jingliu, Sparkle, Acheron, and Aventurine.

Finally, the other major news is a Fortnite collaboration. Starting February 26, Kafka and Blade will join Epic’s battle royale shooter. On that day, you’ll find skins of the two Stellaron Hunters in the Fortnite Item Shop, and the new outfits are even compatible with Fortnite's LEGO styles. You can also expect other customisation bits like Back Bling, Pickaxe, and more to be part of the package.

If you download the game on the Epic Games Store, and take part in Honkai: Star Rail-themed activities, you’ll also get the Blade character outfit in Fortnite for free. Event schedule and timing will be announced at a later date.

#4279. Cozy Magical Sim Witchbrook Gets A January Release Date

Witchbrook is a game I've been looking forward to for a while, and today's Nintendo Indie World showcase finally confirmed the game's release date: January 28. Any game from Chucklefish, best known for publishing Stardew Valley and developing the Wargroove series, is worthy of my attention, and Witchbrook looks more exciting the more we see of it. See it for yourself in the release date trailer below.

The game mixes cute pixel art with a robust suite of magical gameplay systems. As you go to a witch college to learn spells, you'll also build a life in the town, making friends, working jobs, decorating your home, and more. It was an appealing pitch when it was announced nearly 10 years ago in 2017, and it remains so to this day. After a long stretch of relative silence, last year the game was scheduled to launch sometime in 2026. Obviously, the team has faced some delays since then, but we're just glad it's actually coming out.

Witchbrook's release date was announced during today's Nintendo-specific stream, but it's coming to all major platforms: PS5, Xbox Series X/S, Switch 2, Switch, and PC.

#4278. Roblox: One Fruit tier list

We all know that there's a huge difference between every type of fruit in the game. You'll learn what the current meta is from our One Fruit tier list.

As you already figured out by the title, in this article we rank every fruit in One Fruit. You can find out which are the best fruits that made it to the top of our tier list (SS-Tier), and which are the worst ones that you shouldn't bother with.

As you probably already know, tier lists are somewhat subjective. Everyone has a different opinion based on their preferred playstyle. In other words, nobody will ever come up with a One Fruit Simulator tier list that everyone agrees with. That said, if you are a new player (or a returning one), this guide will give you a pretty good idea about the current meta, or rather the best fruits in the game. Also, keep in mind that our One Fruit Simulator tier list will probably change with future updates. If you are playing this game then you already know that some fruits are getting nerfed or buffed from time to time. So, make sure to check back on this page to get the latest fruit rankings.

Since you are on this page, you probably enjoy playing anime-fighting games on Roblox. So you might want to check out our Blox Fruits tier list to find out which are the best fruits to use in that game, or if you're an anime lover, have a look at our Anime World Tower Defense tier list!

Enough with this - let's get right onto the One Fruit Simulator tier list!

When we talk about non-awakened fruits, the ones in SS-Tier are borderline broken. So, use whichever one you feel like. My personal opinion is that the Venom fruit is the absolute best, but hey, aren't all of them like super overpowered really?

These are great fruits; that's why they are S-Tier. They are not as broken as the ones in SS-Tier, but certainly excellent in their own right. Which ones you are going to use and whatnot is up to you and your preferred playstyle.

Now every A-Tier fruit is good. Like, definitely above average. As you transition from mid to late game, these are the fruits that you want to have. You probably won't use them in the very late stages of the game, but that's ok. They'll do until then.

These fruits are not good, but are not terrible either. Let's say they are mid. That's why they go into B-Tier. Think of them as a bridge from the early to mid-game. After that point, you won't really bother with them again, as you are probably going to have better fruits.

OK, so these fruits are straight up bad. That's why I've put them in the bottom tier. But that's only if we are talking about the later stages of the game. During the very early moments, they can be useful until you can equip better ones.

So I've decided to rank the awakened fruits separately because... well, because they are awakened! So, there you have it. If you want to check out their animations and skills, there are many videos on YouTube like this one.

#4277. Heartopia shows off My Little Pony collaboration, and there's a pre-launch event to hold you over

Heartopia’s My Little Pony collaboration is close, and the pre-launch event has already kicked off.

Heartopia has officially shared initial details about its first-ever collaboration event. The game, which launched a month ago to great success on mobile, as well as Steam on PC, has already been a staple among fans of Animal Crossing and The Sims.

Things are kicking into gear, it seems, because the game is already about to host its first collaboration event, and it is with My Little Pony.

The Heartopia X My Little Pony event officially begins on February 14, but a pre-launch login event is now live through the actual collaboration’s start. The limited-time event offers players sign-in puzzles every day that will unlock time-limited Exhibition Passes.

The first actual piece of My Little Pony-themed content can be yours if you complete all puzzles, as that gets you a limited edition costume for your pet, based on the show’s Spike. The event itself, which will be available until March 15, brings My Little Pony’s Tree of Harmony into the world of Heartopia.

The ponies need your help to Wield Elements of Harmony so they can reawaken the tree, and bring it back to Equestria. In gameplay terms, you’re going to want to perform daily sensing at the tree in order to earn three of the six Elements of Harmony: Honesty, Generosity, Loyalty, Kindness, Laughter, and Magic.

The more you do this, the more the tree’s Energy goes up, and the more rewards and resources you stand to earn. Even more time-limited Exhibition Passes, and Moonlight Crystals can be earned as you water the tree.

Badge Pull Tokens are your big reward, which is what you’re actually going to use to get the special Pony Series badges. You’ll earn ten time-limited Exhibition Passes each time you complete one of the three sets of Pony Series badges. Collect all three and you’ll earn Town Collaboration Series badges.

Heartopia is a free-to-play game, so you know there is a Gacha component to this event. Expect six non-replacement Gacha Pools that each map to one member of My Little Pony’s Mane Six. Within each pool, you’ll be able to earn five outfit pieces, and one vehicle.

If any of that sounds interesting, definitely log in now to play the pre-launch event, which should hold you over until the proper show kicks off Saturday. If you’re already enjoying Heartopia, you likely want to learn about Onsen Egg Promise locations, Fish locations, and Bug locations - all of which can be found at those links.

We also recently updated our guides on how to catch Frostspore fish - and if you’re into cooking, how to obtain every recipe and variant. If you haven’t already, definitely see if you missed any of these Heartopia codes, too.

#4276. Nintendo Indie World Showcase Recap: Everything We Saw

The year is nearing its conclusion, and the last big AAA titles are rolling out one-by-one. But today, it was all about the independent titles on Nintendo's latest Indie World Showcase, highlighting new games from smaller indie teams coming to the Switch and Switch 2.

Here's everything we saw at the October 2026 Nintendo Indie World Showcase.

Today's Indie World Showcase started with a big headliner, as the long-awaited witch-life simulator Witchbrook got a release date. Chucklefish and Robtality's cozy magical world goes live on January 28, 2027.

Fans of 3D platformers should probably keep an eye on Winds of Viridia, which looks like a colorful game with a lot of interesting movement and exploration. Shark Jump's fantastical platformer is arriving next year, but if the wait's too long, a free demo is coming today on the eShop.

From one of the co-creators of Celeste, City of None has a gorgeous pixelated art style and colors that immediately remind me of Game Boy Color classics. It's a 2D platformer where you leap around, fight enemies, and explore the strange city around you. The jumping and fighting look solid, and I really like the mysterious atmosphere and art direction. City of None's set for sometime in 2027.

The sword-surfing adventure from the makers of Abzu and Journey is coming to Nintendo Switch 2 on October 29, 2026 - tomorrow! It's a gorgeous adventure that earned a Must-Play badge from us, so it's worth your time if you like the kinds of gorgeous, beautiful adventures Giant Squid (developer of Abzu) is known for.

Take an overhead camera angle, brawler gameplay, and some John Wick sensibilities, and you've got Tenjutsu, a stylish roguelike where you use your martial arts prowess to tear apart crime syndicates. I really enjoy the look and vibe of this one, and it's from one of the designers of Dead Cells, too. Tenjutsu might be one to keep an eye on when it arrives on Switch 2 in 2027.

RPG fans have been eating well, and it looks like the feast could continue next year with Threads of Time. The time-traveling RPG is coming to both Switch and Switch 2 next summer, and it's looking absolutely gorgeous.

Ah, raccoons. Nature's most adorable little scamps. If you and your friends have ever wanted to live out the dream of being a rambunctious band of raccoons wreaking havoc on the town, Dumpster Gang sets out to give you just that fantasy in March 2027.

I've already enjoyed quite a bit of Super Battle Golf on PC, so I'll tell you now: if you enjoy golf games and want some Mario Party annoy-your-friends antics wound around them, Super Battle Golf should be on your radar for its March 25, 2027 launch on Switch 2.

Another port of a PC multiplayer mainstay, the co-op physics-driven horror-looter R.E.P.O. is coming to Switch 2 in 2027. This is one for the crowd that likes to be scared one moment and laughing hysterically the next.

Rounding out the co-op section, Haunted Paws has you and a pal playing as a pair of pups searching for their person in a haunted mansion. The side-scrolling 3D look makes it seem like a less-scary Little Nightmares, and the concept is pretty fun. Look for this one on Switch and Switch 2 in May 2027, or try out the free demo later today.

Enjoy shrines, towns, and strange night-time journeys into the unknown? Follow a fox girl and her frog friend on an adventure through a strange island in Kitsune: The Journey of Adashino on Switch 2 and Switch in spring 2027. I've said it a few times in this recap, but wow, the art here is great.

The second entry in the slime-collecting, home-building sim adventure is coming to Switch 2. Pick up adorable slimes with your vacuum, build a home for them, and explore the Rainbow Island around you in January 2027. Plus, there's an exclusive in-game item for the Switch 2 version.

From the makers of Cozy Grove, this multiplayer game encourages players to build a home above the clouds with friends and explore the world around them. Spirit Crossing looks like a big world to make your own alongside your pals, starting November 16, 2026 on both Switch and Switch 2.

Want something a little sillier? My Arms Are Longer Now is a game about, well, really long arms. With numerous Australian comedians lending their vocal talents to the project, this seems like it could be a quirky, charming, and delightfully funny experience when it arrives on both Switch and Switch 2 on March 11, 2027.

The delightfully Game Boy-styled critter delivery game Petal Runner is aiming for a full launch. I've played a bit of this one at events over the years, and it's charmed me every time. If you like nostalgic adventures with a surprisingly heartfelt core, you should mark down the March 8, 2027 launch, or check out the free demo arriving later today.

The chaotic coin-pushing game Raccoin is coming to Nintendo Switch 2. It's just like those token-shoving games you remember from arcades but with a number of wild and wacky means of pushing even more coins over the edge run-over-run. Raccoin: Chaos Max Edition hits Switch 2 on November 10, 2026, and a free demo is out later today.

#4274. The Legacy and Evolution of Rockstar Games: How One Studio Redefined Open-World Gaming

Usama Mehmood is a Senior Writer at DualShockers with more than five years of experience in the video game industry. He has been writing professionally since 2021 and covering games since 2022, with work spanning guides, lists, reviews, and features across action-adventure games, JRPGs, open-world titles, racing games,

I grew up with an unhealthy obsession with the Grand Theft Auto series. The game wasn’t obviously meant for an 8-year-old, but it showed me the greatest gift: my parents wanting to give me happiness and comfort throughout my upbringing, even if it meant unknowingly handing me a game that was clearly meant for older audiences.

But hey, it didn’t meddle with my behavior, alright? Playing San Andreas was one of my most endearing experiences, with countless playthroughs/save files. And I mean, some of my best video game memories even involved my dad helping me clear a couple of tough missions in both it and Vice City. So from those 3D-era entries to see how far Rockstar has come to be this industry powerhouse with their sandbox video game series is genuinely astounding to see.

Aaron Garbut, co-studio head of Rockstar North, explained that no single person has the entire game mapped out in their head.

Rockstar Games has spent decades building some of the most recognisable worlds in video game history. Whether it's the streets of Los Santos, the mob-boss-riddled underworld of Liberty City, or a quiet ride through the unforgiving American frontier with an on-the-run gang of outlaws, there's something remarkably special about the worlds this studio creates.

With Grand Theft Auto VI approaching in just over two weeks, it's worth looking back at how that journey unfolded. From the studio's transformation and the franchises that shaped its identity to the enormous expectations around its next release, Rockstar's legacy is about much more than the games it has sold. It's about how one developer helped redefine what players expect from open-world experiences.

We’re taking this back to the humble beginnings of Rockstar Games. See, before it became one of the most popular names in the gaming landscape, its story actually began with a much smaller development team in Dundee, Scotland. Founded in 1988 by David Jones and a group of fellow developers, DMA Design started as a relatively small studio with ambitions to make its mark in an industry still finding its footing.

Its early releases, including Menace and Blood Money, showed its interest in arcade-inspired action games, but the arrival of a quirky little game called Lemmings in 1991 truly put the developer on the map. This relatively simple puzzle game (unexpectedly) became an enormous success, selling an estimated 20 million copies across its various platforms.

However, a very different kind of project would ultimately change the studio's future, since in 1997, DMA Design would then release the original Grand Theft Auto, trading its familiar arcade experiences for a top-down crime sandbox that allowed you to steal vehicles, complete odd-job missions, evade the police, and wreak havoc across fictional cities.

As the OG Grand Theft Auto continued to gain momentum despite being an experimental first entry, DMA Design underwent a series of ownership changes before becoming part of Take-Two Interactive and the wider Rockstar Games family around the turn of the millennium.

Eventually, the studio relocated from Dundee to Edinburgh, and in 2002, it officially became Rockstar North. This transformation, or turnaround, whichever one you prefer, would soon carry forward the creative foundations established years earlier. And little did you or I know just how far that journey would take them; this small Scottish team was now at the heart of a studio that would go on to produce some of the most influential open-world experiences in gaming history.

Former Rockstar technical director Obbe Vermeij recalls how GTA 3’s small team made communication easier and gave developers room to experiment.

Funnily enough, I had the chance to revisit GTA 3 this past month as part of my replay of all the mainline entries before VI’s arrival. Forgive me if it was the Definitive Edition; it was dirt-cheap on sale, and I’d already played the OG version on my PS2 as a kid, so I thought, why not try things differently, especially after this much time has passed since this trilogy’s controversial release?

Now, contrary to what the header suggests, although open-world games existed long before Grand Theft Auto III arrived, few developers had managed to bring together the same level of freedom, exploration, and interactive storytelling that Rockstar would eventually become known for. In fact, this is also why I’d like to give a shout-out to my co-worker and friend, Maddie, for discussing how 1999's Urban Chaos, developed by Mucky Foot Productions, was already experimenting with a 3D urban environment, free-roaming exploration, and mission-based gameplay two years before GTA 3 hit the PS2.

While it wasn't the expansive sandbox Rockstar would then create in later titles, it showed the potential of this simple yet experimental idea: letting players explore and interact with a full 3D city. But because it went beyond the formulaic approach of the prior two GTAs, you could absolutely make a case that this game was a generational release for its time.

Instead of simply following a predetermined series of missions, players could steal vehicles, explore different neighborhoods, interact with pedestrians, engage in shootouts, and stumble upon all sorts of unexpected chaos along the way. Driving, shooting, and exploring were no longer separate gameplay modes, but seamlessly interconnected parts of a much larger experience.

Oh, and it didn’t stop there, obviously. The game's success would go on to influence countless developers, establishing a formula that would shape much of the open-world genre for years to come, since Rockstar wasn't simply offering players a large map to explore; it was creating an environment filled with activities, distractions, and opportunities for experimentation.

Playing San Andreas was one of my most endearing experiences, with countless playthroughs/save files.

The studio continued refining that approach with Grand Theft Auto: Vice City in 2002 and then Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas in 2004. The former introduced a distinctive 1980s atmosphere reminiscent of Miami Vice’s stylized tone and an unforgettable soundtrack, while the latter expanded the formula considerably with multiple cities, character customization, and RPG-inspired mechanics.

So by the time San Andreas arrived, Rockstar had shown how much freedom and variety could fit into a single open-world experience. It is genuinely insane that these guys released three back-to-back bangers; it's an honest travesty that they outsourced the modern re-release of them to an external developer under their umbrella.

GTA 3 often ran at just 7 or 8 FPS during development, according to former Rockstar technical director Obbe Vermeij.

While Grand Theft Auto remained Rockstar's biggest commercial success, the company was never particularly interested in limiting itself to a single franchise; these guys were seriously trailblazing their way to the top. That’s because throughout the 2000s, its growing network of development studios experimented with different genres, storytelling approaches, and settings, resulting in some of its most memorable cult favorites.

Bully took the familiar open-world formula and turned it into a crude yet charming coming-of-age adventure. Meanwhile, Manhunt explored a much darker side of the company's creativity through its disturbing atmosphere (enough to give me the frights as a kid) and brutal stealth-based gameplay, and then Midnight Club brought open-city exploration into the street racing scene of the 2000s that other series like NFS also capitalized on with Fast and Furious’ popularity.

And don’t worry, like most of you, possibly longtime fans reading this, I still hold an undying grudge against Rockstar for never revisiting these games again, especially the high possibilities for a sequel to Bully, which I’m never burying the hatchet over because the Scholarship Edition is one of my most played and adored games on the Xbox 360. The bottom line is that these projects showed Rockstar's ambitions extended well beyond crime-driven satire sandboxes, allowing its various studios to establish their own identities across genres.

Rockstar Games has spent decades building some of the most recognisable worlds in video game history.

Of course, Grand Theft Auto wasn't going anywhere. And how ironic that I rolled credits on this just a week ago. With GTA IV in 2008, Rockstar took a noticeably different approach to its established formula for a grittier, more grounded portrayal of Liberty City akin to New York City.

It introduced a string of themes like revenge, organized crime overlords butting heads for power, and the often uncomfortable realities of chasing the American Dream. Plus, things like the ragdoll physics and weight-based driving model were the icing on the cake for an otherwise brilliant crime drama, one that I personally think is the best in the series in terms of writing. However, as much as I hate to admit it, Rockstar wasn't finished pushing those boundaries.

An interview with Rockstar reveals details about GTA 6's morality system.

Grand Theft Auto V arrived in 2013, taking you back to Los Santos and introducing three playable protagonists: Michael, Franklin, and Trevor. Its intertwining storytelling, enormous variety of activities, and remarkable sense of freedom made it a defining open-world release of its generation. Today, it is insane to think about how many records this game has broken: it's one of the best-selling video games of all time, second only to Minecraft, and has generated billions of dollars since its original launch.

Beyond the story mode, GTA Online (unfortunately) gradually grew into a massive multiplayer platform of its own, keeping players invested through years of updates, new missions, vehicles, heists, and activities. And I won’t lie: as someone who spent an unhealthy number of hours on it, this game was partly why I found two of my bestest friends. Also, this mode's longevity and the revenue it generated through microtransactions were low-key part of why GTA V became a cultural phenomenon that kept thriving across multiple console generations.

The wizards at Rockstar didn’t stop there, because the leap that came forward after would soon set the benchmark for people to compare most open-world releases to, even if most of those comparisons became insufferable to come across in social media posts and/or videos.

And that considerable leap came when Rockstar dropped the technical bombshell that was Red Dead Redemption 2 in 2018. You see, I could’ve put the original entry in the section above with the other projects these guys did, but it only felt right to include it here, since both these two Wild West open-world titles became games that almost felt like companion pieces to the GTA franchise. That was evident not only in the mission design, but also in newer additions like the Honor system, a fully realized wildlife ecosystem, and other gameplay elements that made it feel like a sister game to GTA.

Following the success of the 2010 entry, the sequel offered a story centered around Arthur Morgan and the gradual decline of the Van der Linde gang, one that slowly connected to the events of RDR1. Its greatest achievement, however, was arguably the extraordinary level of detail packed into its bygone world. From real wildlife behavior and daily NPC routines to dynamic world events that shifted depending on the protagonist or time passed, almost every aspect of its world contributed to an incredible sense of immersion.

Although years later, you’ll now find some recent verbal engagements about people arguing about its flawed mission design, and as much as I think it's a bit overrated (please put the pitchforks down), I will wholeheartedly agree on the fact that this was THE game that made Rockstar the rightful heir to the throne for creating one of the most immersive and compelling open-world games of all time. Most importantly, it also rewarded those willing to slow down and simply enjoy their surroundings, and I think that’s the best compliment to give RDR2 given the current attention span of most mainstream audiences.

After decades of refining its approach to open-world design, Rockstar Games now stands on the doorstep of what could be its most ambitious project yet, as GTA VI represents more than just another long-awaited sequel, especially considering how much the studio has accomplished since we first stepped foot into Los Santos by repo’ing cars with Franklin and Lamar or just cruising around Ocean Beach as Tommy.

I won’t bore your ear with a bunch of what-if bumbo jumbo, but all I want to sign off with is that, given everything Rockstar has showcased so far, there's plenty of reason to be excited about the possibilities they could improve upon here, particularly when considering the technical artistry demonstrated in RDR2.

We’ve already seen an extent of the full gameplay in action with the Extended Look, as well as tons of deeper details shared online across media outlets that make this entry a proper sim-like experience, which I honestly don’t mind since I genuinely wanted Rockstar to bring back the RPG stuff they introduced back in San Andreas. Heck, even if it’s not confirmed, throw in vehicle schools again to give Lucia and Jason even more stats to manage.

For me, one of the biggest challenges GTA VI faces is delivering a story that can stand alongside GTA IV because Niko Bellic's journey for me remains one of the franchise's most memorable narratives precisely because it went beyond the usual criminal escapade trope. Most of all, it made its protagonist feel like more than another criminal navigating a fictional city, and I'd love to see Jason and Lucia achieve that in their own way.

Their relationship already gives Rockstar an interesting foundation to explore, but what matters most is whether the studio can make players genuinely care about the people behind all the chaos. Give me another round of NPC social links calling either protagonist just for a round of bowling or, y’know, give me reasons to interact with them again via their special abilities/benefits.

Now, with Leonida and the newly imagined Vice City waiting just around the corner, it feels like we're about to experience the next chapter in a legacy that has shaped how an entire generation experiences video games.

While I generally have mixed feelings about the overly eccentric fanbase, I’ll put that aside for now since I’m also proudly blasting Flower in Hurricane and Inner Light on repeat these days to itch my hype fever for the game’s release on November 19th. Whether Rockstar can deliver another landmark open-world experience remains to be seen, but hey, to anyone who made it here to see it happen, I hope we eat good with whatever they’ve cooked up over the past 13 years.

Rockstar says GTA 6 pre-loading begins November 10 and could require up to 212 GB, though some official pages still show the old date.

#4273. KRÜ Blaze win Game Changers Championship from lower bracket, ending Gentle Mates’ unbeaten run

KRÜ Blaze came through the lower bracket to beat Europe's Gentle Mates GC over five maps in São Paulo, giving LATAM its first Game Changers Championship title. They are also the last winners of the standalone event, as next year's final moves to Champions.

KRÜ Blaze are the 2026 VALORANT Game Changers Championship winners. They edged Gentle Mates GC 3-2 at the Riot Games Arena in São Paulo on 1 November. No Latin American team had lifted the title before. No team had ever won it from the lower bracket either.

The event ran from 22 October, with 10 teams competing. Gentle Mates earned US$100,000 as runners-up. Shopify Rebellion Gold took US$70,000 for third place and MIBR GC US$50,000 for fourth.

KRÜ took the long route. They beat Gen.G GC 2-1 in the upper-bracket quarter-finals on 23 October. A 2-0 loss to Shopify Rebellion Gold on 27 October then dropped them into the lower bracket. They answered with clean sweeps of Team Liquid Brazil and MIBR GC. On 31 October they beat Shopify Rebellion Gold 3-1 in the best-of-five lower-bracket final.

The grand final swung back and forth. Gentle Mates took Haven 13-5 before KRÜ levelled on Abyss by the same score. KRÜ led the third map 10-2 at half-time. Gentle Mates fought back, but KRÜ closed it out 14-12 in overtime. Gentle Mates then won Split 13-8 to force a decider. KRÜ led 11-5 on Ascent and won it by the same margin as Split.

Liquipedia named KRÜ’s Argentine player tok1o as the event’s MVP. Brazilian teammates antG and none became the first Brazilians to win an international tournament held in São Paulo.

The result breaks a pattern. Before 2026 the title went to G2 Gozen for Europe in 2022, Shopify Rebellion for North America in 2023 and 2024, and Team Liquid Brazil in 2025. KRÜ’s own record at the event had improved steadily. They finished 7th–8th in 2022 and 5th–6th in each of the next two years. Last year they came fourth.

For European fans, it was a painful near miss. Gentle Mates GC arrived as EMEA’s top seed on circuit points. The team had not lost a series in São Paulo before the final, according to Esports News UK.

It capped a strong debut season in the circuit. Gentle Mates won EMEA Stage 1 by sweeping G2 Gozen 3-0 on 22 February. They lost the Stage 2 final to SK Nebula on 24 May without winning a map. On 30 August they lost the Stage 3 final to G2 Gozen in a fifth map. Silver in São Paulo leaves them with one title from four finals this year.

After a lower bracket run in São Paulo, the LATAM squad claimed the #VCTGameChangers Championship trophy! pic.twitter.com/YeSeb10TZc

— VCT Pacific (@vctpacific) November 1, 2026

The São Paulo final also closes a format. KRÜ are the last team to lift the trophy at a separate event of its own. For the first time, the Game Changers Championship will finish at Champions. Under Riot’s 2027 plan, non-partner teams that qualify for the Game Changers Championship will receive an extra US0,000 incentive. VALORANT Champions 2027 is scheduled for 16 September to 10 October in Austin.

#4272. Nioh 3 is killing it on Steam with over double the series' highest concurrent player count

People seemingly haven't been able to stop playing Nioh 3 since the moment it came out, and everyone helped push the numbers to unprecedented heights for the series.

The upcoming God of War spin-off has been delayed to May 20th, dodging the busy February release window.

Arkane Lyon is one studio that's been in hot water for a long while, struggling to find a buyer before Microsoft closes its doors. Following hopeful news as more buyers step up, a French union with ties to Arkane staff has accused Microsoft of attempting to sabotage the development of the studio’s current project, Blade, by barring hires for over a year.

The development of Marvel’s Blade has been absolutely hectic, between internal shifts in the game’s vision and an early announcement that put heat on Arkane far before they were ready. Now, STJV, the French union representing certain members of Arkane Lyon’s staff, has made a major accusation, claiming the game is coming along fine, despite Microsoft’s interference.

According to STJV in a direct quotation, “Today, as work on Blade is going fine, and the level of quality of the game to be expected is on [par] with what Arkane has accustomed its players, workers have to face the harsh reality: our studio might get closed because, and only because, Microsoft decided to, even if that means sabotaging the game it funded.”

This all still has yet to be confirmed, as no direct response from Microsoft has been released, despite the accusations levied by STJV. Alongside the biting remarks, the union has dropped a series of demands, including a say in who buys Arkane, and a larger payout for the staff if no buyer steps forward.

It's easy to write off every issue in the modern industry as someone else’s fault, but that’s not realistic, every part of the industry is struggling, inside and out.

Despite all of this swinging out, Arkane is still eager to release Blade, staying optimistic that the title will release in the following years if Arkane is allowed to keep their doors open. STJV keeps the argument practical, framing the studio’s progress as a financial incentive for both parties. “Even this closure itself is done against any financial logic, as closing Arkane today would probably be more expensive than finishing the game,” says STJV.

Arkane’s aim to finish the game despite their wild situation is comforting to see, and gives me real hope at the quality of their Blade title, as long as it manages to release. The whispers of big studios like Ubisoft’s interest make it clear more than just Arkane want to see the title released, and as the months continue to tick by with the company still open, those whispers just get louder.

Arkane is a studio that would feel like a serious loss for the larger gaming industry if they closed their doors, even after stumbles like Redfall. Dropping into the mainstream scene with hits like Dishonored and Prey, Arkane Lyon is infamous for worlds that feel so lived-in, even after devastation has raked across them.

They truly do feel like the perfect team to work on Blade, as their mastery of immersive sims and wild powers leaves massive room for the exact type of action Blade is perfect for. It really does feel like every production surrounding Blade is hexed, if the canceled films and Arkane’s own pains are anything to look at.

I’m very eager to hear a response from Microsoft, as STJV has levied some major accusations that could really disrupt how third parties and internal studios interact with them. At present, we only have STJV’s word to go off of, so take these accusations with a grain of salt until more comes out.

#4263. Battlefield 6's next season will speed up battle pass progression, and make it so Redsec players who don't own the game can actually make progress

Season 2 of Battlefield 6 looks to bring a host of broad, positive changes to XP, progression, audio and more.

Ahead of the start of Battlefield 6’s Season 2 next week, Battlefield Studios has shared some insight into a few of the major goals the developer has with the Season 2 patch. The game’s second season was delayed in mid-January, and the developer even brought back Battlefield Labs to test out some of the new content and features coming with the new season.

Indeed, the broader goals BF Studios shared with players in a new blog post reflect some of what Labs players already went hands-on with, while others are the result of work on long-standing issues with both the game itself, as well as free-to-play mode Redsec.

We know that Season 2 is introducing a big new map to the game, Contaminated, which the developer has been teasing. The map will indeed arrive in the first part of the season, and it’s going to do so alongside a new LTM that “introduces a new element of tactics.” A second, “high-intensity map” will debut later into the season, alongside another LTM where players battle through an underground base, in darkness.

The real meat of the blog post, however, covers the broader gameplay changes everyone will see once the new season kicks off. There’s a massive focus on player progression, especially when it concerns free-to-play Redsec players.

Challenges are being streamlined yet again, with more broad parameters that don’t require specific modes. Some, like dailies, will also allow for assists to count towards their criteria. Less restrictive challenges are welcome, but even more so is the faster battle pass progression.

BF Studios is changing the rate at which battle pass Tokens are earned from career XP, and making it so they’re earnable by playing the game normally, and by completing weekly challenges. These changes should also help Redsec players, who will also benefit from faster career and weapon XP earn rates - across both battle royale, and Gauntlet. In general, the career experience should feel more rewarding, especially for earlier ranks.

Weapon balance and recoil are two areas that will continue to evolve in Battlefield 6, it seems, and Season 2 is specifically tackling recoil patterns to make them more consistent when you compensate for them.

Movement is being adjusted with the Season 2 patch, too, though thankfully it’s limited to general feel that touches areas like vaulting, ladder transitions, and acceleration curves. You should also see better continuity and consistency between animations and feel.

Audio is getting a pass with the upcoming patch, especially when it comes to footstep and interaction audio. This also extends to something the developer has been working on improving for a while, and it has to do with how the game decides which audio tracks to prioritise in busy situations.

Tomorrow, the full Battlefield 6 Season 2 trailer will be released, while a more detailed roadmap is expected by the end of this week.

Diablo 4’s segment in the big Diablo 30th Anniversary Spotlight was among the biggest, even if the reason most of us tuned in was somewhat spoiled earlier in the same livestream. Blizzard unveiled the Warlock, the second of two classes coming to the game with the upcoming Lord of Hatred expansion.

The first class, being the Paladin, is already available to play for anyone who pre-ordered the expansion, but the Warlock won’t be accessible until the expansion arrives in late April.

The Warlocks are positioned as the opposite of the Paladins, in that they don’t mind utilising forbidden knowledge, drawing on the powers of Hell itself to fight its own overlords. The Warlock is the edgy, antihero counterpart to the Paladin’s purity and devotion to the Light.

The livestream did not show off any Warlock gameplay, but Blizzard is planning a dedicated livestream to show off the new class’ gameplay, and dig deeper into its lore and abilities. That show is scheduled for March 5.

What we did get to see was our first look at Skovos, the expansion’s new region. This Mediterranean-inspired location is where the new story arc will unfold, but it’s also being positioned as the endgame destination for Diablo 4 once the credits roll.

Lord of Hatred, of course, as previously revealed, introduces two new endgame modes in War Plans, and Echoing Hatred.

War Plans lets you create a custom playlist of up to five endgame activities to target specific rewards and create your own experience. There’s a new activity tree that works with all endgame activities, and creating War Plans is how you earn progression there.

Echoing Hatred, on the other hand, is a rare event that pits you against legions of Mephisto’s minions. It’s triggered through a rare lootable item that unlocks access. It’s essentially horde mode; where you’ll face unending waves of enemies, though not without a couple of twists.

We also got a bit more colour on the expanded class skill trees, which all players will benefit from when the expansion arrives. The Talisman system, which unlocks set bonuses, was also shown off. And, of course, the return of the iconic Horadric Cube, which gives you control over Affixes.

#4259. 5 new mobile games to try this week - November 5th, 2026

Fresh mobile picks you should give a go this week

Who doesn't love new games? We certainly do - there's just something about the exhilaration of a new title you can't wait to dive into, as the loading screen pops up and you enter a brave new world.

Of course, new mobile games are a dime a dozen these days, and who has the time to scour the iPhone, iPad and/or Android stores to catch the latest title that drops? Fret not - we've gathered a quick list of 5 new mobile games you should try this week, whether that's an undiscovered indie gem or a high-profile AAA masterpiece.

That said, you can head on over to our NEW WEEKLY MOBILE GAMES hub if you're on the hunt for more curated adventures to obsess over!

I suppose there's nothing quite like the end of the month than being reminded of your adulting responsibilities, which is probably why Bills Must Be Paid picked November 1st for an official launch. As you might expect from the title, this incremental clicker will have you struggling to, well, pay the bills - but the cathartic thing about it is that you'll at least get the satisfaction of smashing piggy banks out of it.

You'll have all kinds of hammers at your disposal for said piggy bank smashing, which, of course, costs stamina. You can't let exhaustion get the better of you, though, because, as you well know, bills must be paid - and bankruptcy quite literally means game over.

Absolum's art style was what initially caught my eye here, but honestly, the fact that it's a roguelite beat 'em up is already more than enough to pique my interest. The continent is apparently turning into dungeons, and it's up to Dungeon Supporter Mika to save the world. You'll step into each tile not knowing what it holds, but whether it's a fatal trap you're falling into or a bloodthirsty Mimic waiting for the right moment, you'll need to use your powers of backpack organisation to survive every run. It's the backpack handler's job to give those ungrateful heroes their supplies, after all, so you're pretty much the true hero here.

If you've still got a Halloween hangover, perhaps a little bit of Jekyll and Hyde might suffice? Heir of the Dog takes the classic tale and adds a humorous twist to it, and with charming pixel art to boot! The point-and-click mystery will have you searching high and low across Victorian London for clues on a missing dog, with plenty of hilarious hijinks in between.

The main protagonist is named Cummerbund Bandersnatch, for one thing. For another, it takes inspiration from Monty Python, so you know you're in for a treat - if you're up for shelling out $14.99 a pop!

Cute cats in a mobile game is a plus as it is in my book - even more so when there's multiple copies of them! This aptly titled platformer tasks you with creating copies of yourself to solve tricky puzzles across a strange lab, where you can use your titular Copy Cats to stack up high and reach unreachable places.

You might even need to manipulate your clones just to get your main cat to the exit, because when there's a missing cat involved, you need to do everything in your power to help it find its way back home.

#4258. Here's The Best Graphics And Performance Mode For Phantom Blade Zero On PlayStation 5

Phantom Blade Zero is out now for everyone as a console exclusive on PlayStation 5 and on PC via Steam and the Epic Games Store as well. If you missed it, it's my favorite action game of the year so far, and you can read why in Game Informer's Phantom Blade Zero review. That explains why I think you should check the game out; Game Informer's list of Phantom Blade Zero tips and tricks will get you some key information I wish I had when I started the game; and this guide I wrote up about the requirements you need to get the best ending in Phantom Blade Zero will help you find all story-critical content in the game.

However, you're looking for advice on which of the three visual modes Phantom Blade Zero offers you should use on your PS5. This here piece is for you.

Phantom Blade Zero has three visual modes on PS5 Pro: Quality, Balanced, and Performance. I tested all three. My personal favorite was Balanced, which gives you an upscaled (checkerboarded) 4K resolution at 40 FPS, as long as you have a 120Hz TV with VRR. If you have a 120Hz TV, it likely has VRR because most major manufacturers include it with 120Hz. I like this mode because the upscaled 4K looks beautiful, just a hair less than native 4K, and if you aren't someone super trained on those details, I'd wager you won't notice the difference. The best part is that this mode offers 40 FPS gameplay, which, contrary to how math works, is halfway between 30 FPS and 60 FPS; I'm not kidding, look it up. As such, 40 FPS feels much smoother than 30 FPS, and you're still getting crisp 4K resolution. It's a win-win for me and my go-to mode when a game offers it. That said, if you don’t have a PS5 Pro, you won’t see this Balanced mode.

The Performance mode offers an upscaled 2K resolution with a pretty locked 60 FPS. Phantom Blade Zero is an extremely fast, fluid action game, so I think many people will want the buttery smoothness of 60 FPS gameplay. If that's you, pick the Performance mode. Sure, its resolution is lower, and it will look blurrier and less crisp than the other two modes, but if you aren't switching back and forth often or looking at side-by-side images, you likely won't notice.

Quality mode is native 4K resolution (absolutely beautiful, the best visual image you can get playing Phantom Blade Zero), but at 30 FPS... and for a game like this, I don't think 30 FPS does it justice. I don't really recommend this mode for combat, but if you're just waltzing around Wulin, grabbing screenshots and such, turn it on and bask in the wonders of developer S-Game's art team. Note: There is an option for ray tracing on PS5 Pro. I tested all three graphics modes with it on and off and noticed zero performance changes or issues. So, use ray tracing – it’s nice!

And, in case you missed it, below is an image of the PC system requirements and specs needed to play Phantom Blade Zero on Steam and the Epic Games Store:

In the meantime, read Game Informer's Phantom Blade Zero review, then check out our list of Phantom Blade Zero tips and tricks we wish we knew before starting the game. Then check out our breakdown of the requirements to see the best ending in the game.

#4257. Gen.G sweep LYON to end North America’s Worlds 2026 run and set up iG semi-final

Gen.G beat LYON 3-0 in Allen, Texas, removing North America's last team from Worlds 2026. The LCK top seed are now one series from a first Worlds final, with a revived Invictus Gaming in the way.

Gen.G swept LYON in the second Worlds 2026 quarter-final in Allen, Texas. The defeat removes North America’s last team from the tournament. The LCK top seed now face Invictus Gaming in a best-of-five semi-final on Saturday, starting at 16:00 Central Time.

Gen.G went into the series with the better record. That gave them first choice of side for game one, and they picked blue. They stayed on blue side for games two and three.

Reaching the last four secures Gen.G at least third or fourth place. That is a familiar stopping point for the organisation. It has finished third or fourth at four of its last five Worlds and has never played in a Worlds final, GosuGamers reported.

The stakes go beyond one team. Gen.G entered the tournament as the LCK’s top seed. Korean sides are chasing a fifth Summoner’s Cup in a row.

Their opponents bring their own history. Invictus Gaming beat Top Esports 3-1 in the opening quarter-final. That put iG into their first Worlds semi-final since 2019. TheShy and Rookie, who won Worlds with iG in 2018, are back in the last four.

The money rises sharply from here. Worlds 2026 carries a US$5,000,000 prize pool. The champion takes US$1,000,000 (20%), and the runner-up receives US$800,000.

For LYON, the exit still marks clear progress. They go out in joint fifth to eighth place and collect a share of the prize money. GosuGamers called it easily the organisation’s best Worlds finish. In four earlier appearances, LYON never placed higher than 17th.

Their elimination also changes the shape of the event. North America will have no representative in the semi-finals or the Grand Final. The remaining matches in Allen will be contested without a team from the region.

LYON are eliminated from #Worlds2026. pic.twitter.com/y5cWOL9e5K

— LoL Esports (@lolesports) November 5, 2026

The Grand Final is listed for 14:00 EST on 14 November. British fans will have a dedicated place to watch it. The British Esports Federation is holding a watch party at the new British Arena in Sunderland. It is the venue’s first esports watch party.

The arena covers 15,000 sq ft. It has a 17-metre-wide LED screen, a 200-seat viewing area and a bar. Students can get discounted tickets.

Whether Gen.G or iG make it to that final will be settled in Allen on Saturday. The Sunderland watch party runs from 5:30pm on the day of the final until 1:00am on 15 November.

#4255. Sonic Pico Park Review: A Great Party Favor

Sonic the Hedgehog becomes friends with the cute little cats of Pico Park, inviting all of us into a co-op puzzle-platformer that's sure to make you laugh one way or another.

This year marks the big 3-5 for Sega’s patented Mario killer, Sonic the Hedgehog. It’s been an eventful time for all kinds of fans. Of course, it’s hard to celebrate this momentous occasion with the all but ignored elephant in the room that is the mainline game Sonic Team has all but officially unveiled that’s still in development. But we aren’t going without a game for the anniversary, at least!

Enter Sonic Pico Park. Like the title implies, it’s a return to the chaotic co-op world of Pico Park with a new hedgehog-shaped coat of paint. Ever since it was announced in time for the blue blur’s birthday, Sonic Pico Park has been teasing the mechanics and playable characters slowly leading up to the game’s November launch. It’s been a nice little treat between Sonic Racing: CrossWorlds DLC, monthly comics, and a stream of other goodies throughout the year. But there’s a question that I’m sure a lot of us want to ask.

Sonic the Hedgehog is turning 35 this year, and if you're looking for games to celebrate the occasion, there are plenty of options for you.

Is Sonic Pico Park a good game for this milestone? Is it as good and as cute as it’s been advertised? Is it more Pico than Sonic? Luckily for you, I’m here to answer these questions and more. A short answer to keep things quick: Yes, and no. And if that makes you happy, let’s get into deeper details so you know what you’re getting into before dragging your friends into playing with you.

I’ll be honest and say that it’s hard for me to not fall victim to Sonic Pico Park’s charms. I’ve always adored sprite art. Seeing some of my favorite characters of all time as these miniaturized, big-headed versions, dancing around and reflecting their personalities in these quick animations is just too good to resist. But there’s more to Sonic Pico Park than that.

Like the original Pico Park, Sonic Pico Park is a co-op game where teamwork is key to win. It can be played with at least two players, but you can navigate this game with eight people max if you really want these short and sweet levels to be complete ragers in two different senses of the word. I got to team up with two other writers to play this game. The fun of Sonic Pico Park definitely grows with the number of players involved.

The puzzling co-op of Pico Park fits like a glove with Sonic’s trademark speed. If you thought the original Pico Park may have been too slow, this game picks up the pace with ease without making anything too uncontrollable or without giving you and your friends time to think things through. There are fewer twists to the levels that gave Pico Park what fame it has here, though, likely to keep things less frustrating for younger players and their families. Saboteurs who purposefully ignore instructions for a laugh will still have their ways, though.

Plenty of Pico Park gimmicks, like buttons, numbered platforms and blocks, are scattered throughout the level with springs, loop-de-loops, and rings from Sonic. There are more Sonic mechanics to play with throughout the whole game than Pico staples, and there are plenty of surprises for the average Sonic fan to spot. It’s because of these features that Sonic Pico Park really sticks out as a Sonic game, and one that certainly rises to the 35th anniversary occasion. But like most parties, it will end and become a good memory in time.

One important factor Sonic fans should understand before jumping into Sonic Pico Park is that the games that came before it aren’t particularly long. Pico Park itself only takes about three hours, and I managed to play everything the game offered in about four and a half hours according to my playtime stats. Thankfully this balances out with Sonic Pico Park’s asking price, which I think is fair for a cute little romp with friends. Especially since all it takes is for one of those friends to choose violence and a level that would take five minutes has now taken fifteen because everyone’s too busy laughing and screaming to get back on track. You know. Typical co-op game stuff.

As a Sonic game, Sonic Pico Park is a great snack for the hungry, but won’t be enough for the ravenous.

Sonic fans will still have fun seeing the unexpected twists to what Pico Park is known for. If you remove the Sonic flavoring, you can still find a fun platformer underneath, but the personality of each of the playable Sonic characters really completes the experience. It gives it a sense of style that blends both games together to create something unique that fans will love. It might also serve as the perfect gateway for any Sonic-obsessed friends to finally pull you into this series. Play at your own risk.

Without going into too many details, Sonic Pico Park sticks the landing as an anniversary game. There are a lot of surprises to find in this game as you go along, but it comes at the price of the game’s identity at times that might rub a few players the wrong way. There’s an element to Pico Park that remains in these moments, bringing in a new challenge of figuring out how to tackle the old with the new. But that might not be enough to save these moments from feeling like jingling keys to a fan worn out on the last decade or so of nostalgic references.

Still, that’s only a more cynical look at things. Among the game’s levels and modes, I feel like there are far more interesting twists on Sonic mechanics with Pico Park-style platforming and puzzle-solving than anything else. As a Sonic game, Sonic Pico Park is a great snack for the hungry, but won’t be enough for the ravenous. But it might satiate them a little if their friends bring the laughs and some good nibbles to go with it.

Any newcomers to Sonic don’t have to worry much. Sonic Pico Park doesn’t overstay its welcome. There are a few modes to play on the side, and you can always drag more friends into the chaos and not backseat them, but otherwise, it’s hard to see groups of friends coming back to Sonic Pico Park after clearing everything the first time. And sometimes, it’s okay if a party doesn’t last forever. What’s important is the chaos and fun you have with the people you share it with that will stay with you long after those few hours are up.

Sonic Pico Park is a step up for the iconic puzzle-platformer. It adds a sense of style and quick-thinking that only Sonic could bring to Pico Park while giving an element of chaos not entirely new to Sonic, but elevated through the humor of Pico Park. The dedication and love to the Sonic series can be felt in everything it squeezes into its short run time, as well as how every single character’s personality is made far bigger than the sprites used to portray them. It might not be the game fans expected out of this year, but it’s certainly what they need and deserve. Sonic Pico Park, like the games that came before it, will bring plenty of laughs and good memories to players long after this anniversary is over.

#4252. You're not crazy, trying to heal in Nioh 3 sometimes doesn't work - and Team Ninja is fixing it

One of the more insidiously aggravating bugs in Nioh 3 makes it so the game ignores you when you try to use elixirs, but hopefully not for long.

Nioh 3 has received a hot new update that brings plenty of bug fixes to very specific issues, but it also implements fixes for a few of the most common - and incredibly annoying - bugs. Patch 1.03.01 arrived earlier on all platforms, and it comes with a chunky set of notes.

This latest update, predictably, doesn’t add any gameplay features, but some of the included fixes will absolutely delight - or vindicate - so many of the game’s millions of players.

There’s plenty to go through in the patch notes published today for update 1.03.01, but the most impactful is a fix for an issue that “sometimes made it impossible to use elixirs during battle.” This is only a partial fix, but if you ran into the problem of smashing that shortcut button and not seeing your character play the healing animation, you’ll be glad to see it.

This is a problem myself and others have faced, especially in boss fights. You can even see the shortcut register your button press and proceed to ignore you. Another partial fix has been made to an issue that caused the game to crash. Team Ninja didn’t share specifics on that, and though Nioh 3 has been fairly stable for me in 70+ hours, it has definitely crashed a few times.

If you’ve been playing since launch, you likely have - or know someone who has - run into issues with save file corruption and other weird bugs around certain trackable items within save files.

Team Ninja already rolled out a couple of fixes there, and this latest one specifically targets losing valuables during Myths. If your save file has been affected, the game will now check and recover what was lost. Even more interesting is that the game will now automatically create a backup copy of your save data any time you load a save.

If you’ve made it into the Eternal Rift, you’ll be happy to know that today’s update takes care of a few progression blockers, and fixes an issue that allowed some players to obtain certain items before they were supposed to, locking themselves out.

One of the more amusing fixes concerns Mujina, who had a tendency to respawn if you prayed at a Shrine after opening a chest it was hiding in, which made it appear far more often than a mimic should.

Finally, there’s a set of fixes that address bugs (and exploits) when using specific Martial Art with certain weapons. There are a few fixes to AI, Myths, and one problem with the Minamoto no Yoritomo boss fight that made it impossible to interrupt him, even after he runs out of Ki.

Hit the link at the top for the full change log, and check out our Nioh 3 gameplay tips if you haven’t already. You should also change these settings ASAP, as they’re going to make your life much easier and save you a lot of time.

#4251. Genshin Impact Luna 5 takes the squad back to Mondstadt, finally makes Varka playable

Genshin Impact's next update will have you reminiscing about the good ol' days of... 2020.

The latest big content update has been revealed for HoYoverse's breakout game, Genshin Impact. Version Luna 5, which has the unusually long and needlessly layered title — Song of the Welkin Moon: Variation - Homeward, He Who Caught the Wind — is set to arrive February 25.

This one is a bit of a nostalgia play, taking everyone back to Mondstadt, the place where you may remember taking your first steps. And, as with any good return to the ol’ hunting grounds, come familiar characters, too.

The big new arrival is Varka, who joins as a playable character for the first time. Varka, Grand Master of the Knights of Favonius, is a character whose debut has been long-awaited. He is a 5-Star Anemo Claymore wielder with a dual-wield combat style, capable of dealing two different types of Elemental damage. His addition means that there's now finally a burly 5-Star male character of each elemental type... do with that information what you will.

Varka's dual-wielding combat style allows him to deal two different types of Elemental damage at the same time. The way it works is that his Elemental Skill boosts the damage of his regular attacks, but it also converts the damage type of his right-hand claymore to match his teammates’ elements (Pyro, Hydro, Electro, or Cryo). The left-hand claymore always deals Anemo damage.

The more normal attacks you use, the more frequently he can activate a special Elemental Skill, or trigger a Charged Attack that doesn’t consume stamina. He can also rely on the Hexerei effect to trigger more instances of Elemental Skill, as well as Charged Attacks, making him a monster damage-dealer.

Varka, of course, has been a staple member of the cast, featuring in both the original story in a small cameo, as well as taking a bigger role in the recent Nod-Krai chapters. With the return to Mondstadt, his playable debut makes sense. His Story Quest will shed light on his encounter with the Wild Hunt, and the Great Wolf King of the North

The reruns for this version are going to be Flins — who will be available in the first phase of Event Wishes — as well as Skirk and Escoffier in the second phase. You can also look forward to the return of the Chronicled Wish with Mondstadt characters.

Staying on the theme of reminiscence, the big event in Luna 5 is centered around revisiting memories from the beginning of your time with Genshin Impact, and reuniting with old friends. In Echoes of Memory, you’ll witness familiar scenes that have been changed slightly, and you’ll need to use the Spotter Kamera to detect and record those differences.

The Knights of Favonius are hosting several other activities for everyone to take part in, including an event that lets you catch up with old friends over drinks which you make for them.

Outside of events, there’s a new set of Gliding and Combat Challenges. And, of course, there are new minigames that you can relax with. The Kamera is being utilised yet again, and this time you can use to capture sights from your time in spots across Natlan, Fontaine, and Sumeru. There’s also… a horde mode of a sort, where you fend off waves of enemies.
